closed_issues.title: Improve low-level access patterns when reading and writing data to H5md files
closed_issues.description:
The following discussion from !4938 should be addressed:

- [ ] @mark.j.abraham started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/4938#note_2384367004):  (+1 comment)

    > Note how much overhead we've created here - every call to `readFrame` to get a built-in type makes half a dozen calls into the HDF library (including looking up the `dataSet` dims twice), which itself sometimes calls a low-level I/O library like libc. Each jump into a separate translation unit costs a bit, and jumps into separate shared libraries cost even more. That's particularly sad when the values are probably located in a contiguous array somewhere, perhaps after some layer does some bulk decompression. The source of the extra overhead is that we are providing a *stateless* access API.
    > 
    > We won't want to do this for e.g. writing RVecs from mdrun, but fortunately this is not that code. We do care a bit about all the analysis tools that want to read in coordinates with reasonable efficiency. One good way to do this is with *stateful* interface, such as an iterator. That lets the user write code something like
    > ```
    > for (const auto& value : FrameIterator<ValueType>(dataSet)
    > {
    >     // Use value
    > }
    > ```
    > where now the `FrameIterator` maintains (and guards) all the stuff needed to safely call `H5Dread` perhaps after incrementing `index`. Now the user's loop has a lot less trampolining through memory between getting successive values out of that presumed contiguous array. This access pattern suits one where the user gets a sequence of related values, and does not suit one where the user is getting arbitrary unrelated values.
    > 
    > We *can* implement that sugar on top of `readFrame` (storing `index`), and then optimize the sugar so it does not need to call `readFrame`, at a time when we can measure the benefit on a real use case, so no need to drop everything and implement that now. But maybe that principle is a good one for you to have in mind for the future.

closed_issues.title: Improve group and data set handling when creating H5md trajectory class objects
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

When creating a new `H5md` class object we should set up required groups and data sets. This is currently done ad-hoc.

**Detailed description**

When creating new trajectory files we know at runtime which types of data we will be writing. We can use this to create the required structure in the file at once, following the H5md specification.

A mock-up of this is:

```
H5md root
\-- h5md (group with required metadata for H5md trajectory files)
    +-- version ([int32_t, int32_t] tuple attribute with H5md spec version for file)
    \-- author (group with personal information)
        +-- name (string attribute)
        +-- email (string attribute)
    \-- creator (group detailing the software used)
        +-- name (string attribute)
        +-- version (string attribute)
\-- particles (group)
    \-- system (group with trajectory for full system -- can be replaced with groups for subsets of atoms)
        \-- position (group for time-dependent positions)
            \-- step (int64_t data set, 1d)
            \-- (time) (double data set, 1d, optional storage of simulation time)
                +-- unit (string attribute)
            \-- value ([frame, particle, RVec] data set, 3d)
                +-- unit (string attribute for physical unit of values, technically optional)
        \-- velocity (group)
            ... (as above)
        \-- forces (group)
            ... (as above)
    \-- (subgroup 1)
        ... (as above)
    ...
\-- observables (group)
    \-- temperature (group)
        \-- step (int64_t data set, 1d)
        \-- (time) (double data set, 1d, optional)
            +-- unit (string attribute)
        \-- value (double data set, 1d)
            +-- unit (string attribute for physical unit)
    \-- pressure (group)
        ... (as above)
    ...
```

**Constructing trajectories**

* [ ] Construct full structure in `H5md` constructor
* [ ] Remove ad-hoc group creation (all uses of `openOrCreateX` functions)
* [ ] Remove `openOrCreateX` functions

**Opening trajectories**

When opening a trajectory from disk to continue a simulation we need to ensure that the same structure exists in it. When opening a trajectory for analysis we need only check that a subset of these exist.

* [ ] Check required structure when continuing simulations
* [ ] Check availability of data when opening trajectories for analysis

**Links/references/implementations**

H5md specification: https://h5md.nongnu.org/h5md.html#h5md-root-level

H5md tracking issue: #5016

## Summary

## Exact steps to reproduce

Try building with HeFFTe, see:

```
$ cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${ROCM_PATH}/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${ROCM_PATH}/llvm/bin/clang++ \
    -DGMX_GPU=SYCL -DGMX_SYCL=ACPP -DHIPSYCL_TARGETS='hip:gfx90a' \
    -DGMX_CYCLE_SUBCOUNTERS=ON -DGMX_INSTALL_NBLIB_API=OFF -DGMXAPI=OFF \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=--gcc-toolchain=/opt/cray/pe/gcc/11.2.0/snos/ \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGMX_MPI=ON -DGMX_OPENMP=ON \
    -DGMX_GPU_FFT_LIBRARY=rocfft -DGMX_USE_HEFFTE=ON -DHeffte_ROOT=/appl/local/csc/soft/chem/heffte/2.4.0/
$ make
...

```

## For developers: Why is this important?

As a user you can let the developers discuss this, but for those of you who are developers:

1. Is this an actual issue (file it), something that will have major positive impact in the project (file it), or something you are working on (file it)? If it's merely a possibility of making code a bit nicer, or general good-to-have thing, consider that we can likely come up with 10,000 such ideas - most of those work better as concrete merge requests that address the matter rather than first keeping issues open for months or years.

2. If this is a follow-up issue from a previous code review, is this something the author & reviewers agreed to do as a follow-up in the short term (then assign it to them). Avoid using issues as a general way of scratching down code improvements that might be nice to do some rainy day, although neither you nor the original author have any intention of actually looking at it any time in the foreseeable future :-)

3. Again if you are a developer, are you fixing/closing roughly one old issue for every new one you open (in particular this one), or are we creating new minor issues that somebody else will have to go through and close in 3-6 months?

4. closed_issues.title: Incorrect .top formating
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

.top file contain new format of cmap

**GROMACS version**

GROMACS 2025.0

**Steps to reproduce**

1) Prepare protein in AmberTools24
2) Save .prmtop and .inpcrd files
3) use amb2gro_top_gro.py script
4) appeared topology.top file cannot be used for further processing. gmx grompp falls with errors about incorrect symbols in cmaptypes

**What is the current bug behavior?**

I cannot rerun previous projects because of the inapropriate topology.top format in cmaptypes section

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

normal execution of the gmx grompp comand.

**Possible fixes**

previous versions of GROMACS (2024.4 was tested) were able to read the head of the table in the topology.top file:

```
[ cmaptypes ]

C      N      XC     C      N        1     24   24\
```

(6 spaces between columns)

new version of Gromacs (2025.0) can use this topology file only if I leave only 1 space between the columns:

```
[ cmaptypes ]

C N XC C N 1 24 24\
```

closed_issues.title: Major regression in v2025 for multi-GPU with thread-MPI
closed_issues.description:
GROMACS v2025 is no longer respecting the GMX_ENABLE_DIRECT_GPU_COMM environment variable for PME-PP communications with thread-MPI on NVIDIA GPUs due to https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/4946. This is causing a major regression 
for many cases, e.g. v2025.0 is 2X slower than v2024.5 for ADHD on 4xH100. 

This will cause issues with internal NVIDIA testing and for the many NVIDIA GPU users who use thread-MPI in their workflows.

The issue can be fixed by re-allowing (non-default) GPU direct PME-PP communications via the above environment variable, such that release-2025 behaves the same as previous releases for thread-MPI.

closed_issues.title: [release-2025] NVSHMEM code path hang encountered with adh-dodec for 7PP:1PME
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

With release-2025 branch NVSHMEM code path hang encountered with `adh-dodec` for `7PP:1PME`.
`adh-dodec` for 7PP:1PME triggers pulses/dim to increase-decrease-increase based on domain decomposition which is the not handled in
symmetric allocation involving PME rank.


## Exact steps to reproduce

Build with `GMX_NVSHMEM=ON` and run with `export GMX_ENABLE_NVSHMEM=1`.
Run the adh-dodec input as below.
mpirun  -np 8 ./bin/gmx_mpi mdrun -s ../../adh_dodec/topol.tpr  -ntomp 14 -nb gpu -update gpu -bonded gpu  -nsteps 60000 -nstlist 200 -resetstep 40000 -v  -pin off  -npme 1 -dlb no -noconfout

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?
1.) mdrun hangs after certain number of timesteps around 20k
2.) It should hang.

## Possible fixes

MR !4970 contains the fix for this.

closed_issues.title: MSVC + CUDA + OpenMP compilation failure

## Summary

Building GROMACS 2025.0 can fail with:

`
D:\a\GROMACS-Windows\GROMACS-Windows\gromacs-2025.0\src\gromacs\mdlib\lincs_gpu.cpp(322): error C3028: 'gmx::LincsGpu::maxCoupledConstraints_': only a variable or static data member can be used in a data-sharing clause [D:\a\GROMACS-Windows\GROMACS-Windows-\gromacs-2025.0\build\src\gromacs\libgromacs.vcxproj]`

Build on Windows using MSVC + CUDA (OpenMP is enabled by default).

We support this build mode, it should work

An identical problem was fixed in !4822, so should be straightforward to do the same.

closed_issues.title: Can't run a simulation with PLUMED
closed_issues.description:
A user on the forum reported that they can't run a simulation using PLUMED even though no errors occurred during configuration (see [this post](https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/gromacs-with-plumed-error/11542)). I'm able to reproduce the issue using GROMACS 2025.0 and PLUMED 2.9.

Configuring with `cmake .. -DGMX_USE_PLUMED=ON`, `export PLUMED_KERNEL=<path-to-plumed>/lib/libplumedKernel.so`, and running a simulation with `gmx mdrun -plumed plumed.dat` as per the reference manual gives the error
```-------------------------------------------------------
Program:     gmx mdrun, version 2025.0
Source file: src/gromacs/applied_forces/plumed/plumedMDModule_stub.cpp (line 81)
Function:    gmx::{anonymous}::PlumedMDModule::subscribeToSimulationSetupNotifications(gmx::MDModulesNotifiers*)::<lambda(const gmx::PlumedInputFilename&)>

Error in user input:
GROMACS is not compiled with the PLUMED interface, if you want to use -plumed
option, please reconfigure GROMACS with -DGMX_USE_PLUMED=ON.

For more information and tips for troubleshooting, please check the GROMACS
website at https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/run-time-errors.html
-------------------------------------------------------
```
indicating that GROMACS was compiled with the stub implementation instead of the actual plumed interface.

We should make sure that CMake correctly issues a fatal error if it's not able to create the interface when it was asked to, or in case more steps are needed to correctly build with PLUMED support, that we document them properly in the installation guide.

closed_issues.title: Automatically detect neoverse-v2 to choose NEON over SVE for CPU resident GROMACS on that hardware
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

On neoverse-v2, the performance of the non bonded force kernel on CPU is ~10% slower for SVE than NEON. At compile time, if compiling on neoverse-v2 with a CPU build, NEON should be chosen over SVE where currently SVE is the default. In addition, a run time message will warn that SVE is preferred over NEON where the opposite should be true for a CPU build. 

## Exact steps to reproduce

Build with `-DGMX_GPU=OFF`: `GMX_SIMD=ARM_SVE` will be chosen by default

Build with `-DGMX_GPU=OFF GMX_SIMD=ARM_NEON_ASIMD`: 
run time warning issued
```
Likely fastest SIMD instructions supported by all nodes: ARM_SVE
SIMD instructions selected at compile time:              ARM_NEON_ASIMD
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

As well as choosing a more sensible default for performance on neoverse-v2, the method described in the fix is a more robust way to detect cpu info about ARM systems than reading `/proc/cpuinfo` for Linux kernel 4.11+, so could potentially be applied generally to `detectProcCpuInfoArm` in src/gromacs/hardware/cpuinfo.cpp. Would presumably want to fall back to the `/proc/cpuinfo` for older systems. 

## Possible fixes

ARM systems include the MIDR_EL1 register with information about chip implementer and architecture. See https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ddi0601/2020-12/AArch64-Registers/MIDR-EL1--Main-ID-Register. For neoverse-v2, implementer = 0x41 (ARM) and part_number == 0xD4F (Neoverse V2). Note that for NVIDIA Grace the implementer is 0x41. See also https://nvidia.github.io/grace-cpu-benchmarking-guide/developer/cpudetect.html#example-source-code. 

The MIDR_EL1 register is not available from user space but has been emulated by the Linux kernel since 4.11 (see https://docs.kernel.org/arch/arm64/cpu-feature-registers.html). Whether this emulation is available can be tested by querying HWCAP_CPUID with glibc. An example of this is shown in this code snippet attached: [detect.cpp](/uploads/fb2d2c8bbc884689c7d10a9aea9f5e64/detect.cpp)

Still looking into incorporating this snippet into src/gromacs/hardware/cpuinfo.cpp

closed_issues.title: Document PME tuning
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Users should be able to find out how PME tuning works, some experienced GROMACS users don't know: https://github.com/plumed/plumed2/issues/1177#issuecomment-2612037877

**Use cases**

Users can assess whether they want tuning on or off, which could be relevant when they care about the fine details of the potential energy, e.g. HREX with Plumed

**Impact**

Users will know what implementation is used by default in various situations. Developers will learn about that as they review the documentation change.

**Detailed description**

* [x] How it is implemented (scaling of rcoulomb and minimum grid size), impact of the grid being discrete
* [x] When it is on by default
* [x] When it might be a good or bad idea to use it
* [x] Alternatives like `gmx tune_pme` 
* [x] Possible side effects with replica exchange

closed_issues.title: Rework NNPotModel / TorchModel classes
closed_issues.description:
We should address a number of issues with the current way the `NNPotModel`/`TorchModel` classes are set up, raised in discussions in !4868.
This includes the following: 
- [ ] Save a reference to the `t_commrec` object only once at construction, instead of at every call to `calculateForces()`, as this data never changes
- [ ] Remove the unnecessary `init()` function
- [ ] Combine `evaluate()` and `getOutputs()` into one function
- [ ] Make `setDevice()` a free function returning the device type instead of member function
- [ ] Make `loadModelExtension()` a free function being passed a `const string&` and a logger instead of member function. Should use `std::splitString` as well as `camelCase` variable names.
- [ ] Consolidate the precursor input-setting methods with `evaluate()` to simplify usage and avoid creating the need for error checking when only one backend (and pipeline details) is supported

closed_issues.title: Rename/remove provideForces flag in TorchModel
closed_issues.description:
The following discussion from !4856 should be addressed:

- [ ] @mark.j.abraham started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/4856#note_2290501418):  (+5 comments)

    > Only partly related, but energy components are only needed when writing output, so we should probably have a bool parameter to this function about whether the energy needs to be obtained from libtorch, and then put somewhere. Probably density fitting has a model for how to do that. Conversely, mostly we assume that forces are always needed. Why do we have `provideForces` here?

We should rename the `provideForces` flag to make it clear that its function is to determine whether the model provides forces or if we need to calculate them. However, this flag is set from a user input field in the `.mdp` file, and we then check if it matches the actual output of the model. Thus, it might be simpler to just remove this mdp option, and simply check the model output and only compute the forces if the model doesn't provide them.

## Exact steps to reproduce

On intel-gpu04 (happens locally for me too):

```console
$ module load cmake/3.29.5 ninja/1.10.0 clang/18.1.8 
$ git checkout af183b80a00f77af90da4a08241a58879ece0a48  # Latest `release-2025`

$ ninja tests
$ GMX_NBNXN_PLAINC_1X1=1 ./bin/mdrun-fep-test
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

This mode is the basis for autovectorization with RISC-V with RVV (I get the same error on both x86_64 and emulated RV64), so we should make sure it works.

closed_issues.title: Having fully frozen atoms in the same T-coupling group and non-frozen atoms results in incorrect temperature
closed_issues.description: When atoms frozen along all dimensions are present in a temperature coupling group together with non-frozen atoms, the number of degrees of freedom of the temperature coupling group is reduced by 3 times the number of frozen atoms. This leads to too high temperatures being reported and too low real temperatures when temperature coupling is used. Note that you can not detect the latter issue by looking at the temperature in the output, as this will match the temperature of the bath.

closed_issues.title: Replace __AMDGCN_WAVEFRONT_SIZE in SYCL kernels/CMake
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

In some SYCL bits, we use `__AMDGCN_WAVEFRONT_SIZE` to differentiate the code for different architectures and also to detect the target architectures from CMake. Now, this macro is [deprecated in mainline LLVM](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/112849) (to be part of Clang 20) with the suggested replacement ["don't do this"](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/112849#discussion_r1807858498).

In [LLVM OpenMP tests](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/113156/files), the replacement was `__builtin_amdgcn_wavefrontsize()`, but we need to look case-by-case. [Related effort for the HIP runtime itself](https://github.com/ROCm/clr/pull/111/files).

## For developers: Why is this important?

We don't want to use the deprecated functionality, even if it is not being removed yet.

closed_issues.title: Performance regression in 2025-beta when using GPU buffer ops by default
closed_issues.description:
When testing the 2025-beta I noticed a performance drop caused by the use of GPU buffer ops.

The system I tested was FEP simulations of testosterone in water. I was running 16 (3 thr/job) or 8 (6 thr/job) jobs (lambda states) in parallel on a dual Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2650 v4 @ 2.20GHz (24 hw cores/48 threads) and 4 NVIDIA NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070.

I tracked the regression down to commit b28502916d (!4743). I don't seem to regain all of the performance when using `GMX_GPU_DISABLE_BUFFER_OPS`, which indicates that there might be a further regression between that commit and v2025-beta.

In the current state the beta is slower than v2024 (which in turn was slower than previous years), but fixing this regression would regain and improve the performance.

I think there needs to be sufficient testing to set use the buffer ops only when it's expected to be useful or the documentation should be clarified to indicate what systems/hardware are expected to requiring disabling this option.

I'm attaching a plot illustrating the performance regression.[fig_fe_performance_buffer_ops_regression.pdf](/uploads/25b36f59c4b9f390d2b7ee7993b10dd7/fig_fe_performance_buffer_ops_regression.pdf)

closed_issues.title: Incorrect reporting of Coulomb interactions in mdrun
closed_issues.description:
When disabling all non-bonded interactions, e.g. via exclusions in the topology or using `NNPotTopologyPreprocessor`, the `mdrun` logfile still reports a non-zero Coulomb energy, while LJ  interactions are correctly reported as zero:
```
        Statistics over 5001 steps using 51 frames

   Energies (kJ/mol)
  Connect Bonds        LJ (SR)   Coulomb (SR)      Potential    Kinetic En.
    0.00000e+00    0.00000e+00    2.16961e-05    2.16961e-05    0.00000e+00
   Total Energy    Temperature Pressure (bar)
    2.16961e-05    0.00000e+00    0.00000e+00
```
According to the [manual](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/reference-manual/topologies/molecule-definition.html#exclusions), exclusions should remove *all* non-bonded interactions, not just LJ. In fact, I think that's actually the case, because in the absence of any other (bonded) interactions, the atoms do not move. 

Thus, I think what might be happening is that Coulomb interactions are computed, but the resulting force is not applied. Nonetheless, we should fix this because it has been confusing users as to what the exclusion section in the topology file is doing (I've seen related posts in the forum). The expected outcome should be that when all non-bonded interactions are disabled, `mdrun` should report zero energies for both LJ and Coulomb interactions. 

I've tested this in 2025 beta, but this most likely affects older versions as well. If others want to test this, I can provide an example topology.

closed_issues.title: Intel oneAPI on Windows: linker error, cannot find m.lib
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Trying to build GROMACS 2024.4 with oneAPI 2025.0 + MSVC 2022 on Windows fails: `LINK : fatal error LNK1181: cannot open input file ‘m.lib’`

Apparently, the reason is that IntelLLVM has libm.lib, so CMake sets `HAVE_LIBM` to true, and so [`m` is added to the list of libraries](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/v2024.4/CMakeLists.txt?ref_type=tags#L896-898). However, it should be `libm`, not `m`.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Get GROMACS 2024.4 (or any other?), oneAPI 2025, MSVC 2022. Follow the installation instructions from https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/training/build-gromacs-with-intel-oneapi-dpc-c-compiler.html, specifically:

`cmake .. -DGMX_BUILD_OWN_FFTW=ON -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icx -DGMX_GPU=SYCL -DGMX_FFT_LIBRARY=mkl -GNinja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=on`

- Source: https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/gromacs-nmake-error1181/10466

## Possible fixes

CMake's `find_library` correctly stores the library path to `HAVE_LIBM` variable. We should use this value instead of hardcoded `m`.

closed_issues.title: gmx solvate still tells users about change of parameters in GROMACS 5.0
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

When the user doesn't provide a .tpr as input, gmx solvate doesn't know for sure what the atom types are. In GROMACS 5.0, we changed the default values it chooses, and added a note to help users understand any behavioural changes. That note is no longer relevant, we should at most tell them the source of the parameters.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Run grompp providing e.g. a protein in a .gro file

## For developers: Why is this important?

closed_issues.title: grompp suggests changing nstlist, which is often an irrelevant distraction
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

When the user chooses `nstlist < 10`, grompp suggests changing nstlist. This can be an irrelevant suggestion, because mdrun itself now often chooses nstlist by default. grompp should not suggest the user makes a change when mdrun will override that change. We want users to act on our suggestions, so should minimize those that we make to cases that matter.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Run grompp

## For developers: Why is this important?

User feedback from GROMACS tools should be relevant and actionable

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

grompp issues a note advising about a choice that mdrun will typically later override anyway. grompp should talk about things that we expect a user should want to handle.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

```
                      :-) GROMACS - gmx grompp, 2024.2 (-:

Executable:   /nfs/work05/srilekhax/gromacs-gpuaware_gmxmpi_intelmpi_prefix_2024_2_oneapi/bin/gmx_mpi
Data prefix:  /nfs/work05/srilekhax/gromacs-gpuaware_gmxmpi_intelmpi_prefix_2024_2_oneapi
Working dir:  /nfs/work05/srilekhax/gromacs-gpuaware_gmxmpi_intelmpi_prefix_2024_2_oneapi/bin/multisimulation_next_2/sim_a
Command line:
  gmx_mpi grompp -f mdtut_minim.mdp -c prot_solv_ions.gro -p topol.top -o em.tpr

Ignoring obsolete mdp entry 'ns_type'

NOTE 1 [file mdtut_minim.mdp]:
  With Verlet lists the optimal nstlist is >= 10, with GPUs >= 20. Note
  that with the Verlet scheme, nstlist has no effect on the accuracy of
  your simulation.
```

## Possible fixes

Currently grompp does not know when mdrun will override the choice made by the user. It should ask the nbnxm module when that is the case.
For example, refactor `increaseNstlist()` so that it does not change the `t_inputrec` that is provided, but rather returns the proposed changes to rlist and nstlist (or copy grompp's `t_inputrec` to pass to `increaseNstlist()` and compare the result with the original). Then the grompp can issue the note only when mdrun won't change nstlist.

closed_issues.title: Freeze groups options needs energy group exclusions to give correct energies (via gmx energy) but energygrp-excl is not supported
closed_issues.description:
In Gromacs 2024.2 (and all versions for the past several years) energygrp-excl is no longer supported. When atoms are frozen via freezegrps, gmx energy gives erroneous results, because frozen atoms are being included in, e.g., virial calculations. The documentation at https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html states:

>To avoid spurious contributions to the virial and pressure due to large forces between completely frozen atoms you need to use energy group exclusions, this also saves computing time.

Are there plans to include energy group exclusions, or some other way to extract the virial from a system with frozen atoms, in the near future?

closed_issues.title: Fix illegal memory access with FEP and OpenMP
closed_issues.description:
The thread reduction masks for the perturbed non-bonded interaction force buffer are generated by range loops, but the range of the std:: vectors do not correspond to the actual size in use. This would lead to out of bounds access of the mask buffers, but not to illegal memory access, as the only old elements could be out range but the buffers would still have at least that size.

This might also affect performance, as too many buffer elements were flagged with old, no longer used, atom indices.

closed_issues.title: Gromacs fails to build with NVIDIA NVHPC compilers due to a legacy conditionally compiled define
closed_issues.description:
While using NVHPC 24.9 compilers to build Gromacs 2024.2 for Grace CPUs, nvc++ reports many errors such as the following:
```
> "gromacs/math/functions.h", line 118: error: expected an identifier
>   unsigned int log2I(std::int64_t x);
>                           ^
```
The issue has been tracked down by compiler developers, and thus rejected as a compiler bug and classified as user error, to the presence of the following three lines in src/gromacs/fileio/xdrf.h (lines 42-44):
```
> #ifdef __PGI /*Portland group compiler*/
> #    define int64_t long long
> #endif
```
Removal of these lines allows the build to proceed and complete.

closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

In the context of Relative Binding Free Energy (RBFE) calculations, it's increasingly important to support scaffold hopping transformations, such as changing a five-membered ring to a six-membered ring. To enable this type of perturbation, it is necessary to allow alchemical changes to both the Lennard-Jones (LJ) and Coulomb (QQ) 1-4 interactions, which is currently not supported in Gromacs.

**Use cases**

By enabling this feature, users will be able to perform scaffold hopping RBFE calculations using Gromacs.

**Impact**

Currently, Desmond is the only molecular dynamics engine that supports scaffold hopping RBFE, though it requires the use of soft-bond potentials. There is a publication detailing how scaffold hopping can be performed without soft-bond potentials using a modified version of the AMBER MD engine (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8215533/), but no molecular dynamics engine fully supports scaffold hopping RBFE out-of-the-box. If Gromacs adds this functionality, it will become a viable option for scaffold hopping RBFE, provided it supports alchemical transformations of both the LJ and QQ 1-4 interactions.

**Detailed description**

Currently, the Gromacs free energy perturbation (FEP) code supports changes to the LJ 1-4 interactions, but further updates are needed to also allow changes to the QQ 1-4 interactions. This would provide the necessary support for scaffold hopping transformations.
![image](/uploads/0ce43c06ea8c6770b9c929a00fca6c46/image.png)

In this case, from six-membered ring to five-membered ring, the 1-4 interaction between 9-11 and 11-7 needs to be removed, while the 1-4 interaction between 9-7 needs to be added back.

closed_issues.title: incorrect new cluster setup naming and reporting
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

!4371 changed the cluster reporting and introduced new naming in the logging and code which is not appropriate:

```
Using GPU 8x8 nonbonded short-range kernels    

NBNxM GPU setup: super-cluster 2x2x2 / cluster 8, with unified GPU pairlist 
```

There is no such thing as "split" or "unified"  pair list. The search outputs an [Sx]MxM cluster setup and the pruning may transform it to MxN (8x4). The list remains the same. The log should simply report the latter cluster setup since that is what is used for computing pair interactions. This has already been reported before, hence the "with split/unified GPU pairlist" part of the new reporting is redundant and confusing.

In addition, the (i) cluster size is already reported so no need to repeat that either. The super-cluster setup is compile-time constant so it is reported in the log header. Although redundant, it may be useful to keep it, but perhaps unifying it with the first line is best.


## Possible fixes

* remove confusing naming introduced
* remove redundant reporting
* consider adding super-cluster size reporting (and/or geometry reporting).

Memory corruption with VkFFT 1.3.5
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

We manually set the pointer in VkFFT's internal datastructure (https://github.com/DTolm/VkFFT/issues/78). Since version 1.3.5 (in pre-release stage; https://github.com/DTolm/VkFFT/commit/9a96811d58ce09db621526bfd752d583e17d68d2 is the breaking change), VkFFT has ownership of these pointers and tries to `free` them on shutdown, which does not work well with a pointer to a long gone stack variable.

We should set the pointer to `nullptr` to avoid it being used after it's gone out of scope.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Build GROMACS with SYCL (tested with ACpp + CUDA and HIP) and `-DGMX_EXTERNAL_VKFFT=ON -Dvkfft_DIR=/path/to/vkfft/develop`, run ./bin/fft-test

```
....
[ RUN      ] Works/ParameterizedFFTTest3D.RunsOnDevices/5_6_9
free(): invalid pointer
Aborted (core dumped)
```

inline bool targetHasLargeRegisterPool(const DeviceInformation& deviceInfo)
{

}

- ROCm 6.1.1 + RX6400: 65536

closed_issues.title: mdrun should respect OMP affinity-setting variables when already set
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

With `OMP_PROC_BIND` active, EasyBuild CI runners have trouble with tests timing out that are resolved by `unset OMP_PROC_BIND`. (See https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/21430#issuecomment-2391005258.)

## Exact steps to reproduce

Run mdrun test binaries with or without `OMP_PROC_BIND` set.

## For developers: Why is this important?

mdrun and test binaries should behave predictably under a wide range of job-execution environments.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

The defaults cause mdrun to set its own affinities, which can lead to slow-running tests when `OMP_PROC_BIND` is also set, particularly if other processes share the node. mdrun should observe `OMP_PROC_BIND` (and perhaps other such `OMP_*` variables) and not set affinities itself.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

N/A

## Possible fixes

Also check `OMP_PROC_BIND` where `GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY` is currently the only such variable checked. The latter has a similar role, but is specific to the GNU Open MP library.

closed_issues.title: Add config run with ACPP_FORCE_INSTANT_SUBMISSION
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Add a CI build with `ACPP_FORCE_INSTANT_SUBMISSION` once ACpp 24.06+ is available in CI.

Unlike `ACPP_ALLOW_INSTANT_SUBMISSION`, this will throw if the preconditions for instant submissions (how the kernel is submitted, fully determined by code, not by hardware/runtime) are not satisfied, potentially causing bad performance.

From ACpp docs:

> Define the macro `ACPP_ALLOW_INSTANT_SUBMISSION=1` before including `sycl.hpp` to enable it. Instant submission is possible with operations that do not use buffers (USM only), have no dependencies on non-instant tasks, do not use SYCL 2020 reductions and use in-order queues. In the stdpar model, instant submission is active by default.

> `ACPP_FORCE_INSTANT_SUBMISSION` - define to `1` before including `sycl.hpp` to imply `ACPP_ALLOW_INSTANT_SUBMISSION=1` and throw an exception when instant submission is not possible.

## For developers: Why is this important?

Having such a test job will prevent performance regressions caused by accidental breakage of instant submission.

Assigning to %"2025.rc", but this can be done later, as it only concerns CI.

closed_issues.title: Support non-perturbed Restricted bending potential in free energy calculations
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The Restricted Bending Potential plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of dihedral angle calculations, particularly in scenarios where the angle approaches extreme values (0° or 180°). This is especially important in free energy calculations, where decoupling parts of the system can cause angles to become unstable or wobbly. The Restricted Bending Potential ensures that even under such conditions, the dihedral calculations remain stable, preventing disruptions in the simulation.

While I understand that perturbing the Restricted Bending Potential is currently not supported, which I’m completely fine with, I do believe it’s critical that free energy calculations should still be possible when Restricted Bending Potentials are present in the system, especially  if they are not being perturbed.

This capability is essential for accurate simulations in many cases, especially when working with complex systems where the stability of angles is a concern. Without this, there’s a significant risk of instability in the calculations, which could lead to incorrect results and undermine the reliability of the free energy predictions.

Ensuring support for this would greatly enhance the robustness of the free energy workflows and help avoid potential complications during simulation. This is an important aspect to consider, and its implementation would provide substantial benefits to anyone conducting free energy calculations in similar contexts.

## Exact steps to reproduce

gmx grompp -f gromacs.mdp -c gromacs.gro -p gromacs.top -o gromacs.tpr -maxwarn 2
gmx mdrun -deffnm gromacs -v

Gives 

Fatal error:
Function type Restr. Angles does not currently support being perturbed in free
energy calculations

## For developers: Why is this important?
N/A

[Archive.zip](/uploads/0f55624f972b2dbfdc0ac28df23a3e19/Archive.zip)

closed_issues.title: Query, ENH: supporting lambda scaling for MARTINI 3 lipid diversity
closed_issues.description:
One of the most important steps in an MD simulation workflow is the setup of the initial configuration--for massive lipid-based vesicle/virus systems we often face the challenge of an unknown lipid composition, and unknown ratio between inner and outer leaflet populations. As a result of this fact combined with the sizes of these systems, steric conflicts in the process of system construction are hard to avoid.

GROMACS has been an essential tool in relaxing these steric conflicts prior to energy minimization. The lambda scaling/free energy "abuse" mechanism of this steric conflict resolution is well known (and published, i.e., https://doi.org/10.1021/ct501111d) and even suggested by GROMACS proper when energy minimization fails in some cases I believe.

I've created a small (2 molecule) reproducer repo that works with GROMACS `2024.2` (https://github.com/tylerjereddy/gmx_martini3_alchembed_repro) for a problem that happens with some MARTINI 3 lipid types. It would be great if there were a workaround for this. In this particular case, it seems to be the forcefield/parameters for MARTINI 3 `POPI` molecule. Steps to reproduce with that repo cloned locally:

- `gmx grompp -f alchembed-cg.mdp -c system.gro -p topology.top -o alchembed.tpr -maxwarn 20`
- `gmx mdrun -v -s alchembed.tpr -deffnm alchembed_1x_lipids -nt 1 -ntmpi 1`


Should fail with:

```
Program:     gmx mdrun, version 2024.2
Source file: src/gromacs/topology/topsort.cpp (line 142)

Fatal error:
Function type Restr. Angles does not currently support being perturbed in free
energy calculations
```

closed_issues.title: Non-bonded interactions close to cut-off missing with GPUs
closed_issues.description:
With the dual-pairlist setup in GPUs, the dynamic pruning kernel rounds down the number of supercluster entries when dividing by the number of pruning parts. The first call is done in one part, so prunes all entries. The later, rolling pruning calls round down instead of up. Therefore up to numParts-1 entries are left with the originally pruned list. This leads to some pair interactions close to the cut-off missing. As nstlistPrune is usually 10 (and never much larger), this affects up to 4 list entries. Without domain decomposition or a single domain, this is the total number of entries affected. With domain decomposition there are two lists per domain, so many more entries could be affected. But as the domain size is usually not small (for performance reasons), still not many of the total interactions are affected.

We checked runs of both atomistic and Martini coarse-grained systems with CUDA. With atomistic simulations of dense systems and nstlist=100 (the maximum that is chosen by default), we see about 10 missing cluster-pairs over nstlist steps with a single domain. With 4 domains this can be a hundred. Even though a cluster pair contains 8x4 atom pairs, only very few of those will come inside the cut-off distance. As there are already around a million pair interactions for 5000 atom system, we do not expect there to be a measurable effect of this bug. Indeed we have not been able to detect differences in forces or energies larger than what different instances (e.g. CPU vs GPU) give. Martini runs give similar behavior with default nstlist.

With very large nstlist or systems with (partial) vacuum or vapor, some atom/molecules might more much more. In such cases there can be measurable effects, but we have not been able to detect any in simulations that would not crash after a few thousands of steps. Thus we currently have no indication that invalid simulation results might have been generated unnoticed, but we can not exclude the possibility.

closed_issues.title: Incorrect test device teardown when using hipfft as fft backend
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

When building GROMACS with the proposed HIP backend and using hipfft as the GPU FFT backend, test device teardown does not properly clean up created rocfft streams, leading to errors when running multiple tests in succession.

This might also cause issues when running other tasks on the same device that the tests are being run on, but that hasn't been tested .

**GROMACS version**

```
GROMACS version:     2025-dev-20240819-0813556657
```

**Steps to reproduce**

Needs hardware that is supported by hipftt, e.g. the MI50 cards.

Build current branch that enables HIP PME support
```
git clone https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs.git -b 4958-add-hip-pme-kernels
mkdir build && cd build
cmake ../gromacs -DGMX_GPU=HIP -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++ -DGMX_BUILD_OWN_FFTW=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/rocm/ -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/bin/amdclang++ -DGMX_GPU_FFT_LIBRARY=hipfft
```

Run the following test case
```
bin/mdrun-mpi-pme-test -ntmpi 2 --gtest_filter=ReproducesEnergies/PmeTest.Runs/basic_mdrun_notunepme_npme_1_pme_gpu_pmefft_*
```

**What is the current bug behavior?**

The test will start running the `cpu`/`gpu`/`auto` parts of the test, and fail with an error during the generation of the HIPFFT plan when running the second test case on the GPU.

Running the tests individually ensures that each of them passes. Just running GROMACS manually works as well.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

The tests should run without error in any combination of execution order.

**Possible fixes**

The bug has been discussed upstream, and the issue seems to be that the internally generated device streams in rocfft are not cleaned up when resetting the device in-between test cases. It has been proposed to either not reset the device, or to manually clean up the streams before resetting the device.

closed_issues.title: Output file location for colvars modules is always the current working directory
closed_issues.description:
## Summary **Wrong behavior:** The output files of the Colvars module (`.colvars.traj` and `.colvars.state`) get always written into the current working directory, independent of the specified `-e` flag. In fact, the filenames get the correct filename (corresponds to the basename of the energy filepath), but are not written in the correct directory. **Expected behavior:** The output files should be written to the same location as the energy file as specified by the `-e` flag. The [GROMACS colvars documentation](https://colvars.github.io/master/colvars-refman-gromacs.html#sec:colvars_output) states: > When the output prefix output is defined (in GROMACS, this is automatically set to the value of the -eflag of mdrun), the following output files are written during a simulation run [...] ## Exact steps to reproduce This probably happens with every mdrun with an activated colvars setup. The attached files contain an simple example based on the [GROMACS Lysozyme tutorial](http://www.mdtutorials.com/gmx/lysozyme/index.html): [topology.top](/uploads/bcfbe16a4ecf192e2d0487ec648d3831/topology.top) [minimized.gro](/uploads/cb53a171170fc6c95cad0feec3b466a7/minimized.gro) [simulation.mdp](/uploads/ea57c170aac87bef25a6760d0ab1c253/simulation.mdp) [colvars.config](/uploads/8d4c1bb439aecfb20677eb13b13af563/colvars.config) [index.ndx](/uploads/df9996e6020bebb2830a2102448d56c5/index.ndx) The can be run with the following commands: ``` mkdir output gmx grompp -f simulation.mdp -c minimized.gro -p topology.top -o output/simulation.tpr -po output/simulation.out.mdp gmx mdrun -deffnm output/simulation -e output/simulation.edr -v ``` We expect that the colvars output files are also written into the output directory. However, the end up in the execution directory.
The resulting file tree looks like this. ├── minimized.gro
├── topology.top
├── simulation.mdp
├── colvars.config
├── index.ndx
├── simulation.colvars.state
├── simulation.colvars.traj
└── output
  ├── simulation.cpt
  ├── simulation.edr
  ├── simulation.gro
  ├── simulation.log
  ├── simulation.out.mdp
  ├── simulation.tpr
  └── simulation.trr
## GROMACS Information **Version:** 2024.2 **Modifications:** No ## Possible fixes The `.edr` filename is processed in the file [src/gromacs/applied_forces/colvars/colvarsoptions.cpp](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/gromacs/applied_forces/colvars/colvarsoptions.cpp#L277-289). Just removing the `.filename()` part in line 289 of the function `void ColvarsOptions::processEdrFilename(const EdrOutputFilename& filename)` would probably solve the problem.

closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

The alignment check in [simd/impl_arm_sve/impl_arm_sve_util_float gatherLoadTranspose](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/gromacs/simd/include/gromacs/simd/impl_arm_sve/impl_arm_sve_util_float.h?ref_type=heads#L120 ) is hard coded to 64B where [documentation](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/doxygen/html-lib/group__module__simd.xhtml#ga6823a0b3cbc43eee3918b137d2b18384) suggests this should be GMX_SIMD_FINT32_WIDTH.   

**GROMACS version**

v2024 and older. 

**What is the current bug behavior?**

Suspect this has always worked on A64FX which uses 512 bit. This can fail at run time on other hardware eg Grace, due to the failed alignment check. 

**Possible fixes**

Update to `assert(std::size_t(offset) % GMX_SIMD_FINT32_WIDTH == 0);`

closed_issues.title: Missing improper dihedral terms for molecules connected by a specbond.dat bond
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

pdb2gmx does not generate improper dihedral terms for molecules connected by a bond defined in specbond.dat. 
Common examples are side chain to main chain isopeptide/thioester connections in ubiquitylated proteins. 
When generating the topology for such a molecule with pdb2gmx, it will include the bond, angle, dihedral terms in top file, but omit improper dihedral terms, which have to be added manually. 

This is a minor issue and I was torn between submitting it as bug or an enhancement. However, since all other (bond, angle dihedral) terms are included in the .top file, i think it can be categorised as a bug.


**GROMACS version**

This issue has been observed in multiple versions, but in the provided minimal example i have used:

```
GROMACS version:     2024.3-dev-20240514-3095163
GIT SHA1 hash:       30951633e0120d942e73a992f423798e209e58e7
Precision:           mixed
Memory model:        64 bit
MPI library:         none
OpenMP support:      enabled (GMX_OPENMP_MAX_THREADS = 128)
GPU support:         disabled
SIMD instructions:   SSE2
CPU FFT library:     fftw-3.3.7-sse2-avx-avx2-avx2_128
GPU FFT library:     none
Multi-GPU FFT:       none
RDTSCP usage:        enabled
TNG support:         enabled
Hwloc support:       disabled
Tracing support:     disabled
C compiler:          /sw/cluster/gcc-12.2/bin/gcc GNU 12.2.0
C compiler flags:    -Wno-array-bounds -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -msse2 -Wall -Wno-unused -Wunused-value -Wunused-parameter -Wextra -Wno-sign-compare -Wpointer-arith -Wundef -Werror=stringop-truncation -Wno-missing-field-initializers -O3 -DNDEBUG
C++ compiler:        /sw/cluster/gcc-12.2/bin/g++ GNU 12.2.0
C++ compiler flags:  -Wno-array-bounds -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -msse2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpointer-arith -Wmissing-declarations -Wundef -Wstringop-truncation -Wno-missing-field-initializers -Wno-cast-function-type-strict -fopenmp -O3 -DNDEBUG
BLAS library:        Internal
LAPACK library:      Internal
```

**Steps to reproduce**

I have included a minimal example to reproduce the issue: 
- topol.pdb includes two protein chains connected by a thioester bond (CYS2A -> GLY2B).
- Parameters for the thioester bond have been added to the (included) charmm36m forcefield.
- topol.top can be created with `gmx pdb2gmx -f topol.pdb -merge all -ignh -ter` selecting the appropriate forcefield and `None` for c-term chain B .

[minimal_example.zip](/uploads/9229e0803525a38aad55a668fbb9fdcb/minimal_example.zip)

**What is the current bug behavior?**

The topology is missing the (improper) dihedral for the thioester carbonyl:

```
SG(l)-- C(i)-- CA(j)
        |
        O(k)
```

In the minimal example this would correspond to:

```
[ dihedrals ]
;  ai    aj    ak    al funct 
       ...
   47    44    48    19     2
```

Parameters are included in ffbonded.itp (CG2O2    CG321    OG2D1    SG311).

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

The topology should include the improper dihedral term. 

**Possible fixes**

Unfortunately I'm not familiar enough with the code base to suggest possible fixes.

closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Free energy functional dependence of Lennard-Jones terms with vdw modifier force-switch seems to be incorrect.  Specifically, if decoupling an LJ site (so using the softcore pathway), then with free_energy=yes and lambda=0, the energy is different than with free energy off. vdw-modifiers potential-switch and potential-shift do not have this issue, i.e. with free_energy=yes and lambda=0, the energy is the same as with free energy off with those modifiers.   Found by @mrshirts and @lwhitm1

**GROMACS version**

We have observed the same bug with GROMACS 2022.4 and 2024.2.

**Steps to reproduce**

Run the following with the attached files:

[energy_eval_nofe.mdp](/uploads/03ae1f0f0f59023c659b2b85d6edf9bc/energy_eval_nofe.mdp)

```

$GMX grompp -f energy_eval_fe.mdp -p ljs.top -c ljs.gro -o free.tpr
$GMX mdrun -nt 1 -s free.tpr -g free.log -e free.edr -o freeout.trr -c freeout.gro
echo 1 0 | $GMX energy -f free.edr -o free.xvg

$GMX grompp -f energy_eval_nofe.mdp -p ljs.top -c ljs.gro -o nofree.tpr
$GMX mdrun -nt 1 -s nofree.tpr -g nofree.log -e nofree.edr -o nofreeout.trr -c nofreeout.gro
echo 1 0 | $GMX energy -f nofree.edr -o nofree.xvg 
diff nofree.xvg free.xvg
```

Attached is also the output obtained locally from the diff, and the logfiles for force-switch
[nofree.log](/uploads/115893be0efb9a51ac2e494ef6e292d5/nofree.log)

[free.log](/uploads/b016d9950d9568139f0e3e0d513211f7/free.log)

Output for force-switch:

```
<     0.000000    0.941738
---
>     0.000000   -0.987267
```

(not good)

Output for potential-switch

```

---
>     0.000000    5.836455
```

(little off, but probably rounding errors)

Output for potential-shift

```

---

```

(little off, but probably rounding errors)

(In the .mdps, vdw-modifiers  Potential-switch and Potential-shift are commented out - by uncommenting those and commenting out force-switch, proper behavior can be observed)

**What is the current bug behavior?**

See above.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

We expect that the energies are the same with decoupling Lennard-Jones at lambda=0 and free energies on, as with free energies off, and it properly behaves with other VDW modifiers.  

**Possible fixes**

I spent an hour or so going through the current code, but was unable to find where the force-shift modification was currently appearing in the free energy code (or in the main code - it's changed too much since I last edited it!) but I'm happy to help debug and propose solutions if the relevant locations are flagged.

closed_issues.title: Performance regression with oneAPI 2024.2
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Possible performance regression from oneAPI 2024.1 to 2024.2 was found in Intel performance validation, but not yet reproduced by GROMACS team members. Their report is unclear, so this issue is a placeholder for me to investigate when time permits.

**GROMACS version**

2024.x

**Steps to reproduce**

Build and run on any Intel GPU hardware

**What is the current bug behavior?**

Probably slower with oneAPI 2024.2 than 2024.1.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Not slower with more recent oneAPI.

**Possible fixes**

Compiler team analyzed that their change to the implementation of `-ffp-model fast` could be an issue. Issues found with another HPC app on Aurora prompted the team to reconsider how that command-line flag should behave in the presence of NaN. In oneAPI 2024.2, the behavior is more conservative and checks for the possible computation of NaN. GROMACS doesn't need such checks, and wants to preserve the former (default) behaviour. So with oneAPI starting from 2024.2, GROMACS should use `-ffp-model fast=2`. This should probably be implemented by checking whether the compiler supports the more recent version, and using it when available. The core of the change is available in the patch file contents listed below.

```
From 4b8207bf57f1a9f0ca80101937b5fd00f5e2fb09 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mark Abraham <mark.j.abraham@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2024 00:31:08 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] Use -ffp-model fast=2

---
 cmake/gmxManageSYCL.cmake | 17 +++++++++++------
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

diff --git a/cmake/gmxManageSYCL.cmake b/cmake/gmxManageSYCL.cmake
index 36cbabb066..2df45bd570 100644
--- a/cmake/gmxManageSYCL.cmake
+++ b/cmake/gmxManageSYCL.cmake
@@ -367,16 +367,21 @@ else()
         message(WARNING "Cannot compile SYCL with per-kernel device-code splitting. Simulations will work, but the first step will be much slower than it needs to be. Try a different compiler.")
     endif()
 
-    # Add fast-math flag where available
+    # Add fp-model flag where available. "-ffp-model fast" is equivalent to "-ffast-math" (per
+    # https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/oneapi/optimization-guide-gpu/2024-1/fp-computations.html)
+    # and is the default at -O2 and higher. We also want the same numerical behaviour at lower optimization
+    # levels, so we add it explicitly. Before 2024.2, the implementation of "-ffp-model fast" assumed
+    # that NaN and infinite values would not appear, but this has been changed. Using "-ffp-model fast=2"
+    # chooses the older, more aggressive behavior.
     gmx_find_flag_for_source(
-        SYCL_FAST_MATH_CXX_FLAGS_RESULT
+        SYCL_FP_MODEL_FAST_CXX_FLAGS_RESULT
         "${SAMPLE_SYCL_SOURCE}"
         "CXX"
         SYCL_TOOLCHAIN_CXX_FLAGS
-        SYCL_FAST_MATH_CXX_FLAGS
-        "-ffast-math" "/clang:-ffast-math")
-    if (SYCL_FAST_MATH_CXX_FLAGS_RESULT)
-        set(SYCL_TOOLCHAIN_CXX_FLAGS "${SYCL_TOOLCHAIN_CXX_FLAGS} ${SYCL_FAST_MATH_CXX_FLAGS}")
+        SYCL_FP_MODEL_FAST_CXX_FLAGS
+        "-ffp-model fast=2" "/fp:fast=2")
+    if (SYCL_FP_MODEL_FAST_CXX_FLAGS_RESULT)
+        set(SYCL_TOOLCHAIN_CXX_FLAGS "${SYCL_TOOLCHAIN_CXX_FLAGS} ${SYCL_FP_MODEL_FAST_CXX_FLAGS}")
     endif()
 
     if("${SYCL_CXX_FLAGS_EXTRA}" MATCHES "fsycl-targets=.*(nvptx64|amdgcn)")```

/label ~Bug

closed_issues.title: Potential issue with verlet buffer and rlist in the 2024 releases (MARTINI force field)
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Dear GROMACS developers,

We recently ran into an issue with the MARTINI (v3.0) force field (with the [De Jong](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0010465515003628) non-bonded parameters) and the latest GROMACS 2024 releases.

After performing brief energy minimisation (steepest descent) on an [INSANE](https://github.com/Tsjerk/Insane)-generated DOPC bilayer (solvation and addition of NaCl also with INSANE), subsequent NVT equilibration failed when carried out with GROMACS 2024.0 and 2024.2. We have never had these issues previously, using various GROMACS versions (2020 through 2023). This system is named `equil_DOPC-2024_0` in the attached xz archive.

We set up the same simulation with 2023.3 (named `equil_DOPC-2023_3` in the xz archive), where everything proceeded smoothly. Running this (2023.3-generated) simulation with 2024.0 `mdrun` also resulted in a run that crashed immediately (named `equil_DOPC-2023_3-mdrun2024_0` in the xz archive).

It appears the issue might be related with GROMACS not modifying `rlist` after increasing `nstlist` when the verlet scheme is used (default verlet buffer tolerance). Disabling the verlet buffer (by setting `verlet-buffer-tolerance = -1`) and setting `rlist = rcoulomb = rvdw = 1.1` results in a non-crashing simulation (albeit not ideal from an energy conservation point but it could be easily set to 1.4 for example). This run is named `equil_DOPC-2024_0-rlist_1.1-vb_off` in the xz archive.

This behaviour was observed on two very different sets of hardware in our lab (only attaching the `gmx -quiet --version` output for one of them below) and also across different parallelisation schemes (1-32 threads, GPU/CPU builds).

[report.tar.xz](/uploads/a9d690b8bb37a8946bd4e936035a4248/report.tar.xz)

**GROMACS version**

```

                          :-) GROMACS - gmx, 2024 (-:

```

**Steps to reproduce**

The attached archive contains all the relevant files. Simply running any of the tpr files with a 2024 GROMACS release should result in the simulation crashing immediately.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

The `rlist` is not modified and the simulation crashes as soon as it starts.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

We expected the `rlist` to be modified accordingly.

All the log files are included in the attached archive.

**Possible fixes**

Nothing other than the suspicion that the `rlist` modification as a result of using the verlet scheme never actually takes place in this system for some reason.

+    nonLocalStream_ = deviceStreamManager.streamIsValid(DeviceStreamType::NonBondedNonLocal) ? &deviceStreamManager.stream(DeviceStreamType::NonBondedNonLocal) : nullptr;
     updateStream_   = &deviceStreamManager.stream(DeviceStreamType::UpdateAndConstraints);
 
     // Map the atom locality to the stream that will be used for coordinates,

closed_issues.title: Domain Decompositon Fatal Errors with Periodic Crosslinked Networks
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

I'm running systems of crosslinked polymer networks on Gromacs v 2023.3 on an HPC cluster. There appears to be issues with the domain decomposition for these systems. The same exact system works fine when running on one node (it just takes a very long time). I'm hoping to get the parallelization working so it would help to get this issue resolved.

## Exact steps to reproduce

I'm using 2 cores, with 1 thread each to troubleshoot the system. The system contains \~12k atoms. I'm minimizing my system and the minimization looks fine (plot attached below), I'm then heating it to 500K for 500 ps.

I'm attaching the exact files used as input in a zip file.

Previous step files:

* min.gro - The file input from the minimization step.
* min.top - Topology file input from the minimization step.

Current step files:

* heat.tpr
* heat.top
* heat.mdp - File for the step I'm running.
* heat.cpt - heat checkpoint

I run the following to create the heat.tpr (I'm attaching it anyways but adding this for reference.)

`gmx_mpi grompp -f heat.mdp -c min.gro -p min.top -o heat.tpr -pp heat.top -maxwarn 2`

I run the following for my production run:

`gmx_mpi mdrun -v -deffnm heat`

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

(1) Here is the exact error: Fatal error: One or more interactions were assigned to multiple domains of the domain decomposition. Please report this bug.

(2) I expect the system to run, or at least for an atom to not be in two domains.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

I've mentioned the relevant files above.

Here is the minimization of the system:

closed_issues.title: Add DOI to citation records
closed_issues.description:
It would be much more usefull to add DOI to each citation record for please_cite database.

Old view of please_cite records:

```
++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++
W. Kabsch, C. Sander
Dictionary of protein secondary structure: pattern recognition of
hydrogen-bonded and geometrical features.
Biopolymers 22 (1983) pp. 2577-2637
-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------
```

New proposed view of records:

```
++++ PLEASE READ AND CITE THE FOLLOWING REFERENCE ++++
W. Kabsch, C. Sander
Dictionary of protein secondary structure: pattern recognition of
hydrogen-bonded and geometrical features.
Biopolymers (1983)
DOI: 10.1002/bip.360221211
-------- -------- --- Thank You --- -------- --------
```

So in that case we can eliminate issue and pages for papers but add DOI

closed_issues.title: AdaptiveCpp runs fail with hip_queue: hipMemsetAsync() failed (error code = HIP:1)
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

GROMACS built with AdaptiveCpp usually runs fine on Dardel, but with some inputs fails mid-run with:

```
[hipSYCL Error] from /tmp/hellsvik/hipsycl/0.9.4/cpeGNU-22.06-rocm-5.3.3-llvm/hipSYCL-0.9.4/src/runtime/hip/hip_queue.cpp:355 @ submit_memset() : hip_queue: hipMemsetAsync() failed (error code = HIP:1)
============== hipSYCL error report ==============
hipSYCL has caught the following undhandled asynchronous errors:

    from /tmp/hellsvik/hipsycl/0.9.4/cpeGNU-22.06-rocm-5.3.3-llvm/hipSYCL-0.9.4/src/runtime/hip/hip_queue.cpp:355 @ submit_memset(): hip_queue: hipMemsetAsync() failed (error code = HIP:1)
    The application will now be terminated.
    terminate called without an active exception
    srun: error: nid002892: task 39: Aborted (core dumped)
    srun: launch/slurm: _step_signal: Terminating StepId=2789083.0
    slurmstepd: error: *** STEP 2789083.0 ON nid002892 CANCELLED AT 2023-11-03T01:03:07 ***
    srun: error: nid002892: tasks 0-38,40-63: Killed
    srun: Force Terminated StepId=2789083.0
```

- https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/hipsycl-error-when-running-with-multiple-mpis/7549

- @AndPdb92 observed similar errors with GROMACS 2024.1 + AdaptiveCpp 23.10, remediated by `HIPSYCL_RT_MAX_CACHED_NODES=5`.

## For developers: Why is this important?

GROMACS should not crash mid-run.

## Possible fixes

Here is what happens:

- On the step before an NS step, [force buffer clearing is launched](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/1fdbafbcc01e8ebb4a2b3ea4bae3aa9e7f8c3493/src/gromacs/nbnxm/nbnxm_gpu_data_mgmt.cpp#L740).
- It is not submitted to GPU immediately, but cached in ACpp's task graph.
- Then, on the NS step, [force and coordinate buffers are reallocated](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/1fdbafbcc01e8ebb4a2b3ea4bae3aa9e7f8c3493/src/gromacs/nbnxm/nbnxm_gpu_data_mgmt.cpp#L658).
- Then, [force buffer clearing for the new buffer is launched](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/1fdbafbcc01e8ebb4a2b3ea4bae3aa9e7f8c3493/src/gromacs/nbnxm/nbnxm_gpu_data_mgmt.cpp#L694).
- Then the task graph is flushed:
  - the memset operating on the old pointer is submitted (but does not return an error immediately),
  - the memset operating on the new buffer returns asynchronous error from the previous operation, `hipErrorInvalidValue`,
  - and exception is thrown and GROMACS crashes.

In CUDA it does not happen since, IIRC, memory (de)allocation does device-wide synchronization anyway. And even if synchronization is not forced, the buffer clearing is highly likely to succeed since it's quite fast.

Same is true for low `HIPSYCL_RT_MAX_CACHED_NODES` and (theoretically) the instant-submission mode: if we don't delay flushing the task graph, things should work fine.

A solution would be to add Local Stream synchronization before buffer reallocation. I do not think we even intend to explicitly rely on any synchronization before memory (de)allocations, so this would be a good practice anyway.

closed_issues.title: Results of MTTK barostat diffs from other barostats
closed_issues.description:
~"user bug report" 
## Summary

We found the density obtained with the MTTK barostat differs from that obtained with other barostats in GROMACS in 2024.1. 


## GROMACS version

2024.1

## Steps to reproduce

The attachment in GoogleDrive contains input files used for our testing. Except for the files labeled as 2018.8, all others are input files for version 2024.1. They include topology files, initial configurations, parameter files, and scripts submitted to the cluster.

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ZpfznDkV1dtxiIbGMlje_yKofWevwDvG/view?usp=sharing

## Current bug behavior

In GROMACS version 2018.8, the density obtained using all barostats, including MTTK, is approximately 1.018 g/cm³. However, in the latest version 2024.1, the density obtained with the MTTK barostat is 1.043 g/cm³.

|                                                  | Density            |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| GROMACS2018.8 Velocity-Verlet MTTK               | 1.01785±4.29353E-4 |
| GROMACS2024.1 Velocity-Verlet MTTK legacy        | 1.04337±4.32314E-4 |
| GROMACS2024.1 Velocity-Verlet MTTK modular       | 1.04318±8.92863E-5 |
| GROMACS2024.1 Velocity-Verlet C-rescale  legacy  | 1.01831±3.45471E-4 |
| GROMACS2024.1 Velocity-Verlet C-rescale  modular | 1.01788±3.5554E-4  |
| GROMACS2024.1 Leap-frog C-rescale legacy         | 1.01731±2.74053E-4 |
| GROMACS2024.1 Leap-frog C-rescale modular        | 1.01789±5.45831E-4 |
| GROMACS2024.1 Leap-frog PR legacy                | 1.01788±2.6744E-4  |
| GROMACS2024.1 Leap-frog PR modular               | 1.01771±5.76678E-4 |

We tested various barostats, including C-rescale, MTTK, and Parrinello-Rahman, under both leap-frog and velocity-verlet algorithms in both the legacy and modular simulators. It can be observed inconsistent density results are obtained only when using the MTTK pressure controller.

Subsequently, we tested multiple historical versions of GROMACS between 2018.8 and 2024.1. Until version 2020.7, the results with the MTTK pressure controller remained consistent with other barostats. Unfortunately, we were unable to successfully compile any versions from 2021. However, starting from version 2022, inconsistent results were obtained with the MTTK barostat.

## For developers: Why is this important?

The converged values of density should be the same for different barostats that was proved to exactly reproduce the NPT ensembles. The inconsistency of different methods in GROMACS is confusing for users. 


We look forward to the development team carefully analyzing our feedback and promptly addressing this issue. We appreciate their support and attention to our concerns.

## Update

Furthermore, we have tested the spc/fw model. The simulation of the spc/fw model in the literature yielded a density of 1.012 (±0.016) g/cm³.

Here is the literature link: https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2136877.

The result of C-rescale is still diff from MTTK barostat, but more close to the reference value.

closed_issues.title: Backup procedure fir Colvars output files is inconsistent with GROMACS backup
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The version of Colvars currently included in GROMACS 2024 violates the backup file-naming convention of GROMACS, by only keeping a single backup copy of its output files.  This is due to Colvars currently not using GROMACS library functions when backing up files.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Running `gmx mdrun` thrice with the same command line:
```
gmx mdrun -s topol.tpr -deffnm test
gmx mdrun -s topol.tpr -deffnm test
gmx mdrun -s topol.tpr -deffnm test
```
produces three versions of each GROMACS output file, e.g. for the log file:
```
test.log
#test.log.1#
#test.log.2#
```
but only **two** versions of the Colvars output files are produced:
```
test.colvars.traj
test.colvars.traj.BAK
```
because the output file written by the first command is overwritten. Other files (like `.colvars.state` files) are backed up with an `.old` suffix instead.

## For developers: Why is this important?

When running `gmx mdrun`, the expectation is that (1) all existing files whose name clash with new output files will be renamed, and (2) if the renamed file also exists already, an index is appended to distinguish output files.

Not honoring that expectations may lead to data loss.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots
```
 :-) GROMACS - gmx mdrun, 2024.2-dev-20240411-144262e3b2 (double precision) (-:
```
(using a GROMACS build based on Git worktree)

## Possible fixes

Merge request !4241

closed_issues.title: Consider adding access to the parlist to MDModules
closed_issues.description:
There is a need for multiple purposes, and in particular for machine learning potentials, for access to the pairlist. The way GROMACS works, this should be a list of pairs in the system, potentially split over ranks with domain decomposition (not a list of all pairs for each atom). We could provide a list in the ForceProvider callback per step, but for efficiency and for certain needs it is better to provide the list at pairlist construction time. Then a callback is needed that returns a struct with:
```
ArrayRef<const std::pair<int, int>> pairList // list of atom pairs
ArrayRef<const IVec> periodicShifts // the periodic displacements of atoms (will be zero for local atoms)
```

Then we additionally need to provide access to non-local atom coordinates in ForceProvider and we need to provide atom types for non-local atoms.

closed_issues.title: Fix DLB with IMPI+PVC using device UUID
closed_issues.description:
Currently GROMACS finds all available devices, and record in `DeviceInformation::id` the index corresponding to the order in which the runtime provided it to GROMACS. `gmx_hwinfo_t::deviceInfoList` is a vector of handles to `DeviceInformation` objects, the order of which happens to correspond to the runtime order, so the index of an object within `gmx_hwinfo_t::deviceInfoList` happens to be the same as the value of the `id` field of that object.

In some places we use the integer index of such an object as a "device ID" where we should probably use a `DeviceInformation*` directly, given that `gmx:hwinfo_t::deviceInfoList` is effectively a constant. That is a bit harder to misuse and avoids having to pass around the whole `gmx_hwinfo_t` object as well.

The `gmx_hwinfo_t::id` field is used for two things:
* indexing into via `mdrun -gpu_id` and `mdrun -gputasks` to see if the user's IDs correspond to compatible devices
* determining whether ranks are sharing devices to help DLB do better

We tacitly assume that the user understands the impact of any per-rank environment variables (e.g. `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` or the ROCm equivalent, or `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR`) that might affect which devices are visible with which indices. We could look for those variables while handling `mdrun -gpu_id` and `mdrun -gputasks` and warn of possible unexpected consequences.

If such variables are in use (which is routine when using IMPI on L0 and presumably later IMPI on CUDA), then typically each rank sees only a single device whose `DeviceInformation::id` will be 0. This is used to split an MPI communicator for DLB, but that is ineffective because all ranks would end up in the same DLB communicator.

Formally, the behaviour of (at least) DLB+IMPI+PVC is buggy in `release-2024`, but I've not yet made a fixed version that can see how big the consequences are. We'd need that before we decide whether to fix it in `release-2024`.

These thoughts arose following discussion from !4223 and should be addressed

- [ ] @al42and started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/4223#note_1848860585):  (+10 comments)

**Proposal**

Instead of splitting on `DeviceInformation::id` we should detect and use a device UUID to split that communicator. The GPU runtimes provide respectively `struct cudaDeviceProp::uuid`, `cl_khr_device_uuid`, `hipDeviceGetUUID()`, and `sycl::device.get_info<sycl::ext::intel::info::device::uuid>()` to provide the 32 8-bit fields of a UUID, which we can hash to an integer to use with `MPI_Comm_split`.

We still need a field of `DeviceInformation` that corresponds to the order in which the runtime presents the devices. Currently that is `id` but perhaps should be more like `deviceIndexFromRuntime`.

closed_issues.title: Constraint dH/dlambda incorrect with multiple time stepping
closed_issues.description: When doing free-energy calculations with multiple time stepping and perturbed constraint lengths, the slow force contributions to dH/dlambda were incorrectly multiplied by the MTS factor. The effect of this is usually rather small when only integrating the PME grid part less frequently, but can be substantial when the non-bonded pair interactions are not integrated at every step.

closed_issues.title: Inconsistency of gmx hbond analysis
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

The `gmx hbond` tool does not work as expected. Some donor/acceptor groups are not recognized in some instances, while they are recognized by the same tool in the legacy version `gmx hbond-legacy`.

**GROMACS version**

2024

**Steps to reproduce**

With these files

[analysis.gro](/uploads/d681f41335fe207edfb3946c99f580d6/analysis.gro)

[analysis.tpr](/uploads/e1c0dcfcfceaabc7097ef0788232e3a7/analysis.tpr)

[analysis_hbond.ndx](/uploads/3e815746d3e02a74e7929ade73722a35/analysis_hbond.ndx)

just run

` (echo "1";echo "2") | gmx hbond -f analysis.gro -s analysis.tpr -n analysis_hbond.ndx -num hbonds_num.xvg`

and 

`(echo "1";echo "2") | gmx hbond-legacy -f analysis.gro -s analysis.tpr -n analysis_hbond.ndx -num hbonds_num.xvg`


**What is the current bug behavior?**

I am running some hbond analysis because I want to take a look at the interactions between an arginine (ARG) in a protein and a lipid bilayer with two lipid types, cardiolipin (TLCL) and POPC. I am using GROMACS2024 and the tool gmx hbond and I do not modify the standard selection criteria within the tool, the only flags I use are for input/output.

Now, what happens is that I select the group ‘MEMB’, which contains both POPC and TLCL, and I get my hbond num vs time data. Then I do the same but specifying POPC and TLCL to check which of the two is contributing the most. TLCL works, while for POPC I get

```
Inconsistency in user input:
Selection ‘POPC’ has no donors AND has no acceptors! Nothing to be done.
```

Now, same files, but I use gmx hbond-legacy and…it works! I get the number of h-bonds vs time in all three cases, TLCL-ARG, POPC-ARG, and MEMB-ARG.

What is more puzzling, though, is the result. TLCL bounds very rarely with ARG, and this is shown with consistent results by both tools

![a](/uploads/8e5da3abe341a0d83794f0c74baa31e2/a.png)

For POPC I clearly do not have the corresponding non-legacy version for the tool as per the latter, and I get this with legacy

![b](/uploads/a4413e750a97aa27217d2659b2bc5901/b.png)

However, when I compute the h-bonding of ARG with the whole bilayer, I obtain the following

![c](/uploads/8909422555ace2764757eb4882379557/c.png)

Basically, the new tool applied on the whole membrane sees all the hbonds, also the POPC ones, as it can be seen by comparing POPC//legacy with MEMB//new. The only discrepancy is the peak around 286ns where the contribution of TLCL is missing in the POPC analysis, as it should be.

I thought this could have been an error of mine in the groups definitions, but I
i) visualize with VMD and clearly see hbonds with the same criteria between ARG and POPC
ii) I am using the same files with the two tools (the same index file in particular)
iii) I get the same results as `gmx hbond-legacy` if I use the normal `gmx hbond` tool in GROMACS2023.2

closed_issues.title: Checks for unsupported and invalid compilers happen too late
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

A CPU hardware benchmarking effort within Intel was still using GROMACS 2021.4 and icc 2021.6 (perhaps because Intel deprecated icc around then and we removed support for it immediately after in 18f24fc). When I asked them to update to GROMACS 2024.1, they continued using `icc` and ran into issues finding `libstdc++` *before* hitting our CMake code (introduced in that commit) that prompts people to avoid using `icc`. We should provide that prompt earlier. This will also avoid other people using unsupported compilers wasting time resolving issues before being informed that their compiler will never work.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Try to build GROMACS 2021.4 with oneAPI 2021.1

## For developers: Why is this important?

Users wasting time is not nice.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

CMake can stop when it is unable to find `std::filesystem` when we actually want it to tell the user to stop using `icc`.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

N/A

## Possible fixes

Reorder the CMake so we warn about compilers before we search for c++17 support

closed_issues.title: gmx check reads TPR files differently if it was compiled with/without COLVARS support
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

TPRs that were written with COLVARS support cannot be read when GROMACS was compiled without COLVARS.

**GROMACS version**

GROMACS main at 2024-04-03.

**Steps to reproduce**

This was exposed when testing !4105 against re-generated regression tests: https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/jobs/6538982042. The reference TPRs were re-generated in https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs-regressiontests/-/merge_requests/64 with a GROMACS version that supported COLVARS. The tests fail only on  gromacs:clang-9:regressiontest which is set-up without COLVARS support since c6b2c30b. The mdp settings (or TPR files) do not use colvars.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

`gmx check` should not fail because there is an empty colvars block in a TPR file.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

The regression tests should pass regardless if they are run using a binary with or without COLVARS support.

For now, I might re-generate the TPR files using a GROMACS version that is compiled without COLVARS support. That will not fix the issue, but at least make the regression tests pass.

**Possible fixes**

**Summary**

I noticed that when using MTS(multiple time stepping), additional updates are introduced as shown in the following figure:
![image](/uploads/d4955889046539b84822773457a15e7e/image.png)
At the same time, the underlying implementation of update_for_constraint_virial is achieved through updateMDLeapfrogSimple (or updateMDLeapfrogSimpleSimd) in updat.cpp. However, this implementation corresponds only to the integrator=md. In addition, I have identified another potential bug. During the additional update steps, the constrain_coordinates function updates the atomic velocities, which should not happen in reality. Best regards,
Patrick

closed_issues.title: SIMD AVX-512 compiler flags set for Intel compiler are not working on Zen 4
closed_issues.description:
Thanks to #4715, GROMACS selects AVX512 for Zen 4, which sets

```
SIMD_AVX_512_CXX_FLAGS:INTERNAL= -xCORE-AVX512 -qopt-zmm-usage=high
SIMD_AVX_512_C_FLAGS:INTERNAL= -xCORE-AVX512 -qopt-zmm-usage=high
```

This flag is not generating the code that runs on Zen 4. That is, after compiling and running tests, they fail with:

> Please verify that both the operating system and the processor support Intel(R) X87, CMOV, MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4_1, SSE4_2, MOVBE, POPCNT, AVX, F16C, FMA, BMI, LZCNT, AVX2, AVX512F, AVX512DQ, ADX, AVX512CD, AVX512BW and AVX512VL instructions.

We should get something like:

```
-march=skylake-avx512
```

instead (`-march=znver4` is supported only from version 2024).

I see two ways to fix this:

- introduce another branch under AVX-512F that selects different flags if AMD CPU was detected, or
- switch to newer style compile flags for Intel and AMD CPUs since we don't support legacy Intel compiler anymore.

CC @mark.j.abraham
