closed_issues.title: gmxapi.commandline_operation has potentially confusing behavior with relative paths in *input_files* parameter
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

https://manual.gromacs.org/current/gmxapi/userguide/pythonreference.html#gmxapi.commandline_operation briefly mentions that tasks run in separate directories, but does not provide any warning about how this could affect assumptions about relative paths.

This means that a relative path for the calling script is *different* than for the executed subprocess.

Reference https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/4826#note_1469468404

## Exact steps to reproduce

Get the current directory contents with Python's `subprocess` module:
```
python -c 'import subprocess; subprocess.run(("ls", "-la", "."))'
```

Get the current directory contents with `gmxapi.commandline_operation`:
```
python -c 'from gmxapi import commandline_operation as cli; print(cli("ls",["-la"], input_files={"": "."}).output.stdout.result())'
```

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

A user might expect relative paths of *input_files* to resolve relative to the generated task directory. This seems unlikely, since we never implemented a feature to pre-load contents to the task working directory.

A more reasonable expectation is that relative paths should be converted to absolute paths *before* instantiating the command line task.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

See #4826

## Possible fixes

* Implicitly convert relative paths in *input_files* to absolute paths early in `gmxapi.commandline.commandline_operation()`, and/or
* Warn the user when relative paths appear in *input_files*, and cite #4311 for additional discussion

In any case, the documentation needs expansion.

closed_issues.title: gmx dssp: document all the symbols used
closed_issues.description:
The official DSSP manual ([1](https://github.com/PDB-REDO/dssp/blob/trunk/doc/mkdssp.md#details), [2](https://pdb-redo.eu/dssp/about)) only lists the following symbols:

- H = α-helix
- B = residue in isolated β-bridge
- E = extended strand, participates in β ladder
- G = 310-helix
- I = π-helix
- P = κ-helix / poly-proline II helix
- S = bend
- T = hydrogen-bonded turn
- `space` = gap (listed only in [1])

`gmx dssp`, however, also outputs `~` for loop and `=` for break. 

This is not documented anywhere, but should be.

It could be helpful to add a documentation for the "standard" symbols too. Add some kind of auto-generated section to the string passed to `settings->setHelpText(...)`?

User post: https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/dssp-labels-and-making-xpm-eps-files/6799

closed_issues.title: Domain decomposition does not handle bonded interations with large distances
closed_issues.description: mdrun should automatically communicate atoms that do not have all their bonded interactions assigned, such that bonded interactions with distances larger than the pairlist cutoff are handled correctly. Due to a negation in the checks for links between atoms with bonded interactions, this functionality was missing in the 2023 release. Only with a workaround of -noddbondcheck and -rdd could such system be ran.

closed_issues.title: Gromacs 2023.1 never updates *_prev.cpt checkpoint file
closed_issues.description:
It seems that Gromacs 2023.1 never replaces *_prev.cpt checkpoint file with the newer one if there already exist a *_prev.cpt file. It writes a *_prev.cpt only if there is no one already existing, and then never updates it.

For this reason, if you restart your simulation from the previous checkpoint file (*_prev.cpt), you restart it from the very first one and lose the whole trajectory.

closed_issues.title: OpenCL clearDeviceBufferAsync is leaking cl_event's
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

In OpenCL, `clearDeviceBufferAsync` is requesting an event from `clEnqueueFillBuffer`, but does not call `clReleaseEvent` on it or use it in any way. This leads to resource leakage.

Introduced far back in dc6c9960.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Running `gmx mdrun` with OpenCL under valgrind produces, among other warnings, multiple instances of the following:

```
==3859774== 1,296 (648 direct, 648 indirect) bytes in 1 blocks are definitely lost in loss record 2,242 of 2,365
==3859774==    at 0x483CFD3: operator new(unsigned long) (vg_replace_malloc.c:472)
==3859774==    by 0x72B44E4: clEnqueueFillBuffer (in /opt/tcbsys/rocm/5.4.1/20.04/lib/libamdocl64.so)
==3859774==    by 0x55B5113: void clearDeviceBufferAsync<float>(TypedClMemory<float>*, unsigned long, unsigned long, DeviceStream const&) [clone .part.0] (devicebuffer_ocl.h:272)
==3859774==    by 0x55B877A: pme_gpu_reinit_atoms(PmeGpu*, int, float const*, float const*) (pme_gpu_internal.cpp:1445)
==3859774==    by 0x4F2EBB0: gmx::mdAlgorithmsSetupAtomData(t_commrec const*, t_inputrec const&, gmx_mtop_t const&, gmx_localtop_t*, t_forcerec*, gmx::ForceBuffers*, gmx::MDAtoms*, gmx::Constraints*, gmx::VirtualSitesHandler*, gmx_shellfc_t*) (mdsetup.cpp:147)
==3859774==    by 0x56A9F66: gmx::LegacySimulator::do_md() (md.cpp:390)
==3859774==    by 0x56A3551: gmx::LegacySimulator::run() (legacysimulator.cpp:72)
==3859774==    by 0x56D74A3: gmx::Mdrunner::mdrunner() (runner.cpp:2220)
==3859774==    by 0x113607: gmx::gmx_mdrun(tmpi_comm_*, gmx_hw_info_t const&, int, char**) (mdrun.cpp:280)
==3859774==    by 0x113799: gmx::gmx_mdrun(int, char**) (mdrun.cpp:82)
==3859774==    by 0x4EE7A54: gmx::CommandLineModuleManager::run(int, char**) (cmdlinemodulemanager.cpp:569)
==3859774==    by 0x10FDBF: main (gmx.cpp:58)
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

OpenCL is deprecated, but continuously leaking resources while we're running is not nice.

Potentially the reason for https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/increasing-and-excesive-use-of-memory-using-opencl-and-amd-gpu/6604.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

1. GROMACS leaks resources on each call to `clearDeviceBufferAsync`, and the memory usage of the `gmx` process growth over time.
2. GROMACS properly manages OpenCL resources, and the memory usage of the long-running process stays approximately constant.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

- https://man.opencl.org/clEnqueueFillBuffer.html
- https://man.opencl.org/clReleaseEvent.html

## Possible fixes

Since the event is not used, pass `NULL` instead.

closed_issues.title: cuFFTMp testing limited after CI upgrade
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

[Our helper script for cuFFTMp testing](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/db9d71ddbd84bd1c81f39a4fae0f8cdc627751ab/admin/ci-scripts/gromacs-base-test.sh#L22), introduced in !3359, has special logic to:

- Disable PME decomposition codepath on devices with CC < 7.0,
- Disable FFT decomposition unit test on devices with < 8GiB memory.

It was introduced to handle the variety of GPUs we had at the time. Now, we only have NVIDIA T400, which have CC 7.5 and 4 GiB of memory.

Thus, we're always excluding `FFTMpiUnitTests` when running in our CI.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Look at the logs of a recent `gromacs:gcc-11-cuda-11.7.1:testMPI` job.

## For developers: Why is this important?

- Our CI scripts contain outdated code to support the hardware that's not in our CI anymore.
- A cuFFTMp test is always silently skipped in the CI job dedicated to testing cuFFTMp.

closed_issues.title: Non-bonded force computation get very inefficient for inhomogenous systems
closed_issues.description: The NBNxM module sets the size of the cell in x/y for the (cluster-)pair search grid based on the average density in the system. If the system is very inhomogeneous, e.g. contains a lot of vacuum, these cells will be too large. This causes cluster pairs to become very flat which leads to many more cluster pairs ending up in the pair list. The can decrease the performance by one or more orders of magnitude for a system or e.g. a droplet in a large box with vacuum/vapor.

closed_issues.title: gmx hbond produces random output
closed_issues.description: Due to not initializing arrays, gmx hbond could produce random output. The results depend on the state of the memory and the compiler used. Often the first tens of frames would have random hydrogen bond counts.

closed_issues.title: gromacs config package may depend on undefined target std::filesystem
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

810c23890204e36f84fbb99234b28e25727333b1 borrows a `FindFilesystem.cmake` that can be used at configure time in the build tree to help set up C++17 compatibility.

If used, a `std::filesystem` target [becomes part of the INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/1e2b7fd99526dfae57034bbc8615a84d5925e865/src/gromacs/CMakeLists.txt#L405):
```
if(CXX_FILESYSTEM_HAVE_FS)
    target_link_libraries(libgromacs PUBLIC std::filesystem)
endif()
```

There is no provision to satisfy this dependency in [gromacs-config.cmake](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/1e2b7fd99526dfae57034bbc8615a84d5925e865/src/gromacs/gromacs-config.cmake.cmakein), and there is no installed "find" module with which to recreate it.

## Exact steps to reproduce

I don't know specifically how to trigger this path, or whether it is tested in our pipelines. The issue was discovered in a GPU-enabled gromacs build on dardel.pdc.kth.se.

Sample error output:

```
      CMake Error at /cfs/klemming/projects/snic/membrane-infection/install-gpu/gromacs23-tmpi-gpu/share/cmake/gromacs/libgromacs.cmake:83 (set_
target_properties):
        The link interface of target "Gromacs::libgromacs" contains:
      
          std::filesystem
      
        but the target was not found.  Possible reasons include:
      
          * There is a typo in the target name.
          * A find_package call is missing for an IMPORTED target.
          * An ALIAS target is missing.
      
      Call Stack (most recent call first):
        /cfs/klemming/projects/snic/membrane-infection/install-gpu/gromacs23-tmpi-gpu/share/cmake/gromacs/gromacs-config.cmake:56 (include)
        CMakeLists.txt:103 (find_package)
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

We can't advertise interface dependencies that cannot be satisfied.

## Possible fixes

`#include <filesystem>` occurs in several installed (legacy) headers, so we can't just toggle the dependency to PRIVATE.

We either need to provide the same utility to client software or extract the details we actually need into either transitive usage requirements or other CMake hints (provided through `find_package(gromacs)` or through `gromacs-hints.cmake`).

closed_issues.title: hipSYCL builds produce invalid CMake config files
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The exported CMake package has `hipSYCL::hipSYCL-rt` in the `INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES` in `libgromacs.cmake`, but `gromacs-config.cmake` does not have a corresponding `find_dependency(hipSYCL REQUIRED)`.

This means that `find_package(gromacs); target_link_libraries(mysoftware Gromacs::libgromacs)` does not work.

The nature of this bug depends on whether the installed headers and libgromacs actually convey a dependency on hipSYCL to client software.

## Exact steps to reproduce

A GPU build of gromacs 2023 on Dardel (PDC) uses hipSYCL.

After installation, a client build system that tries to `find_package(gromacs)` gets something like the following.

```
      -- Configuring done
      CMake Error at /<prefix>/share/cmake/gromacs/libgromacs.cmake:83 (set_target_properties):
        The link interface of target "Gromacs::libgromacs" contains:
      
          hipSYCL::hipSYCL-rt
      
        but the target was not found.  Possible reasons include:
      
          * There is a typo in the target name.
          * A find_package call is missing for an IMPORTED target.
          * An ALIAS target is missing.
      
      Call Stack (most recent call first):
        /<prefix>/share/cmake/gromacs/gromacs-config.cmake:56 (include)
        CMakeLists.txt:103 (find_package)
      
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

Users of gromacs client software are users of gromacs. Developers of gromacs client software are gromacs contributors. There's something inconsistent with our CMake scripting, and our build system infrastructure will be stronger if we fix it.

## Possible fixes

Either
* downgrade the scope of the dependency: `target_link_libraries(libgromacs PRIVATE hipSYCL::hipSYCL-rt)`, or
* update the export generators for the CMake CONFIG package.

@eirrgang can contribute a fix once it is clear whether the interface dependency is real or accidental.

closed_issues.title: CMake succeeds with broken OpenMP, issuing only a warning
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Some compilers ship with partially-broken OpenMP, for example, Intel LLVM in oneAPI (!3409) or Apple Clang (https://open-box.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation/openmp_macos.html). In both cases, OpenMP can be enabled but requires some manual steps from the user.

Currently, when a user runs `cmake` without any OpenMP-related options with such a compiler, a warning is issued, `GMX_OPENMP` is set to `OFF`, and the configuration proceeds, resulting in an OpenMP-less build.

This behavior can be suboptimal: the warning is easy to miss among the rest of the CMake output, while OpenMP is highly desirable to have.

So, I suggest turning this `WARNING` into a `FATAL_ERROR` unless `GMX_OPENMP` is set to `OFF`.

## Exact steps to reproduce

!3409 provides some detail on the Intel LLVM case.

## For developers: Why is this important?

A build without OpenMP is likely not what most users need, so it's bad to use it as an automatic fallback.

## Possible fixes

!3641

closed_issues.title: The AWH growth factor should be user controllable
closed_issues.description:
The AWH growth factor for the initial, exponential stage is hard-coded to the value of 3. This works well for good reaction coordinates with systems starting from equilibrated initial states. But for degenerate reaction coordinates and/or systems starting from non-equilibrated initial states, a factor 3 can sometimes lead to exiting the initial stage with a too high errors and too low update size.

The growth factor should be user controllable by an mdp parameter.

Changing the default value to 2 is likely also desirable. This increases stability at the cost of a slight decrease in efficiency.

closed_issues.title: Python package build system needs updates for scikit-build-core > 0.4
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The `-C/path/to/cmake-hints` in `$CMAKE_ARGS` from !3531 is no longer being handled correctly since scikit-build-core 0.4.x.

We probably need to update both our tests and our documentation, once we figure out a better way to provide the necessary toolchain hints.

## Exact steps to reproduce

If the following works
```
pip install scikit-build-core[pyproject]"<0.4"
pip install /path/to/gromacs/repo/python_packaging/gmxapi
```

the following may not

```
pip install --upgrade scikit-build-core[pyproject]
pip install /path/to/gromacs/repo/python_packaging/gmxapi
```

Note that, in the failing case, only the scikit-build-core provided cmake cache file is used. The gromacs hints file is ignored.

## For developers: Why is this important?

We should keep on top of the evolution of scikit-build-core since it is the best prospect for progress on #4737 

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

Per discussion at !3531, `CMAKE_ARGS` is the approach that has been documented (for longer) to provide the tool chain hints to dependent Python packages (via the `-C` cmake option to pre-initialize the cmake cache).

If the cmake cache file is not used, scikit-build-core + CMake may use the wrong compiler tool chain and fail to build a dependent package. The `pip` output will likely not be helpful.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

Ref
* !3637

closed_issues.title: GPU performance and energy of tabulated vs analytical Ewald NB kernel
closed_issues.description:
## Introduction
- For non-bonded (NB) force calculations on GPU, GROMACS has the option of using tabulated (tab) or analytical (ana) Ewald kernels.
- tab uses tabulated data which is read from cache (more memory loads), while ana recalculates the data (more flops).
- For modern NVIDIA GPUs (CC>=8.0), tab is default on 8.0 (A100), and ana is default for all others (see https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/987). 
- The default can be overridden with GMX_GPU_NB_ANA_EWALD or GMX_GPU_NB_TAB_EWALD
- Here we analyze the performance *and energy* for these options, to help assess whether current defaults should be changed. 

## Performance and Energy Results
![ANA_TAB_v2](/uploads/65faab1a02cb68b2ba1ca584702d69dc/ANA_TAB_v2.JPG){width=70%}

- Results are end-to-end on single-GPU (which is dominated by the NB kernel)
- tab is best on 8.0 (A100) for both performance and energy
- ana is best on 8.6 (A40) and 8.9 (L40) for both performance and energy
- On H100, there is no significant performance difference, but **energy is lower for ana**. This is likely because more energy is required for the extra loads with tab on H100 than is required for the extra flops with ana.
- Note that the energy measurements are for GPU energy. For more details on the process to obtain these results, and on the typical effect of including non-GPU energy, please see https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/on-demand/session/gtcspring23-s52087/.    


## Conclusions
- Given the above results, indications are that the current default are best, but more experiments should be done to confirm.

TO DO
- [ ] Repeat experiments, using water boxes (to avoid bonded forces in background). To further isolate NB kernel, either use 2xGPU and only measure energy on PP GPU, or use RF.

closed_issues.description:
## Summary

It seemed clever to reference `src/testutils/simulationdatabase/spc216.top` and `src/testutils/simulationdatabase/spc216.gro` in `testdata.json` (https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/commit/929343d11b53d1351c7090170d6cdda931eddce8#note_1369613042), but this means that the test suite is more fragile than might be assumed.

## Exact steps to reproduce

How one can reproduce the issue - this is important; remember to attach all relevant files, in particular the original files so we can regenerate the TPR when necessary.

## For developers: Why is this important?

Flexible and robust testing utilities help troubleshooting and diagnosing more scenarios.

This may be worth fixing in the `release-2023` branch, along with back-porting (at least `conftest.py` from) https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/3574

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

When gromacs and gmxapi are installed, and the `gmxapi/test` directory is available, we should be able to validate the installation with
`python -m pytest -x -rA -l /path/to/gromacs-source/python_packaging/gmxapi/test/`

Instead, the `solvate` command in [spc_water_box_collection fixture](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/python_packaging/gmxapi/test/conftest.py#L111) fails because it can't find files from `src/testutils/simulationdatabase/`.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

```
ERROR ../python_packaging/gmxapi/test/test_fileio.py::test_tprfile_read_old - RuntimeError: solvate failed in spc_water_box testing fixture.
```

## Possible fixes

1. Make the testdata more robust.
  * We can try to rewrite these lines with absolute paths to the source tree while processing in `conftest.py`
  * We can try to set appropriate environment variables (with `os.environ` in `conftest.py`) so that the paths are resolvable by the forked `grompp`. (Requires https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/3574)
2. Either we should embed the necessary files in the sdist, or we should remove the brittle test director from the sdist.

closed_issues.title: gmxapi needs build-dependent argument checking
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Now that gmxapi supports MPI-GROMACS as well as thread-MPI-GROMACS, run time options that used to work may cause mysteriously quiet failures.

The errors are due to command line options that are defined only depending on the gromacs build configuration.

The errors are particularly silent because libgromacs does not have much of a mechanism for API error reporting, and the simulator options are mostly still handled with old command-line-centric parsers.

The potential for such errors was overlooked, and a quick fix is possible at the python level by extending the existing argument processing.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Build gmxapi for MPI-GROMACS and pass the `threads` or `nt` options to the simulator.

## For developers: Why is this important?

The problem is hard to describe or discover when helping someone else troubleshoot or when running automated tests.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

An invalid mdrun command line argument causes a simulation to fail without helpful output.

Preferably, the invalid argument should be caught earlier and reported clearly as a Python exception.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

The cause of the failure can be found exclusively in the `md.log` file.

```
Source file: src/gromacs/taskassignment/resourcedivision.cpp (line 711)

Fatal error:
Setting the total number of threads is only supported with thread-MPI and
GROMACS was compiled without thread-MPI
```

## Possible fixes
We have limited options to improve the user experience with such errors without undertaking (long overdue) updates to the mdrun call stack. For specific cases like this one, though, we can duplicate some error-checking logic and pre-screen the mdrun arguments before passing them to the library.

- [ ] https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/python_packaging/gmxapi/src/gmxapi/simulation/workflow.py#L753 to https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/python_packaging/gmxapi/src/gmxapi/simulation/workflow.py#L756 should be expanded to include a test for an MPI versus tMPI gromacs build.
* Future consolidation and modernization of the mdrun command line processing should provide convenient places to catch exceptions in the API.
* Policy decisions need to be made about how to approach error modes in API use cases.

closed_issues.title: Free energy calculation segmentation fault when "pair" parameters change
unexpected attraction between two separate molecules that are scaled by 0<lambda<1 using the free energy code
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Hello,

We have observed unexpected attraction between two separate molecules that are scaled by 0<lambda<1 using the free energy code (gromacs 2023). There is no such special attraction at either end state (lambda =0 or =1). We can reproduce this behavior in a simplified model system that is a neutral box of water with sodium and chloride ions, with one ion of each type being influenced by the free energy code. We make unique molecules for these, which are like the normal NA and CL except that their charges are zero in the B state.
 

To assess whether or not this issue exists in a give setup, we run 50 ps of MD simulation and track the interatomic distance between the free-energy-relevant NA and CL ions (as compared to other NA/CL distances). We say the issue exists when the free-energy-relevant ions rapidly associate and stay together. A file is attached (ionAssociation_tarball.tgz) that can be used to test this effect.
 

There is an obvious issue when:
- the free energy code is on, and lambda is set to a constant value of 0.5
 

There is no obvious issue when:
- the free energy code is off (free-energy = no in the .mdp file) 
- the free energy code is on, and lambda is set to a constant value of 1 or 0
 

These things did not appear to resolve the issue:
- using the sd integrator (velocity Langevin) in place of the md integrator (velocity Verlet)
- running in serial (single process/thread)
- using beutler (not gapsys) software potentials
- turning off all softcore potentials
- using gromacs 2019.6 or 2016.6 or 5.1.6 (with softcore turned off) instead of gromacs 2023
 

Other analyses we did:
- checked the minimum distance from the coupled Na or Cl to water during the simulations at different lambda values. Closest is at lambda = 0 (fully charged), intermediate at lambda = 0.5, and farthest min distance at lambda = 1.0 (uncharges LJ spheres). 
- ran simulations of a NVT system with only one Na and one Cl and then reanalyzed with gmx mdrun -rerun and gmx energy at different lambda values. Everything made sense (i.e., LJ the same and Coulomb scaled by lambda)
- did 0-step energy minimization to get forces on the two free-energy-relevant ions in a box of water. The force vectors with lambda=0.5 are the exact averages of the force vectors with lambda values of 0 and 1.
- setup a system with only 1 Na and 1 Cl ion lying along the x axis, both affected by the free-energy code. Did single step MD to look at forces, velocities, and changes in coordinates. Everything looks correct in terms of ratios based on lambda.

## Exact steps to reproduce

- download the attached tarball and execute run.sh. Inspect dist.xvg to look at second column (dist between two lambda-modified ions) vs., first column (time), or just look at the thick red line in plot.distances.pdf (if gnuplot is working in your env).

## For developers: Why is this important?

- We suspect that this behavior is caused by a bug. However, it may also be an emergent effect due to charge screening (see comment I left in the second post here: https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/coupling-two-ions-to-lambda-0-5-cuts-their-charge-charge-interaction-force-by-1-2-not-1-4/6028 )

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

- (1) what happens: the lambda-scaled ions reliably associate on the 10-50 ps timescale at lambda=0.5
- (2) what did I expect to happen: no special attraction at lambda=0.5 that is not present at either lambda=0 or lambda=1

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

attached files to reproduce and example output as tarball. Also included the analysis image separately for ease of visualization. In this image, the distance between the lambda-scaled Na and Cl is a red thick line, whereas all other Na/Cl distances are thin lines. 

[plot.distances.pdf](/uploads/15bcd824d787e9cd3908c0b999d4e3b8/plot.distances.pdf)
[ionAssociation_tarball.tgz](/uploads/049da00726c5752360e44587570bd046/ionAssociation_tarball.tgz)

## Possible fixes

Docs should recommend use of update groups, so that we can encourage sites wanting strong-scaling benchmarks to use good ones. Current papers and docs don't reflect our intentions.

Sites will choose hardware based on relevant strong-scaling benchmarks

Users wanting strong scaling indirectly benefit from getting hardware that matches their needs. closed_issues.description:
## Summary

We should set the DOWNLOAD_EXTRACT_TIMESTAMP policy for use with newer CMake. See https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/policy/CMP0135.html.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Use cmake 3.26 and the download-fftw option:

```
...
CMake Warning (dev) at /opt/hpc_software/tools/cmake/3.26.0/share/cmake-3.26/Modules/ExternalProject.cmake:3092 (message):
  The DOWNLOAD_EXTRACT_TIMESTAMP option was not given and policy CMP0135 is
  not set.  The policy's OLD behavior will be used.  When using a URL
  download, the timestamps of extracted files should preferably be that of
  the time of extraction, otherwise code that depends on the extracted
  contents might not be rebuilt if the URL changes.  The OLD behavior
  preserves the timestamps from the archive instead, but this is usually not
  what you want.  Update your project to the NEW behavior or specify the
  DOWNLOAD_EXTRACT_TIMESTAMP option with a value of true to avoid this
  robustness issue.
Call Stack (most recent call first):
  /opt/hpc_software/tools/cmake/3.26.0/share/cmake-3.26/Modules/ExternalProject.cmake:4209 (_ep_add_download_command)
  src/external/build-fftw/CMakeLists.txt:115 (ExternalProject_add)
This warning is for project developers.  Use -Wno-dev to suppress it.
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

We should not have CMake warnings cluttering our build.

## Possible fixes

I suggest we adopt NEW and do it in release-2023 branch, as it is nice for users also and does not impact correctness or stability.

MPI_Send is blocking NB kernel for GPU-direct PP-PME comms with libMPI
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

For GPU Direct PP-PME communications with lib-MPI, the PP rank is using MPI_Send to send coordinate data to the PME rank. But this is unnecessarily blocking the non-bonded GPU kernel (which won't update the coordinate data) from starting. See the gap in the timeline caused by the MPI_Send in the profile screenshot.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Profile STMV using libMPI. 

## For developers: Why is this important?

We want GROMACS to be as optimal as possible.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots
![Screenshot_2023-03-13_125546](/uploads/c50a19f61466f5d4ec05f4758a752e50/Screenshot_2023-03-13_125546.jpg)

This is for STMV running with 4 MPI tasks running across 2 compute nodes. See the gap in the "All streams" row caused by the MPI_Send in the above row.

## Possible fixes

MPI_Send should be replaced with non-blocking MPI_Isend+MPI_Wait. The wait should be called after the NB kernel has been launched.

closed_issues.title: Consider the use of oneMKL interfaces for GROMACS SYCL FFT libraries
closed_issues.description:
The [oneMKL interfaces library](https://github.com/oneapi-src/oneMKL) is a marshalling library that aims to simplify using backend libraries for SYCL. Currently, it supports RNG and BLAS interfaces; however, there are open [PRs](https://github.com/oneapi-src/oneMKL/pull/278) for adding FFT functionality, which could be useful for GROMACS. Using the oneMKL interface FFT domain could significantly simplify the code in GROMACS by offloading the management of the vendor libraries to a third party for both cmake, and the code for the actual computation, by introducing an additional dependency. 

This issue aims to start a discussion on this topic and to asses the requirements that oneMKL interfaces library would need to fulfill before it could be used for GROMACS.

closed_issues.title: Intel LLVM: SYCL_CXX_FLAGS_EXTRA not added to MPI_CXX_LINK_FLAGS
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

When building GROMACS with SYCL/IntelLLVM for a custom target, linker flags must be properly set (e.g., `-fsycl -fsycl-targets=amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -Xsycl-target-backend=amdgcn-amd-amdhsa --offload-arch=gfx90a`).

Normally, these flags are passed to the linker when they are supplied via `-DSYCL_CXX_FLAGS_EXTRA`.

However, when building with MPI support and custom `-DMPI_CXX_LINK_FLAGS` value, these flags are not added automatically. This leads to linker errors.

Not an issue when using IntelMPI, but a problem when targeting NVIDIA/AMD devices.

closed_issues.title: Subprocesses in MPI contexts need more comprehensive environment handling.
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Documentation and pytest configuration may be insufficient for some software environments.

### Example

The problem encountered at https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/gmxapi-runtimeerror-solvate-failed-in-spc-water-box-testing-fixture/6097 was due to heavy-handed environment replacement such as https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/python_packaging/gmxapi/test/conftest.py#L167.

These environment replacements were an attempt at a simple fix to #4421, but the side effects were extreme and egregious. To resolve #4421 without affecting many unrelated use cases, we need a more delicate resolution that filters only MPI-related environment variables so that non-MPI-related environment variables remain intact, as expected.

## Exact steps to reproduce

If the `gmx*` command requires LD_LIBRARYPATH or environment variables other than PATH in order to function correctly,
* the [`solvate`](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/commit/4203b238c526e875a9205676dad365f50549e5c2#f7732bd0dced00a6a4c681f4acae06f0d2ed9e94_119_119) and [`grompp`](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/commit/4203b238c526e875a9205676dad365f50549e5c2#f7732bd0dced00a6a4c681f4acae06f0d2ed9e94_159_160) commands in the pytest fixtures will fail
* the [documentation about using the *env* keyword argument](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/commit/4203b238c526e875a9205676dad365f50549e5c2#f3822607c5faec0e768934c4fd5e25ebd385a7e1_376_394) is insufficient

This is not always reproducible. It is most likely to appear with a shared object build in an environment where transitive dependencies are dynamically linked with reliance on transient runtime environment details. E.g. `module load hwloc` introduces transitive dependencies that do not get included in the libgromacs rpath. 

## For developers: Why is this important?

* Configuring with `-DGMX_PYTHON_PACKAGE=ON` could cause `make check` to fail in an affected software environment.
* The combinatorics of factors involved could cause user confusion and will be difficult to diagnose in discussion on the forums.
* The *env* key word argument to `commandline_operation` will be used more, now that there are more use cases for `gmxapi`+`libgromacs_mpi`

### Background

When running a command line subprocess through `gmxapi.commandline_operation()` from a script that was launched with MPI, we don't know whether the command is MPI-aware.

If it is not MPI aware, then running it on all ranks would duplicate work, and would require separate task working directories.

If it is MPI aware, then we either need to manipulate the environment so that it does not see the MPI context and can then behave well running on a single rank, or run it on all ranks with the _same_ task working directories using some sort of launch method that can handle MPI already being initialized in the parent process (which probably still requires cleaning the environment and making a fresh `mpiexec` (or equivalent) call).

We previously decided on a minimal change in which `gmxapi.commandline_operation()` invokes a single subprocess and advised users to provide an appropriate environment.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

The details discovered by CMake should be sufficient for wrapping command line operations for the installed GROMACS,
* for regular usage
* for the test fixtures
  - in the build tree, and
  - for regular `pip install`+`pytest` use cases.

Instead, build and installation could appear to succeed, but `make check` or run time usage could encounter strange errors ultimately related to mismatched/missing linking details affected by environment variables.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

Ref https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/gmxapi-runtimeerror-solvate-failed-in-spc-water-box-testing-fixture/6097

## Possible fixes

* Better environment manipulation
  * Provide more elaboration in the docs and find a better subset of environment variables to copy for subprocesses in the test suite.
  * Prune specific environment variables from the environment passed to the subprocess.
* Smarter invocation
  * Expand `gmxapi.commandline_operation` to have a more complete expression of multiprocessing / HPC resource contexts.
  * Suppress or manipulate MPI initialization in command line tools that do not use MPI.

closed_issues.title: GPU PME pipelining: Spread does not wait for grid clearing
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

- [`pme_gpu_clear_grids`](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/d0bf2c16479d98b3b2c54f3c4c27d0b62a218b78/src/gromacs/ewald/pme_gpu_internal.cpp#L528) schedules the clearing of PME grids asynchronously in the "main" PME stream;
- It is called, via `pme_gpu_reinit_computation` at the end of the step ([PME-only caller](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/d0bf2c16479d98b3b2c54f3c4c27d0b62a218b78/src/gromacs/ewald/pme_only.cpp#L778); [PP-PME caller](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/d0bf2c16479d98b3b2c54f3c4c27d0b62a218b78/src/gromacs/mdlib/sim_util.cpp#L1032));
- When pipelining is used, we launch Spread kernels in the dedicated streams, only synchronizing with coordinate readiness, but don't check that grids have completed clearing.
- This is rarely (if ever) a problem for native CUDA but causes races with Open SYCL due to caching.

## Exact steps to reproduce

See #4733.

## For developers: Why is this important?

Even on CUDA where it does not seem to happen often, we should make sure the dependencies between streams are correctly set up.

## Possible fixes

closed_issues.description:
## Summary

In SYCL, when doing charge spreading, the atom offsets are not applied. This leads to incorrect results when PME pipelining is used:

- PME is offloaded to GPU, and
- direct GPU communication is active, and
- several PP ranks are used.

This leads to incorrect results.

```console

$ cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-15 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-15  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGMX_GPU=SYCL -DGMX_SYCL_HIPSYCL=ON -DHIPSYCL_TARGETS='cuda:sm_61,sm_70' -DGMX_MPI=ON

$ GMX_FORCE_GPU_AWARE_MPI=1 GMX_ENABLE_DIRECT_GPU_COMM=1 mpirun -np 3 gmx_mpi mdrun -nb gpu -pme gpu -update gpu -npme 1  -nsteps 1000  -ntomp 8 -pin on
```

The energy drift in the output file is around 1e-1 kJ/mol/ps for a 384k water box, way higher than normal, ~1e-4 kJ/mol/ps.

Violating physics is not great.

Prefetching is always enabled in CUDA: https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/blob/f327eecc60bcc487fda0fc157011761837db7909/src/gromacs/ewald/pme_gpu_calculate_splines.cuh#L113-113

Using arbitrary charges for PME when doing FEP will produce incorrect results.

closed_issues.title: dH/dlambda output is incorrect when not coulping all lambda components the same way
closed_issues.description:
The dH/dlambda output from mdrun always report the sum of derivatives with respect to all lambda components, also when only some components are changed. One example is when the Van der Waals and Coulomb are coupled separately along the lambda path.

This likely did not affect any scientific output, as such paths are usually used with BAR and not with thermodynamic integration.

This also affects the friction metric reported by AWH (but not the actual reported free energy differences).

closed_issues.title: FindLibCpp.cmake false positive
closed_issues.description:
I was trying to build GROMACS 2023 via Spack with Fujitsu compilers on a RHEL8 system when I hit this issue.

On this system, GROMACS either requires `--stdlib=libc++` (which is not usable now, and the issue has been reported to the vendor) or a recent `libstdc++`.
I then had no choice but use the `GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH` macro and point it to a recent g++ (g++ 12.2.0 here).

TL;DR `cmake && make` works but `gmx` crashes.

What happens under the hood is that Spack sets the environment in such a way that
the sample code testing c++17 compiles as-is (!)

```
#include <filesystem>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <optional>
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  auto path = std::filesystem::current_path();
  std::optional<std::string> input(argv[0]);
  std::string_view view(input.value());
  return int(view[0])+path.string().size();
```

What went undetected is that even if `libstdc++.so` from GCC 12.2.0 is used (as expected), the program was built with the system headers (e.g. GNU 8.5.0).
And indeed, manually running the sample test results in a crash, likely because of ABI differences.

I was able to make a temporary workaround by **not** trying to compiler the sample code as-is if `GMX_CPLUSPLUS_PATH` is defined at `cmake` time.
Maybe a better option would have been to try a symbol/macro that is **not** available in GNU 8.5 (or pre C++17 compilers)

Could you please suggest the right fix for this issue?

FWIW, here is the workaround I implemented
```
diff --git a/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake b/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake
index 5a9fe1c7c9..352382c130 100644
--- a/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake
+++ b/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake
@@ -65,12 +65,18 @@ int main(int argc, char **argv) {
   std::string_view view(input.value());
   return int(view[0])+path.string().size();
 }")
-check_cxx_source_compiles("${SAMPLE_CODE_TO_TEST_CXX17}" CXX17_COMPILES)
 
-if (CXX17_COMPILES)
-    # The compiler has been set up properly to find a standard
-    # library, and if so GROMACS should leave it alone.
-    return()
+if (NOT DEFINED GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH)
+    check_cxx_source_compiles("${SAMPLE_CODE_TO_TEST_CXX17}" CXX17_COMPILES)
+
+    if (CXX17_COMPILES)
+        # The compiler has been set up properly to find a standard
+        # library, and if so GROMACS should leave it alone since
+        # no specific g++ compiler were requested.
+        return()
+    else()
+        unset(CXX17_COMPILES_CACHE)
+    endif()
 endif()
 
 # The compiler couldn't use the standard libary for an unknown reason.
@@ -180,7 +186,6 @@ endif()
 # of how it was specified or found.
 
 # Test required 2017 standard library features again.
-unset(CXX17_COMPILES CACHE)
 check_cxx_source_compiles("${SAMPLE_CODE_TO_TEST_CXX17}" CXX17_COMPILES)
 
 if (NOT CXX17_COMPILES)
```

This works just fine with `GNU` compilers, but for some reason, LLVM `libc++` chooses to throw an exception when a path does **not** exist.
This can be illustrated with the `equivalent.cpp` reproducer below:

With LLVM 15.0.7 and `libc++`

```
$ clang++ --std=c++17 --stdlib=libc++ equivalent.cpp 
$ ./a.out 
exception when comparing "/tmp" and "/there/is/no/such/path"
filesystem error: in equivalent: Operation not supported ["/tmp"] ["/there/is/no/such/path"]
```

but with `GNU 10.3.0` and `libstdc++`
```
$ g++ --std=c++17 equivalent.cpp 
$ ./a.out 
"/tmp"is not equivalent to "/there/is/no/such/path"
```

I could not decipher `std::filesystem::equivalent(...)` expected behavior from https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/filesystem/equivalent

If you believe this is a bug in LLVM `libc++`, please let me know and I will happily report it to the LLVM debuggers. Otherwise, could you please handle this `libc++` behavior?

The reproducer:
```
#include <filesystem>
#include <iostream>

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {

    auto tmp = std::filesystem::path("/tmp");
    auto nosuchpath = std::filesystem::path("/there/is/no/such/path");

    try {
        if (std::filesystem::equivalent(tmp, nosuchpath)) {
            std::cout << tmp << "is equivalent to " << nosuchpath << std::endl;
        } else {
            std::cout << tmp << "is not equivalent to " << nosuchpath << std::endl;
        }
    } catch (std::filesystem::filesystem_error const& ex) {
        std::cout << "exception when comparing " << tmp << " and " << nosuchpath << std::endl;
        std::cout << ex.what() << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}
```

closed_issues.title: AWH friction is wrong in checkpoints for dimensions > 1
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The AWH checkpoint reading/writing of the friction tensor data has always been incorrect for AWH dimensions > 1. For AWH simulations restarting from checkpoints this has resulted in incorrect friction tensors for dimensions > 1 and the corresponding friction metric volume.

This has not affected PMFs, biases or sampling. If calculating a friction, or diffusion coefficient from the friction, it would be apparent that the data is nonsensical for dimensions > 1.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Run a two-dimensional AWH simulation and restart from checkpoint. The friction metric and friction tensors will be dramatically different when analysing AWH output before compared to after the checkpoint.

## Possible fixes

A fix is on the way.

closed_issues.title: GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH ignored on reconfigure
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

When running on a system with non-standard GCC installation, setting `GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH` might be needed to help CMake find the location of the standard library. 

It sets `--gcc-toolchain` Clang flag: https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/62c6111ce2fb7b14a3ce96f1f229d6fa7f95220c/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake#L175.

However, when CMake is re-run in the same build tree (e.g., due to checking out a new branch or doing any edits to CMake files), this flag is lost.

On this second run, CMake re-uses cached check that C++17 compilation succeeded (set on the first run in https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/62c6111ce2fb7b14a3ce96f1f229d6fa7f95220c/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake#L184), and does an early return without touching either `GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH` or `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` (https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/62c6111ce2fb7b14a3ce96f1f229d6fa7f95220c/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake#L73)

## Exact steps to reproduce

Build GROMACS on a system with non-standard libstdc++ location. E.g., on LUMI. Then

```console
$ cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=${ROCM_PATH}/llvm/bin/clang \
              -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${ROCM_PATH}/llvm/bin/clang++ \
              -DGMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH=/opt/cray/pe/gcc/11.2.0/bin/g++ \
              -DGMX_FFT_LIBRARY=fftpack -DGMX_SIMD=None -DGMX_THREAD_MPI=OFF
... Succeeds
$ cmake --build . 
... Succeeds
$ touch ../../CMakeLists.txt # Force CMake reconfigure on the next build
$ cmake --build .
-- Could NOT find Python3: Found unsuitable version "3.6.15", but required is at least "3.7" (found /usr/bin/python3, found components: Interpreter)
-- Configuring done
-- Generating done
-- Build files have been written to: /users/user/gromacs/build/tmp
.....
In file included from /users/user/gromacs/src/gromacs/linearalgebra/eigensolver.cpp:39:
/users/user/gromacs/src/gromacs/utility/include/gromacs/utility/fatalerror.h:47:10: fatal error: 'filesystem' file not found
```

## For developers: Why is this important?


This can be worked around by using `-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=--gcc-toolchain=/opt/cray/pe/gcc/11.2.0/snos/` instead of `-DGMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH=/opt/cray/pe/gcc/11.2.0/bin/g++`.

So, this is not a blocker, but it makes our build system brittle and unpredictable by making `GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH` unreliable.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

1. The value of `GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH` is lost during re-configuration
2. When configured once with `GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH`, the related flags should persist on further re-configurations.

## Possible fixes

Not sure what's the best way here. Not caching `CXX17_COMPILES` is one way, but probably suboptimal. Can we cache `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`, or is it bad practice?

closed_issues.title: Intel MKL and the confusion about integer types
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

MR !2935 (e52ef39f091c11dd1b9f3607438398aad23ef596) refactored the MKL detection code. Now, by default, the `ILP64` interface is used, meaning all BLAS/LAPACK routines expect 64-bit integers for matrix sizes etc. Before that MR, `LP64` was linked, where the sizes were 32-bit.

GROMACS code, however, always passes `int` to these routines.

At least in oneAPI 2023 release, MKL's CMake machinery refuses to use LP64 libraries: `set(MKL_INTERFACE lp64)` triggers a configure error when using `icpx` as the compiler.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Install Intel oneAPI 2023, try building GROMACS 2023-rc1, observe CMake output:

```
-- Found MKL: intelmpi  
-- Found MKL: /opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/2023.0.0  
-- Found MKL: /opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/2023.0.0/lib/intel64/libmkl_sycl.so  
-- Found MKL: /opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/2023.0.0/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_ilp64.so  
-- Found MKL: /opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/2023.0.0/lib/intel64/libmkl_sequential.so  
-- Found MKL: /opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/2023.0.0/lib/intel64/libmkl_core.so
```

Read the manual on ILP64 vs LP64: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/develop/documentation/onemkl-linux-developer-guide/top/linking-your-application-with-onemkl/linking-in-detail/linking-with-interface-libraries/using-the-ilp64-interface-vs-lp64-interface.html

Read the GROMACS source code (look for `F77_FUNC` in these files):

- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/gromacs/linearalgebra/matrix.cpp
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/gromacs/linearalgebra/eigensolver.cpp

Observe that MKL functions, in this config, expect 64-bit integers, but plain `int`s are passed.

This tends to work fine, but it causes runtime error in the double-precision build of GROMACS (#4700). For some reason, it does not trigger any warnings, even though MKL declares 

```
void dsyevr_( const char* jobz, const char* range, const char* uplo,
              const MKL_INT* n, double* a, const MKL_INT* lda,
              const double* vl, const double* vu, const MKL_INT* il,
              const MKL_INT* iu, const double* abstol, MKL_INT* m, double* w,
              double* z, const MKL_INT* ldz, MKL_INT* isuppz, double* work,
              const MKL_INT* lwork, MKL_INT* iwork, const MKL_INT* liwork,
              MKL_INT* info ) NOTHROW;
```

with `MKL_INT` defined as `MKL_INT64`, and the function being declared with `extern "C"`, making overloads impossible.

## For developers: Why is this important?

When functions expect pointers to 64-bit integers, it is not polite to give them pointers to 32-bit integers.

While MKL is not our main target as CPU FFT/BLAS/LAPACK library, it is used by default in SYCL/oneAPI build.

## Possible fixes

1. Force the use of LP64-libraries, even though Intel's CMake file does not want to do it. Revering !2935 works in practice.
2. Make our code flexible enough to use 64-bit integers when `MKL_ILP64` is defined.
3. Mark MKL with ILP64 as incompatible.
4. Fix MKLConfig and bundle the patched version with GROMACS.

closed_issues.title: Nosé--Hoover documentation has several typos and is not consistent with source code
closed_issues.description:
**Summary** The description of Nosé--Hoover temperature coupling in the reference manual has several typos and unexplained variables. In addition, the equations presented in the manual are inconsistent with the implementation in the source code
**Relevant files** `src/gromacs/modularsimulator/nosehooverchains.cpp` `docs/reference-manual/algorithms/molecular-dynamics.rst`
**References** 1. M.P. Allen and D.J. Tildesley. [Computer Simulation of Liquids](https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198803195.001.0001), Chapter 3.8.2, 2nd Ed. New York: Oxford University Press, 2017.
**Use cases** Difficult to reproduce NVT calculations from other software, as the appropriate choice of Nosé--Hoover parameters (specifically, the Q masses) cannot easily be determined
**Impact** Fix requires relatively little work: simply correcting the documentation. The fix is useful in better understanding the choice of `tau-t` for the Nosé--Hoover thermostat.
**Detailed description** ***Typos*** In the "Nosé--Hoover temperature coupling" section of the reference manual, there are several missing factors of the Boltzmann constant $k$, as well as confusions between the reference temperature $T_0$ and instantaneous temperature $T$. These include: - Eq. (5.43): missing factor of $k$ on the right-hand side - Eq. (5.45): missing factor of $k$ in the numerator of the right-hand side - equations above (5.46): - missing $k$ multiplying $(T - T_0)$ in the second equation - subscript of $\xi_i$ should go from $2 \ldots M-1$ in the third equation - subscript $\xi_N$ should be $\xi_M$ in the third equation - both the third and fourth equations should have $T_0$ rather than $T$ - missing factor of $k$ in the equation below (5.47) Additional typos: - Eqs. (5.44) and (5.46) should have $\boldsymbol{p}_i \boldsymbol{\cdot} \boldsymbol{p}_i$ on the right-hand side, for the kinetic energy - the equation for $\xi$ is not given in the single-chain case, and the equation for $\xi_i$ is not given in the chained case - the quantity $Q'_k$ is not defined in Eq. (5.46) - the quantities $Q_k$ are not related to the period $\tau_T$ in the chained case, in an analogous way to Eq. (5.45) **Major inconsistency:** Given the definition of $p_{\xi_i}$ and $Q_i$ in the manual, the driving force in the last two equations above (5.46) should be $k T_0 / N_f$, **not** $k T_0$. This results from the manual's choice to scale both $p_{\xi_i}$ and $Q_i$ by a factor of $N_f$ relative to Allen and Tildesley [1]. This can easily be seen from the governing equation for $p_{\xi_1}$, and comparing it to Eq. (3.68) in Ref. [1]. According to this scaling, the definition of $Q'_k$ highlighted above would be given by $Q'_k := Q_k / N_f$. Unfortunately, however, the current implementation of the Nosé--Hoover thermostat in the source code does **not** use this additional scaling by $N_f$. This is easily seen in the `nosehooverchains.cpp` file mentioned above, in which `invXiMass` (i.e. $1/Q_k$) tells us that $$ Q_k = \frac{\tau_T^2 k T_0}{4 \pi^2} \cdot \Big( N_f, 1, 1, \ldots, 1 \Big) $$ Thus, the source code in fact uses the definition of the "bath particle" mass and momenta in Allen and Tildesley. Changing the documentation to accurately reflect the source code would simply require adding factors of $N_f$ in several location. The choice of the $Q_k$ would then be straightforward to compare with other numerical implementations of the Nosé--Hoover thermostat.

closed_issues.title: gmxapi Python package should be more conservative about when to initialize MPI.
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

`gmxapi` imports `mpi4py.MPI` (resulting in a call to `MPI_Init_thread`) more than it needs to.

Other than just being annoying, this can cause strange interference with compute resource management in conjunction with process forks during common (but surprisingly complex) tasks like simply installing the package or client packages.

`gmxapi` 0.3 is also affected.

## Exact steps to reproduce

```python
>>> import sys
>>> from gmxapi.utility import config
>>> "mpi4py" in sys.modules
True
>>> hasattr(sys.modules["mpi4py"], "MPI")
True
>>> sys.modules["mpi4py"].MPI.Is_initialized()
True
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

By default, `import mpi4py.MPI` calls `MPI_Init_thread` to initialize MPI. `gmxapi` has some module level mpi4py imports.

1. We should be more conservative about the circumstances under which `mpi4py.MPI` is imported.
2. We might want to be more conservative about automatically initializing MPI when importing `mpi4py.MPI`.
3. We probably shouldn't assume that MPI is initialized, just because we imported `mpi4py.MPI`, since the automatic behavior can be suppressed by a user or another module that is imported earlier.

See also
* https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mpi4py.html#mpi4py.mpi4py.rc.initialize
* https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mpi4py.html#mpi4py.mpi4py.rc.finalize
* https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/mpi4py.run.html#module-mpi4py.run
* https://mpi4py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/mpi4py.MPI.Is_initialized.html#mpi4py.MPI.Is_initialized

### Additional considerations

The `mpi4py.run` wrapper (e.g. `python -m mpi4py myscript.py`) makes sure that `MPI_Abort` gets called if an exception escapes unhandled from `myscript.py`. A wrapped script will see `mpi4py` in `sys.modules`, but the wrapper does not import `mpi4py.MPI` or call `MPI_Init`.

Any software component that calls `MPI_Init` should ensure that `MPI_Finalize` will be called. But we don't want a library to call `MPI_Finalize` too aggressively or prematurely. Is there a situation in which `brer-md` needs to insist on initalizing MPI (now or in the future)? If so, how should we make sure that MPI is finalized?

Note that if we inspect `"mpi4py in sys.modules`, we can see whether mpi4py has already been imported and whether there is a chance that `mpi4py.rc` was adjusted, so we can save existing values before setting `mpi4py.rc.initialize = False` and/or `mpi4py.rc.finalize = False`. But there is not necessarily a clear scope at which to restore the caller's expected behavior if our plan is to `import mpi4py.MPI`. Whatever we decide to do, we should document that we `import mpi4py.MPI` and what affect we expect to have on that module's configuration and state.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

We should not provoke libfabric to complain for things like package installation.

We should be able to perform some basic actions, like checking the installed configuration, without triggering MPI initialization.

In other cases, we might expect that gmxapi does not actually trigger MPI initialization unless work is actually being launched. We can at least try to delay initialization until MPI is actually needed rather than as modules are imported.

## Possible fixes

A series of patches eliminates MPI initialization at import.
* !3415 
* !3416 
* !3417 
* !3418

I don't think there are any barriers to upgrading from gmxapi 0.3 to 0.4, so I don't think it is necessary or appropriate to back port a fix.

See below for a possible problematic interaction---and mitigation option---with certain versions of libfabric.

## See also

https://github.com/kassonlab/brer-md/issues/47 illustrates an error from libfabric 1.11.0 on the GitHub Actions compute resources. As a workaround, the caller can force libfabric to tolerate the `fork()` with `RDMAV_FORK_SAFE=1` in libfabric < 1.13 and with `FI_EFA_FORK_SAFE=1` in more recent versions.

* For libfabric errors before the patches, see https://github.com/kassonlab/brer-md/actions/runs/3757421206/attempts/2
* For the RDMAV_FORK_SAFE workaround, see https://github.com/kassonlab/brer-md/actions/runs/3757704789
* For the mitigation provided by the above-linked merge requests, see https://github.com/kassonlab/brer-md/actions/runs/3772006950, or compare the exact same job with gmxapi 0.4.0rc1 vs. gmxapi 0.4.0rc2: https://github.com/kassonlab/brer-md/actions/runs/3757421206/jobs/6384661472 versus https://github.com/kassonlab/brer-md/actions/runs/3757421206/jobs/6412521225

```
cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGMX_GPU=SYCL -DREGRESSIONTEST_DOWNLOAD=ON -DGMX_FFT_LIBRARY=fftpack && m && m tests && SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=1 SYCL_DEVICE_FILTER=opencl:gpu GMX_TEST_REQUIRED_NUMBER_OF_DEVICES=1 m check
...

FAILED. Check checkpot.out (4 errors) file(s) in vdwalone for vdwalone
3 out of 10 freeenergy tests FAILED
```

"Ryckaert-Bell." energy is off; other terms are okay.

Works fine with: oneAPI 2022.0.2, /nethome/aland/modules/modulefiles/intel-llvm/20220414-ae284f17b-rocm5.0.2 and earlier.

Reproduces with 22.02.22151 and 22.39.24347 compute-runtimes.

Does not affect Gen12 GPUs. On `intel-gpu01` reproduces very reliably.

## For developers: Why is this important?

Slightly wrong energies are not good.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

(1) Regression tests fail

(2) Regression tests pass

**Summary**

When using ROCm's amdclang directly as a compiler, cmake-time errors prevent configuring GROMACS on HPE/Cray systems with older images (e.g. Dardel GPU); system gcc 7.5, gcc 11.2 available in the path 

**GROMACS version**

2023-beta (and release-2023 at the time of writing)

**Steps to reproduce**

```
cmake ../ -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=`which amdclang` -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=`which amdclang++` -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$FFTW_ROOT" -DGMX_CYCLE_SUBCOUNTERS=ON -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DGMX_PREFER_STATIC_LIBS=OFF -DGMX_EXTERNAL_BLAS=OFF -DGMX_EXTERNAL_LAPACK=OFF -DGMX_INSTALL_NBLIB_API=OFF -DGMXAPI=OFF -DGMX_GPU=OFF

-- Detecting C compiler ABI info - done
-- Check for working C compiler: /opt/rocm-5.0.2/bin/amdclang - skipped
-- Detecting C compile features
-- Detecting C compile features - done
-- Detecting CXX compiler ABI info
-- Detecting CXX compiler ABI info - done

  Please report to developers.
Call Stack (most recent call first):
  CMakeLists.txt:83 (find_package)

```

The above error is misleading as on this system `c++` is not in that path, working around the issue by checking the custom path:

```
diff --git a/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake b/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake
index 8c2f76baaa..5e92bc9e40 100644
--- a/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake
+++ b/cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake
@@ -148,7 +148,8 @@ if(NEED_TO_FIND_GPLUSPLUS)
         get_filename_component(GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH "${GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH}" REALPATH)
         get_filename_component(GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH "${GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH}" DIRECTORY) #strip g++
         get_filename_component(GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH "${GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH}" DIRECTORY) #strip bin
-        if (NOT EXISTS "${GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH}/include/c++")
+        if (NOT EXISTS "${GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH}/include/c++" AND
+            NOT EXISTS "${GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH}/bin/c++")
             message(FATAL_ERROR "${GMX_GPLUSPLUS_PATH}/include/c++ doesn't exist even though it should. "
                 "Please report to developers.")
         endif()
```

does not solve the issue as the compiler test still fails:
```

CMake Error at cmake/FindLibStdCpp.cmake:181 (message):
  GROMACS requires C++17, but a test of such functionality in the C++
  standard library failed to compile.  The g++ found at
  /opt/cray/pe/gcc/11.2.0 had a suitable version, so ;something else must be
  the problem

```

closed_issues.title: MPI compiler flags always used, even when building without MPI
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The flags reported by `mpicxx -showme:compile` / `mpicxx -compile-info` are used during compilation/linking, even with `GMX_MPI=OFF GMXAPI=OFF`. `MPI_CXX_LINK_FLAGS` are always added to the `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS`, and `MPI_C(XX)_COMPILE_OPTIONS` are always added to `C(XX)FLAGS`.

This can cause problems if a user has broken MPI installation even when building without MPI, as in https://gromacs.bioexcel.eu/t/error-installing-gromacs-2022-c-one-definition-rule/5322. This also affects reproducibility since compiler flags depend on seemingly irrelevant parts of the environment.

## Exact steps to reproduce

I don't want to try making a buggy MPI, so here we check that MPI-specific linker flags are used:

```console
$ module load openmpi/4.0.7 
Loading openmpi/4.0.7 with path /opt/tcbsys/openmpi/4.0.7
$ mpicxx -showme:link
-pthread -L/opt/tcbsys/openmpi/4.0.7/lib -L/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/openmpi/4.0.7/lib -Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -Wl,--enable-new-dtags -lmpi
$ cmake .. -DGMX_MPI=OFF -DGMXAPI=OFF
...
$ # Checking that there are no other sources for the flag besides MPI:
$ cmake .. -LAH | grep enable-new-dtags
MPI_CXX_LINK_FLAGS:STRING=-Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/openmpi/4.0.7/lib -Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -Wl,--enable-new-dtags -L/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -pthread
MPI_C_LINK_FLAGS:STRING=-Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/openmpi/4.0.7/lib -Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -Wl,--enable-new-dtags -L/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -pthread
$ VERBOSE=1 make 2>&1 | grep enable-new-dtags
... I won't copy-paste the whole output, but the "-Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/openmpi/4.0.7/lib -Wl,-rpath -Wl,/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -Wl,--enable-new-dtags -L/opt/tcbsys/hwloc/2.7.0/lib -pthread" flags are used when linking `libgromacs.so` and other objects.
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

We should not use extraneous compiler flags.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

1. Compiler/linker flags reported by `mpicc`/`mpicxx` are used in non-MPI build.
2. Non-MPI build should not be affected by the installed MPI.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

Affected: `v2022.4`, `v2022`, `v2022-beta1`. 

Not affected: `v2021.6`.

Not sure if worth fixing in 2022, but I think it would be nice to avoid having it in 2023.

closed_issues.title: Different results from free energy perturbation simulations when run on GPU/CPUs vs. CPU only
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

We obtain different results from free energy simulations when running Gromacs only on CPUs or on CPUs/GPU.
Specifically we used Gromacs version 2022.3, CUDA version 11.6.2 and free energy perturbation simulations using bar.
Running only on CPUs, we reproduce the correct result from the literature for the solvation free energy of a magnesium ion in water (Grotz et al. J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2021, 17, 2530-2540).
Running the exact same input files on one GPU and CPUs, the solvation free energies are 8 to 9 kJ/mol too high. 
In summary, we obtain: -1829.7 (for simulations on CPU/GPU) or -1838.5 (CPU only).
Moreover, older gromacs versions (2019.6 and 2020.7) reproduce the correct values when running on CPUs/GPUs (or only on CPUs).
The bugfix reported in https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/3164 did not resolve this issue, as we have also run these simulations with version 2022.4 and the beta release of 2023 on CPUs/GPU, but the results with GPU remain inconsistent relative to CPU only simulations.

**GROMACS version**

2022.3 and 2022.4

**Steps to reproduce**

The input files for reproduction of these results are included in the attached zip file: [FEPInput.zip](/uploads/2c4cc8df3e7cc5b03d385b799d9a2a26/FEPInput.zip). The required simulations can be run by executing the included bash script and also the analysis with the BAR method is performed.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

The values for DG reported at the end of the file bar.log deviate between simulations run on CPUs only and on GPU/CPUs.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

That the values for DG deviate by not more than some statistical uncertainty, i.e. by less than 1 kJ/mol.

**Possible fixes**

No suggestions.

closed_issues.title: Changing an atom type at lambda = 1 affects the computed energies at lambda = 0
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Changing a single atom type at the lambda = 1 endpoint affects the short-range electrostatics at lambda = 0 using GROMACS 2022.4 (it shouldn't).

## Exact steps to reproduce

Using the two folders in [these input files](/uploads/e8704e0e5587a4bec0ed910b0bf1d47d/Archive.zip), one obtains different potential energies for the short-range electrostatics (using `gmx energy -f gromacs.edr`):

input0: 13.0602 kJ/mol

input1: 13.0313 kJ/mol

The *only* difference between the two inputs is a single line in the topology file. For input0 this is:

`7      C2      1     LIG   C7x      7  -0.054060    12.010780      C2  -0.054060    12.010780`

And for input1 this is:

`7      C2      1     LIG   C7x      7  -0.054060    12.010780   C2_du  -0.054060    12.010780`

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

Since both MDP files have this section:

```
fep-lambdas          = 0.00000 0.00000
coulomb-lambdas          = 0.00000 1.00000
init-lambda-state = 0
```

The energies should not be affected because of this change, because 1. changing the atom type should not affect the electrostatics and 2. changing something at lambda = 1 should not affect the energies at lambda = 0.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

All attached. This was run on macOS.

## Possible fixes

This seems to be related to an issue that was fixed in 2022.4. I would be interested in learning how to circumvent it if possible.

closed_issues.title: More elaborate adjustments for test timeouts
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Currently, we build gromacs on all archs but x86(_64) without SIMD. This apparently causes some test to exceed its timeout.

We see errors like:  
`[ 1978s] 	 64 - MdrunTestsTwoRanks (Timeout)`  
or near misses like:  
`[  790s] 5/5 Test #64: MdrunTestsTwoRanks .............................   Passed   78.30 sec`

## Exact steps to reproduce

Build gromacs without SIMD/GPU support, run on a fairly slow host.

## Possible fixes

Timeouts are defined in
https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/testutils/TestMacros.cmake

1. Allow to set a different timeout baseline, instead of 30 seconds:  
   https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/testutils/TestMacros.cmake#L265
2. Set other timeouts as a multiple of the base value, e.g.  
   `math(EXPR _timeout "4 * ${_timeout}")`  
   https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/math.html
3. Add an additional timeout for non-SIMD cases (e.g. multiply by 2).

cmake -DGMX_MPI=OFF -DGMX_THREAD_MPI=ON -CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
make && make tests
ctest --exclude-regex 'physicalvalidationtests|regression' --tests-regex Rank --parallel 8
```

**What is the current bug behavior?**

Tests which are run with 1 MPI rank and 2 MPI ranks use the same temporary files. Typically one of the two will fail if run concurrently.

Tests can be executed in parallel. Running tests in parallel results in a significant speedup.

- Make temporary file names / directories dependent on MPI rank
- Add a lock file

One workaround is to add '2Rank|TwoRanks' to the `--exclude-regex`, and run these separately.

closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

RDF's produced by the gmx rdf function have a small error in r. This error probably affects all RDF calculations. We found this when simulating a box of water. We tried with the gmx rdf in both gromacs 2022.2 and 2019.6. We find the problem when comparing the RDFs with that produced by the python module mdtraj. We also verified with the RDF function of VMD

**GROMACS version**
```
c1330:rjweldon:~$ gmx --quiet --version

                         :-) GROMACS - gmx, 2022.2 (-:


Executable:   /home/rjweldon/Software/Gromacs/binaries/bin/gmx

  gmx --quiet --version

GPU support:        disabled

SIMD instructions:  AVX_512

CPU FFT library:    fftw-3.3.3-sse2

GPU FFT library:    none

RDTSCP usage:       enabled

TNG support:        enabled

Hwloc support:      disabled

Tracing support:    disabled

C compiler:         /opt/rh/devtoolset-11/root/usr/bin/cc GNU 11.2.1

C compiler flags:   -mavx512f -mfma -mavx512vl -mavx512dq -mavx512bw -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -O3 -DNDEBUG

C++ compiler:       /opt/rh/devtoolset-11/root/usr/bin/c++ GNU 11.2.1

C++ compiler flags: -mavx512f -mfma -mavx512vl -mavx512dq -mavx512bw -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -fopenmp -O3 -DNDEBUG
```



**Steps to reproduce**

```
gmx rdf -f traj.trr -s topol.tpr -n index.ndx -ref O -sel H -bin 0.00001 -o OH_RDF
```
The r from the command above is shifted to be approximately 0.0005 nm longer than the correct values. The shift is insensitive to choices of bin sizes.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

gmx rdf produces an RDF file with r values shifted up by approximately 0.0005 nm.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

We expected the RDF to match that produced by VMD and MDTraj. This won’t cause major problems but it leads to appreciable error when we try to read the intramolecular OH bond length from the RDF for one of our projects.

**Possible fixes**

None at the moment.

closed_issues.title: std::filesystem::path::c_str broke MSVC
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Switch from `gmx::Path` to `std::filesystem`, done in !2885, broke Visual Studio build.

From [CppReference](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/filesystem/path/native):

> `std::filesystem::path::c_str`, `std::filesystem::path::native`, `std::filesystem::path::operator string_type()`

> Return value: The native string representation of the pathname, using native syntax, native character type, and native character encoding. This string is suitable for use with OS APIs. 

In GROMACS, we were assuming that `c_str()` always returns `char*`, but that's not the case on Windows.

## Discussion

- [Dmitry Morozov @aracsmd](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/3136#note_1112527648):

> Whenever `std::filesystem::path` is converted to string we need to explicitly convert it, i.e. using `.string()` method. Reason is that implicit conversion on Windows fails because native strings in Windows are `std::wstring`

> OK got it. I just went yesterday through the whole MSVC fixing process in order to debug "small" problem of Pavel's code


- [Roland Schulz @rolandschulz](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/3136#note_1112964898):

> I believe it is incorrect to call `path.string()` or `path.c_str()` in GROMACS. Currently GROMACS assumes that all strings (both `std::string` and `char*`) are UTF8. Therefore we should always call `path.u8string()` or `path.u8string().c_str()`. Calling the wrong one won't give a warning and won't show a problem on Unix. Meaning we likely will get it often wrong. Microsoft said they would accept a PR to add a warning but so far no one has created one ([STL issue](https://github.com/microsoft/STL/issues/909)). It might be better if we use `u8path` instead of `path` everywhere. Even if it is deprecated in C++20 ([stackoverflow "Why is std::filesystem::u8path deprecated"](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54004000/why-is-stdfilesystemu8path-deprecated-in-c20)). We would still not get a compiler warning if someone accidentally used `path` instead of `u8path` somewhere.

> Actually I think it seems less error-prone than I initially thought. If we use implicit conversion of `string`/`char*` to filepath it is OK because Windows uses the default code-page and we set that to utf8 so this should give the correct results. And accidentally using `path.string` or `path.c_str` shouldn't be possible because the return type is `wstring`/`w_char*` (on Windows) and therefore won't compile if passed to `string`/`char*`. Therefore I don't think we need to worry about accidentally using utf16 in places we don't intend to.

> And for Windows only code (low level file handling) we might as well switch to \*W functions so that string don't need to be converted twice.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Look at the recent job status in https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/actions, or try to build locally using Visual Studio (tested with 2022).

## For developers: Why is this important?

We want to be portable and standard-compliant.

## Possible fixes

Paul started in !3120, but it seems more fixes are needed. Dmitry says he already went through fixing things, though.

N/A

closed_issues.title: Wrong Relative Free Energy on GPU
closed_issues.description:
## Summary
Simulation of the Relative Free Energy on GPUs (using gmx 2020-2022.3) gives dramatically different results between BAR and TI (Thermodynamic Integration) methods. The problem is observed in all tested mutations even in the simplest 1-atom mutation of Acetone->Acetamide in Water with PME:

| Device |      dG(BAR)      |         dG(TI)       |
| ------ | ----------------- |----------------------|
|  GPU   | -173.70 +/-  0.12 | -181.7074 +/- 0.1501 |                 
|  CPU   | -181.42 +/-  0.10 | -181.5248 +/- 0.1512 |

As you can see the BAR results disagree between GPU and cpu computations while TI results are in the perfect agreement.

This is important issue to fix asap since all FEP computations on computationally efficient GPUs with the default method BAR are incorrect.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Please, find attached input/output files for the test example of Acetone->Acetamide mutation in Water.

## Possible fixes

Since TI integral of dhdl values is correct (dG by TI method) the dhdl values are computed correctly.
The problem seems to be in the BAR cross energy term computation or output to dhdl.xvg files. I suggest debug using -rerun option on the same trajectory, e.g. for Lam=0, and compare cross energy terms between cpu and GPU runs.

**Summary**

Expanded ensemble simulations performed by GROMACS 2022.3 (including the thread-MPI and MPI-enabled versions) seem to easily fail with a segmentation fault in a few ns of simulations. This situation did not happen with previous GROMACS versions. Specifically, using GROMACS 2021.4, I was able to run several expanded ensemble simulations for hundreds of ns using exactly the same set of input GRO/TOP/MDP files without having any error, but several trials that I performed using GROMACS 2022.3 all failed with a segmentation error. 

**GROMACS version**

**Steps to reproduce**

Here I have attached a compressed folder `issue` ([issue.zip](/uploads/8f7cfd272bf0a50da43bbfc3701e64ea/issue.zip)), which contains two subfolders `inputs` and `outputs`. The subfolder `inputs` contains the input TPR file and the corresponding GRO, TOP and MDP files. The file `mdout.mdp` shows the adopted values of all MD parameters and the command I used to generate the TPR file. The subfolder `outputs` contains the LOG files and the SLURM outputs of two trials respectively performed with the thread-MPI and MPI-enabled versions of GROMACS 2022.3. closed_issues.title: Question on gmx dump for VSITE3FAD parameters
closed_issues.description:
I am running GROMACS 2022.2 with CHARM36ff.

When I ran `gmx dump -s ProtE1_V1.tpr -param` to get the virtual site parameters I was expecting for the VSITE3FAD parameters to see value for angle `theta` and length vector `d` but instead I only see an `a` or `b` parameter.  Looking at the [notes in the code](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/gromacs/mdlib/vsite.cpp#L534) it's obvious these are the transformed values `a = d * cos(theta)` and `b = d * sin(theta)`.  

There are a few interesting things I noted.  For my `vsite3fad` atoms created in the itp topology from `pdb2gmx` I realized that none of these `ai    aj    ak    al` atoms are actual a virtual site.  They are all `H* - N - C - C` atoms for c-c-nh2 groups but from figure 34 below and the code notes [here](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/gromacs/gmxpreprocess/vsite_parm.cpp#L521) it seems that `ai` should be a virtual site atom (grey atom) and then you have your three actual atoms.  I am pretty new to virtual sites so the hydrogen atoms may very well be the grey virtual site atom.

However when I run `gmx dump` I only see a=-5.00000007e-02 and b= 8.66025388e-02 or b=-8.66025388e-02.  I calculated distance between H-N bond which should be vector `d` according to image and it's usually around 1 ang or 0.1 nm which is good.  But when I run inverse calculations

```
arccos(a/0.1) = 2.09439511048
arccos(abs(b)/0.1) = 1.03515470454 = pi - arccos(a/0.1)
```

Is this the intent to have two thetas to add up to pi?  And based on notes in code `cos(theta) = a/d` and `sin(theta) = b/d` what hypotenuse is `d` representing in figure 34?

![image](/uploads/dbab1a582021c477c53ee86495c2f22a/image.png)

Fig. 34 The six different types of virtual site construction in . The constructing atoms are shown as black circles, the virtual sites in gray.

![image](/uploads/297ff15ff33b140922a44503b3651d84/image.png)

Follow up question would be if I want to write the `cO` and `c1` parameters in my itp file, for `vsite3fad` atoms would I enter values for `a` and `b` from gmx dump or should I be using the theta and length d and if so which theta value based on my post above.

closed_issues.title: hipSYCL+vkFFT: linking the right CUDA libraries
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

With CUDA, using vkFFT requires linking the binary to some CUDA libraries.

Since hipSYCL/CUDA/vkFFT is not supposed to be widely used by the end users, we decided in !3156 to use the simplest way possible, even if it is not the most robust.

But there might be cases where the version of CUDA picked up there differs from the one used by hipSYCL runtime. Things might get funky.

We shall either parse the hipSYCL's config (which still does not protect us from runtime weirdness but at least makes things more robust in compile time) or somehow convince the build system to defer the linking and use whatever symbols get loaded by hipSYCL in runtime.
