closed_issues.title: Incorrect output of dH to other lambdas in GROMACS 2022 on GPU.
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Inconsistent BAR results are observed from GROMACS2021.3 and GROMACS2022.3 with the same simulation setup to calculate relative hydration free energy between two molecules.

**GROMACS version**

v2022.3

**Steps to reproduce**

Please download the attachment first.

[reproduce.tar.gz](/uploads/6f63541157d7d83b7a9c0d08e1e9adbb/reproduce.tar.gz)

Next, execute comands as below.
```bash
# Supposing we have 2 Gromacs versions installed in `/path/to/gmx2021` and `/path/to/gmx2021` respectively.
OLD_PATH=$PATH

PATH=/path/to/gmx2021:${OLD_PATH}
version=gmx21
tar zxf reproduce.tar.gz
for device in cpu gpu; do
    cd $device/$version
    sh run.sh
    cd ../..
done

PATH=/path/to/gmx2022:${OLD_PATH}
version=gmx22
tar zxf reproduce.tar.gz
for device in cpu gpu; do
    cd $device/$version
    sh run.sh
    cd ../..
done
```

Now, check values of `\xD\f{}H \xl\f{} to (0.6000, 1.0000)` in files as below:
```text
./gpu/gmx22/2/gmx22_rerun_gpu/dhdl.xvg
./gpu/gmx22/2/gmx21_rerun_gpu/dhdl.xvg
./gpu/gmx22/2/md.xvg
./gpu/gmx22/2/gmx21_rerun_cpu/dhdl.xvg
./gpu/gmx22/2/gmx22_rerun_cpu/dhdl.xvg
```

**What is the current bug behavior?**

Inconsistent BAR results are observed from GROMACS2021.3 and GROMACS2022.3 with the same simulation setup to calculate relative hydration free energy between two molecules, toluene and benzene, for example. The inconsistency comes from the intermediate steps of changing the partial charges from toluene to benzene. Below shows the comparison of dG calculated by gmx bar for two neighboring lambda windows in the intermediate steps, values in kJ/mol.
| Device | GROMACS2021.3 BAR (2 x 1 ns) | GROMACS2022.3 BAR (2 x 1 ns) |
| ------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
|    GPU |                         3.92 |                         1.42 |
|    CPU |                         3.92 |                         3.92 |

Interestingly, the results calculated by TI are all in agreement, which indicates there maybe something wrong with the dH output from GROMACS2022.3 running on GPU. Further comparing the dH output from GROMACS2022.3(GPU) with the dH outputs from rerun using the trajectory produced by GROMACS2022.3(GPU):

*Comparing the values of column s4 legend "\xD\f{}H \xl\f{} to (0.6000, 1.0000)"*
| Time (ps) | GROMACS2022.3(GPU) | GROMACS2022.3(GPU) rerun | GROMACS2022.3(CPU) rerun | GROMACS2021.3(GPU) rerun | GROMACS2021.3(CPU) rerun |
| --------- | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------ |
|    0.0000 |          1.5620121 |                1.5620243 |                4.0245035 |                4.0243885 |                4.0244259 |
|   10.0000 |          1.5159204 |                1.5159204 |                4.0204750 |                4.0204754 |                4.0204723 |
|   20.0000 |          1.1021023 |                1.1021084 |                3.6126774 |                3.6126739 |                3.6127457 |
|   30.0000 |          1.0576748 |                1.0576931 |                3.5818871 |                3.5818819 |                3.5818789 |

To clarify, dH values from GROMACS2022.3(GPU) are different to the dH values produced by rerun on the same trajectory using GROMACS2022.3(CPU) and GROMACS2021.3.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

BAR result of Gromacs-2022.3 GPU is consistent with that of other devices or versions.

**Possible fixes**

None.

closed_issues.title: Performance report on Apple-designed GPUs
closed_issues.description:
Even with GPU-accelerated PME enabled, the GPU is never more than 1.9x as fast as using only the CPU. I ran all the benchmarks from [grubmueller/bench](https://www.mpinat.mpg.de/grubmueller/bench). For benchMEM/benchRIB/benchPEP, this is the speedup:

- benchMEM (80,000 atoms): 1.2x
- benchRIB (2,000,0000 atoms): 1.75x
- benchPEP (12,000,000 atoms): 1.9x

I'll put the benchmarks in a comment below, but I hope this explanation can help you understand the performance patterns of Apple GPUs. How does this compare to the GPUs you regularly test?

Unlike CUDA, Metal has severe driver overhead when encoding GPU commands. Unless you use the API just right with native API calls, it's often slower than CPU. This is because after each command buffer, it flushes the command stream. It's like using OpenCL, but after every `clEnqueueKernel`, you call `clFlush`. Apple's OpenCL driver probably flushes excessively behind the scenes. When accessing Metal directly through hipSYCL, we could avoid that flushing.

Another issue - even though the CPU and GPU share memory, the overhead for CPU <-> GPU communication is severe. It takes 200 microseconds to launch a kernel, wait, and safely read its results on the CPU. It's so slow that you might as well be using a discrete GPU. However, there are some advantages. The GPU has access to virtual memory, where you can allocate more memory than physically exists in RAM. As long as one single allocation doesn't exceed RAM size, the driver can page allocations to and from disk before executing GPU commands. This means my M1 Max has 32 GB of physical memory, but 1 TB of actual theoretical memory (SSD disk size).

Next - an overview of the Apple GPU architecture. Each GPU has many "cores", analogous to "compute units" on other GPUs. The A14 has 4 cores, while the M1 Max has 32. Each core can run work from 256 threads at any given moment, but stores register files and shared memory for 3072 threads. This is an extremely excessive ratio (12x), while AMD GCN has 3.2x. Apple does this to maximize ALU utilization, improving performance/watt at a steep transistor cost. This could explain why Apple has such low maximum shared memory (32 KB) compared to GCN (64 KB). Given the same budget of shared memory per core, they have more threads, but less shared memory per thread.

The GPU "core" has 550-600 KB of register file. Allocating up to 192 bytes of register/thread, it can run up to 3072 threads. Afterwards, occupancy decreases to 1152 threads (37.5%) at 512 bytes/thread. AMD has the same maximum number of registers/thread, so anything that doesn't cause a register spill on RDNA2, won't on M1 either. However, the saturation of ALUs at that maximum is different. At 37.5% occupancy, Apple is still overutilizing ALUs (1152/256 = 450%), while GCN not so much (768/640 = 120%). Thus, Apple achieves incredible power efficiency even with maxed-out register allocation.

Regarding ALU/FLOPS performance, each core runs 256 threads simultaneously in workgroups of up to 1024 threads. These are subdivided into 32-wide waves, which can perform simd-wide reductions just like Intel's subgroup operations for OpenCL. These are only accessible through Metal, not Apple's OpenCL driver. Each wave can also perform two out-of-order, superscalar 16-bit operations. The best analogy is to Fugaku: has 1024-bit vectors, which are two 512-bit vectors behind the scenes. This is also restricted to Metal shaders, and not available from OpenCL.

That's all I will say about architectural performance for now; I might not post the full benchmarks for a few hours. I hope this report wasn't excessively long, and provided useful insight into what we can expect from Metal via hipSYCL.

> Edit: Apple has extremely slow threadgroup memory, around 2.5x slower than other vendors. This design reduces static power consumption, based on advice from the maintainer of VkFFT. The fact also explains why generic matrix multiplication kernels reach 25% theoretical FLOPS on Apple, but 50% on AMD. Apple added a `simdgroup_matrix` instruction to bypass the slow threadgroup memory on A14, reaching 75-80% theoretical TFLOPS (100% ALU utilization based on FMA cycle counts).

<!--
> Edit 2: With the M2 architecture, Apple may have doubled the number of ALUs per compute unit, while halving the clock speed. This would increase each GPU "core" from 256 to 512 active threads. To pull this off without doubling the transistors, Apple would halve the inactive:active threads ratio from 12.0 to 6.0. That would counteract their extensive efforts to improve power efficiency, unless they modestly enlarged the register file. Alternatively, Apple could have done the same thing as AMD with RDNA3: each GPU thread has double-throughput out-of-order execution. This would not change the number of active threads or require more SRAM.
>
> Finally, Apple's developer video about A15 could have been misleading. Wikipedia statistics say ALUs doubled from A13 to A14. Perhaps Apple could have meant ALUs doubled from A13 to A15, not from A14 to A15. Then, M2 would improve performance by slightly increasing clock speed. This is offset by a slightly more power-efficient semiconductor node, TSMC N5P, creating equivalent power consumption.
> 
> M2 clock speed is 1398 MHz: https://github.com/tlkh/asitop/issues/47
-->

closed_issues.title: Linking error with muParser on Fedora
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

When building GROMACS with externally linked muParser, builds fail due to linker errors. Example reported by the Fedora project, build here: https://koji.fedoraproject.org/koji/taskinfo?taskID=92400080

**GROMACS version**

Failed build was with 2022.3, but likely affects all versions that allow linking to external muParser.

**Steps to reproduce**

Try building GROMACS against muParser with release version 2.3.3 on Fedora. Set following in addition to regular commands on CMake command line: `-DGMX_USE_MUPARSER=EXTERNAL`

**What is the current bug behavior?**

GROMACS build fails in the linking stage due to undefined symbols. I confirmed that there are no changes of the muParser API, so this is only due to failure to link properly.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Either we shouldn't accept the external library, or we should be able to build with it.

**Possible fixes**

Fix linking flags in CMake.

closed_issues.title: Warn about invalid CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE value
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Currently, CMake gladly accepts any value passed via `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=`.

The only indication that something is wrong is an easy-to-miss compile-time warning like

```
In file included from /tmp/gromacs/src/gromacs/mdlib/lincs.cpp:45:
/tmp/gromacs/build/tmp/src/include/config.h:269:26: warning: "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE_RELEASEWITHASSERT" is not defined, evaluates to 0 [-Wundef]
  269 | #define CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE_RELEASEWITHASSERT
      |                          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
/tmp/gromacs/build/tmp/src/include/config.h:269:26: note: in definition of macro ‘CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE’
  269 | #define CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE_RELEASEWITHASSERT
```

However, as a result, any checks for the value of `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` macro in the code return `false`. CMake does string comparison, so it might work partially.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Try to compiler GROMACS with  `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithAsserts` or `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=ReleaseWithAssert` (the correct one should be `RelWithAssert`). Observe that the code compiles with warnings.

## For developers: Why is this important?

Easy to make and easy to miss error that makes the code behave in a slightly wrong way. Not good.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

(1) The code compiles

(2) Fatal error at configure time

closed_issues.title: gmxapi 0.4b1 misbehaves when `mpi4py` is not available at CMake configure time.
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

A linking error and unhelpful error messages result if `mpi4py` is not discoverable when the gmxapi Python package is configured.

Work is in progress to rely less heavily on `mpi4py` for a full resolution of #4422, but these bugs should be fixed in the mean time.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Option 1: Build and test GROMACS with `-DGMX_PYTHON_PACKAGE=ON` in a Python environment without the `mpi4py` package available.

Option 2: `pip install --extra-index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --pre "gmxapi==0.4.0b1"`

Option 3: ref https://github.com/kassonlab/run_brer/actions/runs/3098807457/jobs/5017168536 and https://github.com/kassonlab/run_brer/actions/runs/3099189669/jobs/5018029327

## For developers: Why is this important?

#4422 is a long-awaited feature, and we should have as complete a solution as possible going into the beta release so that we can get the most thorough possible feedback. Even if caveats or unsupported edge cases exist, the results should be comprehensible to users.

The first part of this issue is a simple bug from a rebasing oversight, and easily remedied.

@eirrgang will provide all technical contributions for the solutions.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

`mpi4py` is not strictly required.
* Valid software builds should occur with or without `mpi4py` installed
* The software is intended to detect `mpi4py` availability and to provide helpful output when attempting to perform the subset of operations that require `mpi4py`.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

Linking error: `ImportError: /home/runner/venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/gmxapi/_gmxapi.cpython-39-x86_64-linux-gnu.so: undefined symbol: _ZN5gmxpy6detail19export_mpi_bindingsERN8pybind117module_ERKNS1_9exceptionINS_9ExceptionEEE`

Unhelpful error: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'Get_size'`

closed_issues.title: The deform option is not suited for shear flow
closed_issues.description:
The deform option in mdrun gives and constant velocity to box vectors and scales coordinates at each step to follow the box deformation. This works acceptably in case the goal is to see some disruption after slow deformation.
However for a shear flow setup the following is needed
* no coordinate scaling
* correction of the particle velocities of atoms when they are reset along periodic vectors
* substract the flow profile when computing the kinetic energy; problematic as a reference location is needed
* grompp should have the option to initialize the flow given given the deform matrix

This setup should also work fine for the "disruption" case, so we should do this by default.

closed_issues.title: Incorrect handling of -gputasks when running PP and PME on the same rank
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The `-gputasks` flag of `mdrun` allows specifying the GPU to use for each GPU task. However, GROMACS only supports one GPU per rank. This results in the reported (and requested) task assignment being different from the one actually used when both PP and PME tasks are executed on the same rank.

The issue was uncovered when using a single rank. With PME decomposition, it might also manifest with multiple ranks.

Reported by @rolandschulz.

## Exact steps to reproduce

```console
$ gmx  mdrun -ntmpi 1 -nb gpu -pme gpu -gputasks 01 -nsteps -1
          :-) GROMACS - gmx mdrun, 2022.4-dev-20220914-4ebda133b7 (-:
[....]
2 GPUs selected for this run.
Mapping of GPU IDs to the 2 GPU tasks in the 1 rank on this node:
  PP:0,PME:1
```

But in fact, only GPU #0 is used.

## For developers: Why is this important?

We should not lie in our log file and silently disregards user's explicit requests.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

1. GROMACS reports that it runs PP and PME on different GPUs, but runs them on the same device.

2. Both GPUs are being used or an error message saying this is impossible.

closed_issues.title: gmx solvate segfaults in releases after series 5.1 for particular solvents (hexanes, methanol, etc.)
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

I appear to have encountered a bug in recent releases on Gromacs that was not present in previous releases. When attempting to solvate a small molecule with certain organic solvents whose pdb structures and topologies have been published on virtualchemistry.org and described in https://doi.org/10.1021/ct200731v, the command gmx solvate will segmentation fault. While gmx solvate will work for most of these solvents that have been tested, a few will consistently segmentation fault, such as hexanes and methanol. This is only observed in recent releases including 2016.3, 2018, 2021.3, and the latest available container version (2022.2). No error arises when using an older version such as 5.1.2. We have also noticed that the errors in the latest versions do not happen when using the double-precision version, gmx_d solvate.

**GROMACS version**

Segmentation fault occurs in GROMACS versions 2016.3, 2018, 2021.3, and 2022.2. It does not occur in GROMACS version 5.1.2.

**Steps to reproduce**

The attached files should enable reproduction of the bug. A sample small molecule structure is given in CPD.gro. A structure file for hexane, one of the problematic solvents, is given as a PDB file. The submit.sh file provides the gmx solvate command used to try and solvate the small molecule with hexane. Three output files are also provided: the full output when running the command on version 2021.3, the command line output from the 2022 container version, and the output from version 5.1.2 where the solvation worked without error.
[2021_output.txt](/uploads/4ba656e38b1f5ea8dc1415041d919a37/2021_output.txt)

[2022_container_output.txt](/uploads/a6d33e8a7e4c61e09e64b06536f4a975/2022_container_output.txt)

[CPD.gro](/uploads/72dd9796a27047fb8e2bccf01036399b/CPD.gro)

[HEX.pdb](/uploads/a062fd7e8f1f498f9abb89486bf15a67/HEX.pdb)

[submit.sh](/uploads/feec349a8a8b206408114eec78de0786/submit.sh)

[v5_success_output.txt](/uploads/d887a1bd7b7ed8fe1b7bb9aa712eaace/v5_success_output.txt)

**What is the current bug behavior?**

The solvation does not finish, but gives a segmentation fault for particular solvents. However, running the commands with 
double-precision (gmx_d solvate -cp CPD.gro -cs HEX.pdb -o CPD_HEX.gro) does appear to work in the recent releases.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Simply running the command gmx solvate -cp CPD.gro -cs HEX.pdb -o CPD_HEX.gro should work as is, generating a solvated gro structure file of small molecule CPD in hexanes. No segmentation fault should occur. This is seen for the earlier release Gromacs 5.1.2. Please see the attached output files.

**Possible fixes**

Our cluster support specialists have determined, by looking at the core dump, that it does appear to be an internal software issue. Something has changed since the 5.1.2 release that no longer allows gmx solvate to work with these solvents, except with double-precision.

closed_issues.title: Document the caveats for new behavior under CMake policy 104.
closed_issues.description:
Follow-up from "Enable CUDA language in CMAKE"

The following discussion from !2994 should be addressed:

- [ ] @eirrgang started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2994#note_1098482998): 

    > Was there any discussion on how to mitigate the `NEW` behavior? Since !3057 proposes to require CMake > 3.18.0, is the new behavior something we can/should address sooner than later?
    > 
    > In any case, could someone offer a comment or a link to a conversation about what is needed before we can change this to `cmake_policy(SET CMP0104 NEW)`?


[CMP0104](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/policy/CMP0104.html) `NEW` behavior requires that [CUDA_ARCHITECTURES](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_tgt/CUDA_ARCHITECTURES.html) is set explicitly. (An explicit `OFF` counts as "set" to disable automatic flag generation.)

Note that special values `all` and `all-major` become available in CMake 3.23. Special value `native` becomes available in CMake 3.24.

Does one of the special values of `all`, `all-major`, or `native` suit our preferred default behavior?

If so, we could set CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES to the appropriate value (if it has not been set by the user) and set `cmake_policy(SET CMP0104 NEW)`, conditional on the CMake version. Then it will be obvious when we can standardize on the `NEW` behavior as our CMake requirements are updated.

closed_issues.title: Gromacs on FPGAs using SYCL
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Examine whether one can do effective molecular dynamics on FPGAS and whether maintenance of a single codebase that runs on FPGAs, GPUs and CPUs is feasible.

**Use cases**

FPGAs have very fast local memory and can allow for faster mathematical operations so users will see faster time to solution for long running simulations.  FPGA clusters can also use custom networks, allowing for improved strong scalability.

**Impact**

Previous work has examined performance of FPGAs for the Amber molecular dynamics code, finding performance that is competitive with a single GPU.  Specialized computers such as Anton can also give significant time to solution improvements, however they are more costly to develop and not easily reconfigurable.  An efficient FPGA based version of GROMACS can be a tool for better discovery for molecular simulations.
(For whom will this matter? Is it likely to have large impact relative to the amount of work required? If you are a developer, is this something you expect to prioritize higher than the (many) other things that could be done to the code? Will it simplify/remove code, rather than add more code? Avoid adding very general nice-to-have features unless you are planning to work on it yourself in the immediate timeframe.)

**Detailed description**

This is initial exploratory work. The aim is to examine kernels and understand communication patterns used by GROMACS. Thus, changes to the GROMACS code should not be required, but feedback from users and developers would be helpful. The initial aim is to develop a toy molecular dynamics code in SYCL that is useful for explaining how molecular dynamics simulations work and examining performance on different hardware architectures.  The code can also be useful for scientists who want to learn about programming and programmers who want to learn about molecular dynamics.

closed_issues.title: Improve Kernel Performance on AMD GPUs
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The hipSYCL port with a ROCm backend currently underperforms compared to AMD's HIP port due to larger kernel runtimes. There might be opportunities to improve the SYCL code to AMD GPUs based on the work we have put on the AMD HIP port. 

## Use cases

Faster Gromacs available on AMD GPUs!

## Impact

The aim here is to improve GROMACS performance for RDNA/CDNA AMD GPU for the user community. 

## Detailed Description

The HIP port is currently unsupported by the Gromacs development team. The way to currently target AMD GPUs is to get the SYCL code compiled with hipSYCL and a ROCm backend. 
However by doing so, we did detect that the kernels underperform compared to the HIP code. 

Here's what we need to do in order to bring performance up:

- [x] Include support for vkFFT as an alternative for hip/rocFFT (WIP: [\#2867](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2867))
- [x] Improve Spread and Gather kernels for PME (addressed by [\#2988] - no performance delta compared to HIP)(https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2988) )
- [ ] Incorporate HIP optimizations for the Nonbonded Kernel into SYCL
- [ ] Testing / Optimizing listed forces (WIP: [\#3928](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/3928))
- [ ] Improving hipSYCL runtime inefficiens and diagnose hangings on API calls
- [ ] make sure to use compiler flags known to be beneficial (note that as hipSYCL targets both CUDA and HIP backends those specific to either need to be passed somehow, e.g. `-Xarch_device` or hipSYCL env var)

There has been a lot of recent improvements into the NB kernel on the HIP port currently. I see a performance delta of 32% on HIP vs SYCL on AMD GPUs for larger benchmarks (STMV) on MI200s, so there is a lot of room for improvement there. Most kernels underperform compared to the native HIP code, but I think it's good to focus on the main guy first.
 
Since the HIP NB kernel is based on the CUDA version, I am not sure if we can incorporate some of the improvements directly on Gromacs itself or if they should be done on the hipSYCL level.
@sbalint98 this is based on the plan you guys sent me a couple days ago. Let's coordinate work here so it is also visible to the Gromacs team.
Suggestions / improvements are appreciated!

closed_issues.description:
## Summary

We want to set `-ffast-math` and other optimization flags for hipSYCL builds.

Unfortunately, hipSYCL's CMake works via compiler launcher mechanics, which is per-target; thus, the flags can only be applied to all the files in `libgromacs`. This causes multiple test failures since we want to use accurate, NaN/inf-aware math in some cases in the host code.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Checkout 4fb03de6d28a766b38bf7393bcaecdcd381aead6 (!2975), build with hipSYCL and clang-14, observe failures of `./bin/math-test`, `./bin/trajectoryanalysis-test`, and `./bin/selection-test`. Log attached: [job.log](/uploads/cc509c1a839d7723e1205fddbdef9bb7/job.log).

Note: some cases above, especially 0 vs. 1.33 and the like, make me think that our host code can be made more robust.

## For developers: Why is this important?

We want to use `-ffast-math` and other flags for the device code without applying them to the host code.

## Possible fixes

As discussed in !2975 and email:

- Perhaps adding `#pragma clang fp contract(fast) reassociate(on)` to the kernel lambda might help with performance instead of `-ffast-math`. Or keeping `-ffast-math` adding the opposite pragmas to the fragile bits of the host code. Have not tested it, though.

- One way would be to have an extra cmake target for all source files actually needing SYCL. This could be a static or shared library, although in the static library case you would make sure that it gets linked correctly.

- Submit a PR fixing hipSYCL's CMake machinery.

closed_issues.title: Avoid halo exchange of forces
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

When running with domain decomposition, GROMACS breaks the NB PP work into local and non-local work. The local work requires only the positions of particles "home" to the domain, ie. consists of NB work for particles sufficiently inside the domain boundaries. The non-local work requires the positions of particles "home" to adjacent domains, so does halo exchange of positions near the start of the force calculation. Each domain is responsible for computing interactions whose midpoints are within its boundaries, which keeps the overall workload balanced and minimizes the number of messages needed, while requiring a halo exchange of forces before the domains can reduce the total forces needed for update+constraints on their home particles.

In domain decomposition, it is generally desirable to overlap the communication with computation. This can be done by ensuring that the local work starts before the position halo exchange, and that the non-local work completes while local work remains to overlap with the force halo exchange. One way to do this is to split the local work into two parts and schedule a pipeline of local, then non-local, then remaining local. This would be relatively expensive on GPUs because the irregularity of pair list sizes would lead to low-occupancy tail effects on all three kernels.

So, currently on GPUs we schedule the local kernel first and the non-local when it arrives and rely on GPU stream priority to try to complete the non-local work ASAP. Historically this has worked fairly well on Nvidia GPUs, which have supported `cudaStreamCreateWithPriority` (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__CUDART__STREAM_1ge2be9e9858849bf62ba4a8b66d1c3540) since compute capability 3.5. For simplicity, we do the same on CPUs (where there is no stream priority) so the final force halo exchange may have no computation overlapped with it, which may hurt performance. The current approach will not work well on Intel or (perhaps) AMD GPUs, which lack hardware support for high-priority streams, even though there is language support for this e.g. in SYCL. The current approach will not work well at high scale on any hardware, because the local work shrinks to zero so little or nothing overlaps the communication.

**Proposal**

It is not necessary to do halo exchange of forces if the logic of halo exchange, grid, and pairlist construction changes so that forces between particles home to different domains are computed on both domains. This avoids communication of the force halo at the end of the force-computation phase by doing some redundant computation. The force contributions are computed identically on the two domains, but the accumulation of forces on particles will inevitably be different because the summation order will be different than it was previously. However we do not aim at reproducibility of GPU force computation. If ever we would aim at that, the proposed approach will work fine with it.

**Use cases**

Expected changes to simulation speed with multiple PP ranks:
* using Intel GPUs will be faster always
* using AMD GPUs may be faster always (**Edit**: AMD hardware has HW support, hipSYCL has support for priorities, whether that translates into scheduling with priorities honoured is unclear) 
* using Nvidia GPUs may be faster at sufficiently high scale that the communication cost is worth saving
* using only CPUs will be faster at sufficiently high scale that the communication cost is worth saving and where there was not already computation to overlap with the communication

**Impact**

Over time, the tradeoff for avoiding the force halo exchange is increasingly likely to be the correct one, as CPU and GPU performance continues to increase faster than communication.

It will also simplify the force schedule once we have enough confidence in the correctness of the implementation and its effect on performance to remove the old schedule.

Improving this situation is the highest priority for Mark in 2022, primarily to improve outcomes on Intel hardware.

**Detailed description**

Known issues:
* with 2D and 3D DD, the midpoints of the interaction for a pair of particles can lie in a domain home to neither particle. It is likely that the existing pulsing of communication in multiple dimensions can be adapted to ensure that such particles are communicated multiple times. If this proves problematic, then in the short term we can choose to implement support for only 1D DD, where this case cannot arise.

No issues are expected with simulations using
* separate PME ranks
* PME running on GPUs
* GPU-aware MPI (in any of the various forms, though halo exchange will now communicate more particles)
* FEP
* AWH
* pulling
* multi-simulations (including replica exchange)
* anything that currently only works with a single PP rank
* energy minimization
* rerun
* update groups
* vsites
* constraints
* bonded interactions
* MTS

Useful items of work currently identified:
- [ ] unit tests for DD grid construction
- [ ] extend those unit tests for new code paths
- [ ] unit tests for CPU neighbour lists
- [ ] extend those unit tests for new code paths
- [ ] unit tests for DD grid construction when GPUs are targeted
- [ ] extend those unit tests for new code paths
- [ ] unit tests for GPU neighbour lists
- [ ] extend those unit tests for new code paths
- [ ] unit tests for halo exchange particularly with multiple pulses
- [ ] extend those unit tests for new code paths
- [ ] add new feature-flag environment variable e.g. `GMX_ONLY_POSITION_HALO_EXCHANGE`
- [ ] extend `SimulationWorkload` data structure to permit force halo exchange to be skipped
- [ ] adapt force schedule to skip force halo exchange for 1D DD CPU-only simulations
- [ ] adapt force schedule to skip force halo exchange for 1D DD Intel GPU simulations
- [ ] measure performance and decide whether the new feature flag should support any other cases
- [ ] is there a reduced need to sort pair lists, particularly for non-local region?

Quality assurance during beta phase
- [ ] test all of the things listed above that are likely to Just Work
- [ ] try to use physical validation on larger scale
- [ ] run e.g. membrane simulations and observe correctness

Future work:
- [ ] support 2D and 3D DD CPU-only
- [ ] support 2D and 3D DD with GPU
- [ ] default to this code path when overall performance warrants making the code simpler
- [ ] consider switching to direct rather than pulsed multi-dimensional DD

closed_issues.title: CMake hang in gmxGenerateVersionInfo.cmake
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

CMake can hang at `execute_process(COMMAND /usr/local/bin/git name-rev --annotate-stdin RESULT_VARIABLE GIT_NAME_REV_KNOWS_ANNOTATE_STDIN OUTPUT_QUIET ERROR_QUIET )` while waiting for stdin to finish.

## Exact steps to reproduce

* CMake version 3.24.0
* git version 2.37.2
* configure with `GMX_GIT_VERSION_INFO=ON` (default)

and otherwise satisfy the conditions to get to line https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/cmake/gmxGenerateVersionInfo.cmake#L153

(Identified with `/usr/local/Cellar/cmake/3.24.0/bin/cmake -D GIT_EXECUTABLE=/usr/local/bin/git -D PROJECT_VERSION=2023-dev -D PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR=/Users/eric/develop/CLionProjects/gromacs2023 -D VERSION_CMAKEIN=/Users/eric/build/gromacs2023/release-tmpi/VersionInfo-partial.cmake.cmakein -D VERSION_OUT=/Users/eric/build/gromacs2023/release-tmpi/VersionInfo.cmake -P /Users/eric/develop/CLionProjects/gromacs2023/cmake/gmxGenerateVersionInfo.cmake --trace-expand`)

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

The CMake scriptlet was looking to see whether there was an error or not, but did not close the standard input filehandle.

## Possible fixes

Use the `INPUT_FILE` option to https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/execute_process.html

I don't know whether there is a CMake abstraction for `/dev/null` or empty input file.

closed_issues.title: Settings of `ReplicaExchangeType::Lambda` is mistakenly routed to `ReplicaExchangeType::TemperatureLambda`.
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

When replica exchange is enabled in the lambda-only mode, all reference temperatures `ref-t` are the same among replicas.

However, the log tells that another branch `temperature+lambda` is used. 
```text
Replica exchange in temperature and lambda state
 298.1 298.1 298.1 298.1
     0     1     2     3
```

**GROMACS version**

2021, 2022, etc.

**Steps to reproduce**

Suppose there are 4 simulation replicas with the MDP option snippet as below:
```text
; Temperature coupling
tcoupl = V-rescale
ref-t = 298.1  ; Values are the same in other MDP option files

; Free energy control stuff
free_energy = yes
init_lambda_state = 0  ; Values in other MDP option files can be 1,2,3
```

Then, launch multiple simulations with the following command:
```bash
gmx mdrun -multidir 0 1 2 3 -replex 200 ...
```

**What is the current bug behavior?**

The log tells that another branch `temperature+lambda` is used. 
```text
Replica exchange in temperature and lambda state
 298.1 298.1 298.1 298.1
     0     1     2     3
```

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Here are the log that we expect: 
```text
Replica exchange in lambda state
     0     1     2     3
```

**Possible fixes**

Fix comparison of float numbers in function repl_quantity.

closed_issues.title: LJ-14 energy computation does not apply "vdw-modifier" option, instead "vdw-modifier=None" is picked
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

I would like to report a possible bug. The [vdw-modifier](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html#van-der-waals) is not taken into account to compute the LJ-14 energy. Instead, LJ-14 is computed using [vdw-modifier](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html#van-der-waals)=None whatever the settings in the MDP file. As expected, the modifier is taken into account to compute the other LJ terms (1-5, 1-6, etc. intramolecular and intermolecular pairs).

**GROMACS version**

```
               :-) GROMACS - gmx_d, 2022.2 (double precision) (-:

Executable:   /home/kkempfer/venv/gromacs-2022.2/gromacs/bin/gmx_d
Data prefix:  /home/kkempfer/venv/gromacs-2022.2/gromacs
Working dir:  /home/kkempfer/projects/shared-external/2022-08-22-Gromacs-vdw-modifier/bcc-gaff
Command line:
  gmx_d -quiet --version

GROMACS version:    2022.2
Precision:          double
Memory model:       64 bit
MPI library:        thread_mpi
OpenMP support:     enabled (GMX_OPENMP_MAX_THREADS = 128)
GPU support:        disabled
SIMD instructions:  AVX2_256
CPU FFT library:    fftw-3.3.8-sse2-avx
GPU FFT library:    none
RDTSCP usage:       enabled
TNG support:        enabled
Hwloc support:      disabled
Tracing support:    disabled
C compiler:         /usr/bin/cc GNU 9.4.0
C compiler flags:   -mavx2 -mfma -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -O3 -DNDEBUG
C++ compiler:       /usr/bin/c++ GNU 9.4.0
C++ compiler flags: -mavx2 -mfma -pthread -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -fopenmp -O3 -DNDEBUG
```

**Steps to reproduce**

Compute single-point-energy of a single octane molecule in vacuum using various [vdw-modifier](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html#van-der-waals) options. Parameterization of the molecule using GAFF force field. Inputs were produced with AmberTools and converted to GROMACS with ParmEd. Single-point-energy with SANDER MD package showed correct file conversion (comparison made using GROMACS vdw-modifier=None option).

Coordinates and topology:
* [octane.gro](/uploads/6e9762ac2e7c9e2b5ac7137ec686cfdf/octane.gro)
* [octane.top](/uploads/d510ca5b5e279168c80a1c646e6b73ac/octane.top)

MDP, TPR, XVG and bash commands to produce the outputs:
* vdw-modifier=None: [spe.mdp](/uploads/6a7fc7f36017616715b44c1fcaf52490/spe.mdp), [spe.tpr](/uploads/31137207ceb528d886d7c436b1245e35/spe.tpr), [spe.xvg](/uploads/2b5bd61899292d2234a452ed28fcba73/spe.xvg) and commands [spe.sh](/uploads/158e3fcc81061fa2a3671ef1b24de28e/spe.sh)
* vdw-modifier=Potential-shift: [spe.mdp](/uploads/a3d0476450d0cd37b154a2459ddfc348/spe.mdp), [spe.tpr](/uploads/80736369ffde171515235466bde949c6/spe.tpr), [spe.xvg](/uploads/b5a58cf249bf4911bb3ec5b5052589cd/spe.xvg) and commands [spe.sh](/uploads/d968acc2d99adef1016bbf93d98f3106/spe.sh)
* Same example using vdw-modifier=Force-switch and vdw-modifier=Potential-switch available on demand.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

The [vdw-modifier](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html#van-der-waals) is not taken into account to compute the LJ-14 energy. Instead, LJ-14 is computed using [vdw-modifier](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html#van-der-waals)=None whatever the settings in the MDP file.

```
@ s0 legend "Bond"
@ s1 legend "Angle"
@ s2 legend "Proper Dih."
@ s3 legend "LJ-14"
@ s4 legend "Coulomb-14"
@ s5 legend "LJ (SR)"
@ s6 legend "Coulomb (SR)"
@ s7 legend "Potential"

==> spe-gromacs/spe.xvg <==
    0.000000    1.206725211560   14.634074247574   14.278744975558    7.825652923985    1.714272125542    4.297731077350    2.535255733900   46.492456295470

==> spe-vdwFswitch-gromacs/spe.xvg <==
    0.000000    1.206725211560   14.634074247574   14.278744975558    7.825652923985    1.714272125542    4.549744051510    2.535255733900   46.744469269629

==> spe-vdwPswitch-gromacs/spe.xvg <==
    0.000000    1.206725211560   14.634074247574   14.278744975558    7.825652923985    1.714272125542    4.325040426721    2.535255733900   46.519765644840

==> spe-vdwshift-gromacs/spe.xvg <==
    0.000000    1.206725211560   14.634074247574   14.278744975558    7.825652923985    1.714272125542    4.373003418385    2.535255733900   46.567728636504
```

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Applying a VDW modifier, _e.g._ [vdw-modifier](https://manual.gromacs.org/current/user-guide/mdp-options.html#van-der-waals)=Potential-shift shifts the potential by a constant for all distances (such as the potential equals zero at the cutoff), even very short ones. This behavior works as expected for the LJ term, but not the LJ-14 term. The same shift should be applied for every pair, without excluding the 1-4 ones. LAMMPS [pair_modify shift yes](https://docs.lammps.org/pair_modify.html) command applies the shift for every LJ pairs, including LJ-14.

Using other VDW modifiers, _e.g._ [Force-switch or Potential-switch](https://manual.gromacs.org/documentation/2019/reference-manual/functions/nonbonded-interactions.html#modified-non-bonded-interactions) changes the functional form of the LJ pairwise interaction. It should also be applied between atoms connected through 3 bonds (LJ-14).

**Possible fixes**

Similar to LAMMPS MD package, apply any vdw-modifier to compute the LJ-14 term. Thank you for your comments.

closed_issues.title: pdb2gmx generates wrong virtual sites for tetrahedral amine
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

I am to simulate a protein with a modified lysine, where the side chain has been extended so that the amine is now a secondary amine and neutral. It should be in a tetrahedral configuration, with one H and one lone pair (the latter not explicitly modelled at present). I have created an rtp entry for the residue and added all required new parameters to the forcefield files, but pdb2gmx makes the wrong virtual sites parameters for the amine hydrogen. Specifically, it generates a virtual_sites3 type 2 (3fd) entry, which makes the amine flat, but I would expect a virtual_site3 type 4 (3out). Changing it manually is error prone and tedious. Also this error could go unnoticed, as it did during my first round of simulations.

**GROMACS version**

  gmx -quiet --version
```
GROMACS version:    2022.2
Precision:          mixed
Memory model:       64 bit
MPI library:        thread_mpi
OpenMP support:     enabled (GMX_OPENMP_MAX_THREADS = 128)
GPU support:        disabled
SIMD instructions:  ARM_NEON_ASIMD
CPU FFT library:    fftw-3.3.8
GPU FFT library:    none
TNG support:        enabled
Hwloc support:      disabled
Tracing support:    disabled
C compiler:         /opt/homebrew/bin/gcc-11 GNU 11.2.0
C compiler flags:   -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -O3 -DNDEBUG
C++ compiler:       /opt/homebrew/bin/g++-11 GNU 11.2.0
C++ compiler flags: -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -fopenmp -O3 -DNDEBUG
```
**Steps to reproduce**

`gmx pdb2gmx -ignh -water tip3p -f LFR_A.pdb -o LFR_p2g -i LFR_p2g -p LFR_p2g -vsite hydrogens`
Choose amber99sb-ildn LFR/S.

[files_for_reproducing.tar.gz](/uploads/2843161b4f4bd86fa07f7b09ad241125/files_for_reproducing.tar.gz)

I have tested using the resulting topology for an energy minimization (after solvating etc) and the amine becomes planar during the run. If I manually edit the topology (like the expected result below) I get a tetrahedral geometry.
(Please describe how we can reproduce the bug, and share all files needed - ideally both the TPR file and the raw GRO/MDP/TOP files needed to regenerate it. Bugs that only appear after running for 3 hours on 200 GPUs unfortunately tend to not get a lot of attention. You will typically get much faster attention if you have been able to narrow it down to the smallest possible input, command line, system size, etc.)

**What is the current bug behavior?**

pdb2gmx makes virtual site parameters that makes a tetrahedral amine flat: a 3fd site.

```
[ virtual_sites3 ]
...
 1450  1449  1446  1451     2
```
(1450 is the H on the amine)

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

A tetrahedral geometry with 3out construction.
```
[ virtual_sites3 ]
...
 1450  1449  1446  1451     4
```

**Possible fixes**

I have not yet found where the vsites are handled in pdb2gmx, but I can probably have a closer look if someone gives me a few pointers (no pun intended).

closed_issues.title: Incorrect formula and references in Manual for restricted bending force
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Hi, I believe that the formula of [Restricted bending force](<https://manual.gromacs.org/current/reference-manual/functions/bonded-interactions.html#restricted-bending-potential>), Eq. 189, contains the following error.  

- There should not be factor 2.
- There should be a minus sign at the beginning.

Also, on the same page, journal information of references (83) and (88) are swapped. (Titles and authors are correct.)

Current (incorrect)
> 83 M. Bulacu, N. Goga, W. Zhao, G. Rossi, L. Monticelli, X. Periole, D. Tieleman, and S. Marrink, “Improved angle potentials for coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations,” J. Chem. Phys., 123 [11] (2005).  
> 88 M. Bulacu and E. van der Giessen, “Effect of bending and torsion rigidity on self-diffusion in polymer melts: A molecular-dynamics study,” JCTC, 9 [8] 3282–3292 (2013).

They should be
> 83 M. Bulacu, N. Goga, W. Zhao, G. Rossi, L. Monticelli, X. Periole, D. Tieleman, and S. Marrink, “Improved angle potentials for coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations,” J. Chem. Theory Comput., 9 [8] 3282–3292 (2013).  
> 88 M. Bulacu and E. van der Giessen, “Effect of bending and torsion rigidity on self-diffusion in polymer melts: A molecular-dynamics study,” J. Chem. Phys., 123 [11] 114901 (2005).


## Additional information

This error must have been inherited from the original paper Ref 83 (2013 JCTC). 

Briefly looking at the code <https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/src/gromacs/listed_forces/restcbt.cpp>, it seems the force is correctly calculated without factor 2 (otherwise one would notice this earlier).

closed_issues.title: CMake 3.24 breaks `.../share/gmxapi/gmxapi.cmake`
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

If GROMACS is configured and installed with CMake 3.24, the installed `gmxapi.cmake` file will cause `find_package(gmxapi)` where it would have succeded before.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Configure GROMACS with CMake 3.24 and GMXAPI enabled (default). Install, and observe the addition in `gmxapi.cmake`:


```
# Make sure the targets which have been exported in some other
# export set exist.
unset(${CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_NAME}_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE_targets)
foreach(_target "Gromacs::libgromacs" )
  if(NOT TARGET "${_target}" )
    set(${CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_NAME}_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE_targets "${${CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_NAME}_NOT_FOUND_MESSAGE_targets} ${_target}")
  endif()
endforeach()
```


The issue is confirmed on GROMACS 2019, 2021, 2022.

## For developers: Why is this important?

CMake 3.24.0 is new, and this could even be unintended behavior of `install(TARGETS ... EXPORT ...)`. We should try to figure this out so it can be in the next GROMACS patch release(s) before 3.24+ is more widely used.

It is less of an issue for older releases, because (presumably) they are already installed, configured before CMake 3.24 was out.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

Excerpted error:

      CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:79 (find_package):
        Found package configuration file:

          /Users/eric/install/gromacs2021-mpi/share/cmake/gmxapi/gmxapi-config.cmake

        but it set gmxapi_FOUND to FALSE so package "gmxapi" is considered to be
        NOT FOUND.  Reason given by package:

        The following imported targets are referenced, but are missing:
        Gromacs::libgromacs


The following should just work.

    . path/to/GMXRC
    pip install gmxapi

It definitely _shouldn't_ depend on the CMake version used to configure and install GROMACS.

## Possible fixes

Apparently updates are necessary to https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/api/gmxapi/cpp/cmake/gmxapi-config.cmake.in and/or
https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/main/api/gmxapi/cpp/CMakeLists.txt

**Work-arounds:**

* Use CMake less than 3.24 when configuring and installing GROMACS.
* `find_package(GROMACS)` successfully before doing `find_package(gmxapi)` (see !2934).

**Additionally**

The Python package installation code should have a workaround added, just in case someone installs a no-longer-maintained GROMACS release with CMake 3.24+.

@eirrgang will want to patch the Python package installers for gmxapi 0.1 and 0.2, but these are maintained in release-2020 and release-2021, respectively, and presumably no longer eligible for patches in gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/.

closed_issues.title: New command line wrapper tool for gmxapi
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

The gmxapi Python package includes a command to wrap command line calls as gmxapi Operations. Since we have been slow to add Python bindings for tools other than the simulator, `gmxapi.commandline_operation` has been a much more commonly used tool than originally expected. With use, we find many shortcomings and fundamental design weaknesses.

I propose a new `executable()` command line wrapper, which I expect will replace `commandline_operation` within a few releases.

**Use cases**

Requirements to address:
* express input files (dependencies) without requiring a mapping to command line flags
* express output files that may not be represented as command line flags
* avoid tight coupling to assumptions about the structure of command line options
* allow expression of pre-launch requirements (e.g. `module load` or other scriptlets that should be run in the execution environment before the main subprocess)
* provide for input data staging for commands that expect certain files to exist in the working directory (or at a known/knowable path) (See also #4311)
* express resource requirements that affect the ability of tasks to run concurrently, or which must be reserved via #3718 (E.g. MPI-aware commands that expect or require an MPI context and related environment variables; GPU-accelerated programs; See also #4542.)

Stretch goal:
* flexibly express available resources to the tool. E.g. provide the value of a `-n` command line option or `OMP_NUM_THREADS` environment variable in terms of number of cores available to the user, possibly modified according to resource division between concurrent tasks in an ensemble. This would require work on #4542 to realize, but we should at least try to define the interface for expressing inputs related to resource allocation, and any supporting helper functions, which might produce something even more dynamic than the regular Futures.

**Impact**

The two major areas of use most affected are
* ensemble workflows involving accelerated command line tools
* command line tools with implicit inputs and outputs

**Detailed description**

@eirrgang will provide a proposed specification (preview the work-in-progress at the snippet https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/snippets/2381417
), and begin soliciting comments for iterative refinement towards an initial version in late Q3 or Q4 2022.

**Requirements**

*tbd*

**Links/references/implementations**

We should consider whether there are any specific workflow management systems or execution managers that we would like to directly interact with, but we should at least try to make sure there is a clear mapping to/from a few popular ways to portably represent command line tasks.

* CWL
* Parsl bash_app
* RADICAL Pilot executable
* Copernicus

closed_issues.title: Update the Sphinx html theme
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

http://manual.gromacs.org/ looks like the old [Python 2 documentation](https://docs.python.org/2.7/reference/index.html)

We are using an essentially unmaintained theme that makes poor (and non-dynamic) use of browser window real estate, renders hard-to-read API documentation, and is arcane to configure.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Compare https://manual.gromacs.org/current/index.html to, say, https://pradyunsg.me/furo

## For developers: Why is this important?

We can (and should) modernize the look and feel of the built documentation, start to unify the look and feel with other gromacs.org web sites, take advantage of new technologies (like inline tabs, nested "admonitions", and HTML5 elements replacing JavaScript), and improve the readability of API and code docs.

## Possible fixes

[furo](https://pradyunsg.me/furo) has become a popular sphinx theme. By default, it is more visually consistent with the 'alabaster' theme currently in use at https://www.gromacs.org. It's appearance is easy to [customize](https://pradyunsg.me/furo/customisation) via `html_theme_options`.

For an example of what the refresh could look like,

    docker run --rm -p 8080:80 gromacs/docs:furo

and browse to http://localhost:8080/

@eirrgang offers https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/commits/mei-web-theme as a branch from which one or more merge requests can be derived, but it may take some additional time to update the GitLab CI Docker images and to check for any necessary updates to minimum required software versions for the Sphinx build targets.

closed_issues.title: Allow gmxapi.commandline_operation to run ensemble tasks concurrently.
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

* Let `gmxapi.operation` map ensemble tasks to MPI ranks, generally.
* Let `gmxapi.commandline_operation` map new keyword argument(s) to assertions about task-concurrency safety and MPI resource requirements.

**Use cases**

When gmxapi scripts are invoked with `mpiexec` and multiple cores, gmxapi operations should have more generic ability to use those resources.

**Impact**

For non-trivial workflows that mix simulation set-up or analysis steps between large ensemble simulations, only the `gmxapi.mdrun` operations have benefited from parallel resources. For short simulations, large ensembles, or expensive non-simulation steps, we should try to make much better use of resources.

**Detailed description**

Historically, `gmxapi.commandline_operation()` has not had a way to distinguish whether arrays of commands are safe to run concurrently or not, and thus it has run ensemble members sequentially.

With the addition of the (*env* kwarg)[https://manual.gromacs.org/current/gmxapi/userguide/pythonreference.html#gmxapi.commandline_operation], we can work around issues related to MPI-enabled CLI tools run from `mpiexec`ed Python scripts. Along with isolated task directories, we should have the tools in place to be able to run CLI tasks concurrently on separate gmxapi ranks.

1. We need to let the basic operation ResourceManager map MPI ranks to ensemble tasks (as with gmxapi.mdrun), subject to some controls about whether concurrent execution is safe and how output should be made available on other ranks.
2. `gmxapi.commandline_operation()` needs at least one new kwarg that will allow *env* to be cleaned automatically and appropriately, direct appropriate allocation of ranks (some commands may prefer to execute sequentially under the full MPI context), and direct concurrent execution, when appropriate.

This is a pure Python fix, but will extend our reliance on `mpi4py`.

@eirrgang will try to prepare these features for gmxapi 0.4, but the issue priority is uncertain, and it may miss the feature-freeze deadline.

closed_issues.title: Capture terminal output for gmxapi.mdrun
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Try to capture stdout and stderr to files in the working directories of gmxapi.mdrun tasks.

This issue is intentionally orthogonal to library-level updates to output environment management. Before libgromacs first uses the stdout and stderr filehandles, we will attempt to replace them (from the Python interpreter) with alternative filehandles.

* facilitate debugging of ensemble simulation jobs.
* provide a normalized way to programmatically access more output (through the filesystem, at least)

**Use cases**

* Capture output from multiple simulations more robustly in ensemble contexts.
* Capture terminal output as `stdout.txt` and `stderr.txt` until better library-level output handling can be devised.

**Impact**

This is important to gmxapi users who use `gmxapi.mdrun` for ensemble simulations, especially when they are trying to debug failures on non-root ensemble members.

This workaround takes some pressure off of developers to make short-term progress on remediating C stdlib writes to stdout/stderr or extending the output_environment library facility.

@eirrgang proposes to provide a pure-Python patch for gmxapi 0.4.

**Detailed description**

libgromacs currently has many cases of output being written directly to the stdout or stderr

Previously, when libgromacs wrote to stdout or stderr in a gmxapi script, the output would not be seen by the Python interpreter. In the case of an ensemble simulation (Python interpreter launched with `mpiexec`, simulations run with thread-MPI), outputs from non-root-ranks were at the mercy of the MPI framework, and, at best, only available at the job level.

We can manipulate the process filehandles from the Python interpreter before and between calls into libgromacs. This should allow us to record a `stdout.txt` and `stderr.txt` for each task executed through libgmxapi Python bindings.

In many cases, libgromacs forces the process to crash hard during API calls that fail. In many cases, the Python interpreter has no opportunity to do any sort of clean shut down when an error occurs during simulation. This may result in some unflushed output missing from `stdout.txt` or `stderr.txt`. Since this may be the most useful output of the job (for debugging purposes), we should probably avoid fancy IO streams or pipelines, and just close/open/close `w` filehandles with little to no buffering.

We can refer to the current library implementation as a baseline. If the current implementation relies on the parent process to flush the file descriptors, and it is inappropriate to do otherwise (in order to avoid possible deadlocks while exiting, for instance), we may have to do one or more of the following
* use less stdio buffering for gmxapi.mdrun
* register additional handlers (or traps), e.g. `MPI_Comm_set_errhandler`, and use an extra thread or parent process to try to perform clean-up without dead-locks or unnecessarily long blocking I/O.
* wait for GROMACS library development that defers more error handling to the API caller

closed_issues.title: "gmx mdrun -cpnum -cpt 0" produces very much output
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

This is a mixture of an odd observation and a wishlist item. I was looking for a way to output the state of an MD as a cpt file every 1000 steps and found the -cpnum flag. Now there are a couple oddities that bugged me:
1. The interval between cpt outputs as given by the flag -cpt can only be given in (wall clock) minutes, which is not useful for me.
2. Giving the flag -cpt 0, the MD generates a cpt state file every 50 steps. Why 50? I have no idea. The number 50 does not seem to be dependent on any mdp parameter and instead seems to be hardcoded.

**GROMACS version**

GROMACS version:    2023-dev-20220429-2420017e34

**Steps to reproduce**

Run "gmx mdrun -cpnum -cpt 0" on your favorite toy model MD.

**What could/should be done**

I see two possible ways to improve this behavior:
1. Introduce a flag e.g. -cptstep to allow for the state to be saved every fixed number of steps.
2. Expose the number 50, which is used if the flag -cpt 0 is applied, in the mdp file, e.g. as "nstcpnum".

It would be great if something like this could be implemented. Unfortunately, I do not know the code well enough to have any idea where to start looking if I were to try adding it myself.

closed_issues.title: Update to PDB Atom Name (V3)
closed_issues.description: We need to update to the Atom Name (V3) naming convention.  Most programs have already updated to this including Tinker, OpenMM, pdbfixer, APBS, pdb2pqr, etc.  See example http://ligand-expo.rcsb.org/reports/P/PRO/atom-names.html.  All beta and gamma carbons `two tetrahedral hydrogens, e.g. C-CH-C` should use the naming convention HB2/HB3 and HG2/HG3 instead of HB1/HB2 and HG1/HG2 like what is currently used.  Either update these to follow V3 or we need to find a way (probably add additional column) in the hydrogen database files *.hdb to be able to start the numbering other than default of 1.

closed_issues.title: Error in the Manual page "Managing Long Simulations"
closed_issues.description:
Hello!
I'm a researcher and a GROMACS user and I was trying to learn how to continue a simulation with a modified .mdp file with some different parameters than initially used in that simulation, as described in the GROMACS manual page entitled "Managing Long Simulations".

In that manual page, in the topic "Changing mdp options for a restart" one is instructed to create a new .tpr file with the modified .mdp file with the command line "gmx grompp -f possibly-changed.mdp -p possibly-changed.top -c state.cpt -o new.tpr". The problem is that for the flag/option "-c" the format .cpt of the checkpoint file is not acceptable. Instead, one must use the flag/option "-t" with the state.cpt file. Not only that, but one must also provide a coordinate file with the last or desired frame of the trajectory with the flag/option "-c" but in another format, such as .pdb or .gro.
So the command line should actually be "gmx grompp -f possibly-changed.mdp -p possibly-changed.top -c frame.gro -t state.cpt -o new.tpr".

Then, there's another issue with the next suggestion in that same manual page, which instructs one to run the simulation with the command line "gmx mdrun -s new.tpr -cpi state.cpt". When I try to do that, gromacs throws the error:

"Inconsistency in user input:
Some output files listed in the checkpoint file md_0_5000.cpt are not present
or not named as the output files by the current program:)
Expected output files that are present:

Expected output files that are not present or named differently:
  md_0_5000.log
  md_0_5000.xtc
  md_0_5000.edr

To keep your simulation files safe, this simulation will not restart. Either
name your output files exactly the same as the previous simulation part (e.g.
with -deffnm or explicit naming), or make sure all the output files are
present (e.g. run from the same directory as the previous simulation part), or
instruct mdrun to write new output files with mdrun -noappend. In the last
case, you will not be able to use appending in future for this simulation."

But those files it says are missing are actually present on the working directory and are named exactly that way.
Now, if I try to run the simulation with the flags "-deffnm" and "-noappend", as the program suggests on that error message, then I get another error:

"Fatal error:
Cannot change a simulation algorithm during a checkpoint restart. Perhaps you
should make a new .tpr with grompp -f new.mdp -t md_0_5000.cpt"

And that suggestion is exactly what I did before to create a new .tpr file as per the manual page in question.

Finnally, I got the simulation to run without referencing the checkpoint file with the flag/option "-cpi".
(command line "gmx mdrun -s new.tpr").
Considering the new .tpr file was generated with the coordinates from the last frame of the trajectory with the flag/option "-c frame.gro" and the velocities of that trajectory with the flag/option "-t state.cpt", in the same way it's done when creating a .tpr file to run a production MD simulation continuing from an NPT equilibration stage, is it really necessary to reference the checkpoint file with the flag/option "-cpi" when calling the "gmx mdrun" program? Because this is not usually done when starting a production MD (we do not reference the npt.cpt checkpoint file from the pressure equilibration stage when calling the "gmx mdrun" program, only when creating the .tpr file with the "gmx grompp" program).

Thanks for your support and time!

closed_issues.title: Feature request: gmxapi "Future slicing"
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

We should normalize behavior of Future subscripting with respect to subscripting of results.

We have always had partial support for subscripting the outputs of gmxapi operations, but confusing or erroneous behavior when subscripting a gmxapi Future that, itself, is the result of subscripting a gmxapi Future.

Consider an operation of the following sort.
```python
grompp = gmx.commandline_operation('gmx', arguments=['grompp'], ...,
    output_files=[{
        '-o': filenames[i],
    } for i in range(n_sim)])
grompp.output.file['-o'][0].result()
```

Given such a workflow,
`grompp.output.file['-o'][i].result()` is reported to cause `TypeError: issubclass() arg 1 must be a class`, whereas `grompp.output.file['-o'].result()[i]` behaves as expected, returning the `i` th member of the `'-o'` output from the `grompp` operation.

* We should be able to index into indexable Future slices.
* We should be clear about the appropriate order of subscripting and provide more helpful error output when the subscripting does not make sense.

To the latter point, I think the appropriate syntax for this use case would have actually been `grompp.output.file[i]['-o']`, but it is not yet determined whether that would have worked differently, and it is certainly not clear from the error.
It appears that the logic for Future slicing is not doing a good job with the multiple levels of indirection. Early attempts to address #2993 were discouraged, so we had to allow `None` as a placeholder data type for Futures, such as when we take a value from a Mapping of unknown value type. However, we probably neglect the logic for when we then want to take an element from a possible list value through that proxy to the Mapping.

Resolution of this issue requires refinement of the gmxapi data model, which is already necessary for the work in progress on #2993.

See also
* https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/4460
* https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/3179

closed_issues.title: Improve SIMD warnings - instructions sets are not incremental
closed_issues.description:
Nandan has reported crashes he could not understand where the output merely contained a minor recommendation:

`Compiled SIMD: AVX_128_FMA, but for this host/run AVX2_128 might be better (see log).`

This specific crash happens because AVX2 is not a superset of AVX_128_FMA (which happens to contain AMD-specific instructions. 

However, apart from a specific error message, in particular our MPI code makes assumptions that SIMD instruction sets are incremental and just tries to identify the "lowest" and "highest" level supported, which in general is not true. I believe we need to change this to always provide a short warning when SIMD instruction sets are mismatching (in particular when nodes are different in an MPI job), and only make explicit exceptions to be quiet in cases where we know we should NOT warn.

closed_issues.title: DD setup incorrect with GPU comm + update
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

The DD initialization will assume `-dlb auto` for the initial grid setup even with direct GPU communication which forces DLB to be permanently disabled.

This happens due to initialization order since the DD builder in ``DomainDecompositionBuilder::Impl::Impl()` first makes a DD grid setup taking into account initial cell size limits, but shortly after checking DD restrictions it may disable DLB if GPU direct communication is left enabled. As a result, the cell limits assuming DLB may turn on remain active. 


**GROMACS version**

2022.1 and earlier

**Steps to reproduce**

Run mdrun with direct GPU communication enabled with DLB auto and off.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

Incorrect DD cell setup with direct GPU communication and `-dlb auto`.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

The DD cell setup to be the same with GPU direct communication `-dlb auto` and `-dlb no`.

**Possible fixes**

* In the 2022 code: ?
* In main since the DD limitations are eliminated, turning off DLB should happen earlier.

closed_issues.title: Default value of verlet-buffer-tolerance may not be appropriate for some coarse-grained systems
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

The default value of verlet-buffer-tolerance (0.005 kJ/mol/ps) may not be appropriate for some C-alpha coarse-grained systems. My simulations of coarse-grained intrinsically disordered proteins will invariably crash due to atom separation errors when using the default value of verlet-buffer-tolerance.
A sentence or two should be added to the manual to explain to users that if they are using a bespoke coarse-grained system, they might need to test different values of verlet-buffer-tolerance/rlist if their simulations are crashing.

All files can be found in this .zip file: [reproduction_files.zip](/uploads/7cc7e3b5232007df49e286085113bf0d/reproduction_files.zip)


**GROMACS version**

Versions of code tested: 2022.1 vanilla (cpu; MPI enabled), 2021.1 vanilla (cpu; MPI enabled; CUDA enabled), 2020.2 Modified (MPI enabled).


**Steps to reproduce**
I generated a 92-bead, C-alpha coarse grained protein molecule (see "./top/linker_segment.itp" and "./top/linker.top" for description) and excluded angle potential and dihedral potential terms from the molecule. I placed 50 copies of this molecule in a box and ran 200 ps of NVT equilibration to produce the "MDproduction_input.gro" file. The run file "MDproduction_input.tpr" was generated using "./mdp/md.mdp" and the provided .gro and .top files with command `gmx grompp -f mdp/md.mdp -c MDproduction_input.gro -p top/linker.top -o MDproduction_input.tpr`.

Gromacs 2022.1 (vanilla) was used to reproduce the error for the current set up (the `-nt 4 -pin on` flags were passed to mdrun). After 123360 ps of simulation (out of 300 ns), the simulation crashes.


**What is the current bug behavior?**

(What actually happens)
The simulation crashes -- here is the error message produced from `gmx mdrun`:
`WARNING: Listed nonbonded interaction between particles 711 and 714
at distance 2.001 which is larger than the table limit 1.912 nm.

This is likely either a 1,4 interaction, or a listed interaction inside
a smaller molecule you are decoupling during a free energy calculation.
Since interactions at distances beyond the table cannot be computed,
they are skipped until they are inside the table limit again. You will
only see this message once, even if it occurs for several interactions.

IMPORTANT: This should not happen in a stable simulation, so there is
probably something wrong with your system. Only change the table-extension
distance in the mdp file if you are really sure that is the reason.`


**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

(What you should see instead)
I expected a fully flexible (no angle/dihedral potential terms) coarse-grained molecule to run successfully without crashing. Please see the attached "MDproduction_output.log" file for additional information.

Once I change verlet-buffer-tolerance to a value like 1E-7, then the simulation no longer crashes.


**Possible fixes**

A sentence or two should be added to the manual to explain to users that if they are using a bespoke coarse-grained system, they might need to test different values of verlet-buffer-tolerance/rlist if their simulations are crashing. 
There is currently nothing in the documentation that would suggest that the default value might lead to simulation crashing of coarse-grained systems and adding a sentence might help future users more quickly troubleshoot issues.

closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

In gromacs documentation Release 2022.1 (Apr 22, 2022), the value of Universal gas constant (R) has been misprinted and appears to be incorrect after decimal.

It may be unclear to the user whether gromacs is utilising the proper value from the source they mentioned (https://www.nist.gov/).

**Detailed description**

'The values used in GROMACS are taken from the NIST Homepage,' says page 311 of the gromacs manual, which was published on April 22, 2022. On the internet, I looked up the value of the universal gas constant (8.314 462 618... J mol-1 K-1) and compared it to the value in the gromacs handbook (8.314 462 1 J mol-1 K-1, Table 5.4: Some Physical Constants on page 312). The inconsistency was discovered at the 7th position after the decimal.

closed_issues.title: Implement VkFFT FFT backend for SYCL
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

Implement VkFFT support for the SYCL backend. We have found that VkFFT is far superior on AMD GPUs therefore adding VkFFT support could increase performance substantially. This is a performance improvement and therefore not critical. Nonetheless, I would be very happy to contribute.

### Expected performance improvement

Below the runtime of a forward and backward 3DFFT was measured. Based on the data it is clear that rocFFT is still lagging behind VkFFT by a substantial margin. The measurements are from a MI210 card. RocFFT 5.1.3 and rocFFT latest (32465af) were tested and compared against VkFFT latest (5fd8d7e). In most cases, VkFFT reduced the runtime of the FFT computation by more than 60%. 

| MI210         | Y\*Z\*X         | hipFFT 5.1.3 | hipFFT latest  | vkFFT | vs hipFFT | vs hipFFT latest |
|---------------|-------------|--------|---------------|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| aqp           |    84\*84\*72 |    116 |           104 |    84 |   -27.59% |         -19.23% |
| eag1          | 128\*128\*120 |    186 |           180 |   156 |   -16.13% |         -13.33% |
| adh           | 100\*100\*100 |    130 |           126 |   110 |   -15.38% |         -12.70% |
| cellulose | 280\*128\*128 |    990 |           871 |   320 |   -67.68% |         -63.26% |

closed_issues.title: muparser CMake logic may not find OpenMP headers
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

`external/muparser/CMakeLists.txt` sets `ENABLE_OPENMP` to `${GMX_OPENMP}`, which will set the `MUP_USE_OPENMP` define used in `muParserBase.cpp` to determine whether to try to `#include <omp.h>`.

However, the `muparser` CMake target is not configured to use any of the other logic that the gromacs targets use to find OpenMP details.

This means that muparser may fail to compile while the rest of gromacs compiles (when `omp.h` is not available through some global mechanism).

## Possible fixes

The recommended fix would be to `target_link_libraries(muparser PRIVATE OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX)`.

I'm not sure whether this should be done in `src/external/muparser/CMakeLists.txt` or whether that will cause problems merging updates.

closed_issues.title: CMake "Darwin" checks may be too aggressive
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

For MacOS, we have a conditional `if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Darwin")` block to
* make sure that CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET is sufficiently modern, and
* avoid universal binaries and/or non-64-bit builds

These may no longer be helpful, and may be overly aggressive (doing more harm than good).

In particular, forcefully setting `CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES x86_64` <s>prevents</s> *would prevent* attempts to build for `arm64`/`arm64e` *(if the conditional were actually evaluated)*. *update: I find that CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is not actually set automatically by this point in the processing.*

Recent versions of MacOS and XCode seem to have adequately updated defaults.

If there are still problems that we want to help users with on Darwin, we can probably provide more dynamic support with advice on forums if we minimize the intrusiveness of our CMake scripting. If we choose to try to address this sort of thing in CMakeLists.txt, it would probably be more appropriate to do checks and provide status messages, rather than to override the user interaction with CMake, if we can avoid it.

## Suggestion

Replace the `set` statements with `if` blocks that provide helpful messages if
* CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET has been set and is `VERSION_LESS` than 10.14
* CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES has been set and includes `i386`

Alternatively, just remove the whole block, wait to see if there are problems, and restore a less aggressive / more targeted help as is shown to be necessary.

In any case, the block is not effective unless we change the conditional to use a better check. CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME is not automatically defined by this point in the processing, so `if(APPLE)` would be a better conditional.

For the convenience of using the insert-molecules command and reducing manual topology editing, I propose to add
1. a concentration parameter (as in genion command) of added molecules for automated calculation of their quantity,
2. optional in-out topology file to record this quantity.
3. An additional convenience would be the optional addition of include itp-files for molecules to the topology.

I have already tried to implement the first two points, they work. If my suggestions are interesting, I can try to finish the third point.

../src/gromacs/simd/scalar/scalar.h:110:21: note: candidate function

                    ^

closed_issues.title: c-rescale doesn't work in NPH
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

C-rescale uses the reference temperature in its stochastic term. When using MD and no temperature coupling algorithm, `grompp` silently sets the reference temperature to 0, independently of the mdp value of `ref-t`. C-rescale then, just as silently, uses this reference temperature in its stochastic term. 

This leads to the stochastic term cancelling out, and c-rescale essentially retrieving Berendsen barostat behavior. Under NPH, c-rescale is therefore having the same non-physical behavior as Berendsen, without any notice to the user.

**Edit:** As mentioned by @GiovanniBussi below, c-rescale doesn't become identical to Berendsen, as c-rescale still does velocity scaling which is not present in Berendsen.

This affects all versions of GROMACS in which c-rescale is present.

## Possible fixes

I think we can 
* forbid the combination (i.e. throw an error if c-rescale barostat is chosen with ref-t == 0), which would mean that c-rescale can't be used for NPH calculations. 
* add an additional mdp value for the barostat reference temperature. That would likely require some sanity checks when ref-t != 0 (what happens if a user choses different temperatures for thermostat and barostat??).
* change the behavior of grompp, and avoid it setting the reference temperature to 0. I think that would be the cleanest solution, but would require careful checking that no other code is depending on this value being zeroed in NVE / NPH calculations.

Happy to hear your thoughts, @GiovanniBussi and @berkhess.

milestone.title: 2023.beta1
milestone.description:
Milestone for the first beta release of GROMACS-2023. Milestones for the current release are on Fridays, and the actual release will take place during the week after to have some time to fix unexpected bugs, pipeline errors, handle MRs that are delayed by a day etc.
Due to unexpected personal workload, this release is delayed by a few days compared to the original plans (now planned for 17 November). Sincere apologies for that!

Any *planned* changes should be done by the end of devcycle3, and changes to our infrastructure/testing that can potentially influence other MRs need to be done well before the end of devcycle3.

Then we will have two more weeks for unexpected issues or delays to critical stuff, which we will bump to the beta milestone towards the end of devcycle3.

In contrast to earlier years, we have postponed the date for the beta. However, this means we will only have a single beta, and ALL code changes (not just significant ones) MUST be *MERGED* before the beta, or they will be bumped. We will only fix bugs after the beta.
