closed_issues.title: Improve MKL flag detection with open-source IntelLLVM
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Currently, using MKL requires setting all flags manually unless we're using branded Intel compiler.

While using MKL with non-Intel compiler for CPU FFT might be quite obscure.

Besides, MKL is required to run FFTs on Intel GPUs, but is not automatically detected when using open-source IntelLLVM SYCL compiler. At the moment, open-source IntelLLVM is used in development, since it (a) offers CUDA support, disabled in oneAPI; (b) helps to prepare for the future oneAPI release.

In situations where MKLROOT environment variable is set, we might still set flags automatically.

References:

https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/onemkl-link-line-advisor.html#gs.q0zhgt

CMake options confirmed to work with SYCL build:

```
-DMKL_INCLUDE_DIR=${MKLROOT}/include
-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_OPTIONS=-DMKL_ILP64
-DMKL_LIBRARIES="-Wl,--start-group;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_sycl.a;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_intel_ilp64.a;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_sequential.a;${MKLROOT}/lib/intel64/libmkl_core.a;-Wl,--end-group;-lpthread;-lm;-ldl"
```

closed_issues.title: Incorrect treatment of perturbed constraint length for the Verlet buffer estimate
closed_issues.description:
The Verlet buffer estimate always used the A-state constraint length. This leads to an incorrect buffer estimate with perturbed constraints. In practice this is never an issue as nearly always very few constraints are perturbed, so the effect on the buffer is much smaller than the effect of other approximations that always give a large overestimate of the buffer size.

Another effect was that a division by zero (constraint length) occurs in the verlet buffer calculation when the A-state constraint length is zero with a dynamic FEP lambda. But in the 2020 and 2021 releases this setup is disallowed by grompp, so only the 2022-RC was affected.

closed_issues.title: Missing intra-warp synchronization in LINCS and SETTLE CUDA kernels
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

When doing shared memory reduction, we don't call `__syncwarp` on the last iterations. This is not correct for Volta+ GPUs with 

Issue exists since the LINCS and SETTLE kernels were introduced and can lead to incorrect results when using GPU Update.

Note: SYCL kernels are fine, although SETTLE had a related, even more serious, issue problem by !2484.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Build GROMACS with CUDA support. Run any code using GPU update with either SETTLE or LINCS under `compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck`. Observe:

```
$ GMX_FORCE_UPDATE_DEFAULT_GPU=1 compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck ./bin/mdrun-output-test --gtest_filter=MdrunCanWrite/Trajectories.ThatDifferInNstxout/2
...
========= Warning: Race reported between Write access at 0x1cc0 in void gmx::settle_kernel<(bool)1, (bool)1>(int, const int3 *, gmx::SettleParameters, const float3 *, float3 *, PbcAiuc, float, float3 *, float *)
=========     and Read access at 0x1c90 in void gmx::settle_kernel<(bool)1, (bool)1>(int, const int3 *, gmx::SettleParameters, const float3 *, float3 *, PbcAiuc, float, float3 *, float *) [60 hazards]
=========     and Read access at 0x1ec0 in void gmx::settle_kernel<(bool)1, (bool)1>(int, const int3 *, gmx::SettleParameters, const float3 *, float3 *, PbcAiuc, float, float3 *, float *) [4 hazards]
========= 
...
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

We don't want data races on most popular([citation needed]) end-user GPUs.

## Possible fixes

Add `__syncwarp` call.

application called MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1) - process 1

closed_issues.title: Transformation Coordinates are broken
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Transformation coordinates are not working (and probably never worked). They have wrong interaction with pulling code, which prevents propagation of their forces onto real atoms of system.

**GROMACS version**

GROMACS 2022-beta1 and onwards until 2022.rc1

**Steps to reproduce**

[tc-bug.zip](/uploads/66125da2a9a5c50b79d295d29460d78f/tc-bug.zip)

Attached a simple system that shows problem: Na atom between two frozen Cl atoms (1nm apart). MDP tries to pull Na towards center of the system using transformation coordinate that defined as `x2-x1` where x1 - distance between Na and Cl1 and x2 - distance between Na and Cl2

**What is the current bug behavior?**

Instead of pulling it does nothing.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Na ion should be pulled towards the center of the system, where value of transformation coordinate would be 0

**Possible fixes**

I already have the fix (will post MR later today or tomorrow), it happens because `pull_potential` in pull.cpp treats transformation coordinate forces **after** all of the normal pulling coordinates, where it should do it other way around first all transformation coordinates and the normal coordinates. Also it has a problems if transformation coordinate gets its force from AWH, that I also fixing now.

closed_issues.title: gmxapi 0.3 Python package is not backwards compatible.
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

f30dbf44 introduced `gmxapi::MissingImplementationError` as the
replacement for `gmxapi::NotImplementedError`,
but inappropriately updated the exception thrown in a code block
specifically intended for older API versions, which do not have the new
exception.

The gmxapi Python package through 0.3.0b5 does not build on GROMACS installations older than f30dbf44, but should be compatible at least back through to 2020.0.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Activate a GROMACS installation from 2022rc1 or earlier and a Python 3.7+ venv, then
`pip install --pre gmxapi==0.3.0b5`

## For developers: Why is this important?

The gmxapi interfaces are pretty stable, so we shouldn't let a simple error break backwards compatibility at this point.

We will be advertising gmxapi 0.3 at a GROMACS workshop this week, and we should not have a broken version on PyPI at the time.

I am contributing a minimal quick fix. In a follow-up issue, we should consider more carefully the exceptions that can propagate through the Python package (and how they should be converted from C++ to Python exceptions). 

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

`pip install gmxapi` should work according to the installation instructions for GROMACS 2020 and later (at least until this is no longer feasible). Currently, the tagged prereleases for the gmxapi 0.3 package produce compiler errors on all tagged GROMACS releases.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

Compare https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/jobs/2059780590 to https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/jobs/2059773819

Note that https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/commits/mei-client-backwards-compatibility illustrates how we could screen for this sort of issue in the future. Unless it is deemed a high priority, though, I will wait to issue a corresponding MR until after the 2022.0 release.

## Possible fixes

1. Separate the sources for exporting exceptions bindings before and after libgmxapi version 0.3.1.
2. Export bindings for the deprecated `gmxapi::NotImplementedError` (until gmxapi 1.0).
3. Don't use features that don't exist yet (especially in version-conditional branches).

closed_issues.title: GmxApiTest.RunnerChainedMD fails with GPU direct communication
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

In the "chained MD" test of GmxApi, when using GPU direct communication, the second segment of the trajectory starts force calculation by trying to clear the Force buffer before the force buffer is allocated.

With threadMPI, this test binary always runs in a single rank (#4378), so the issue only affects libMPI builds.

- First segment:
  - Step 0:
    - `stepWork.useGpuFHalo` is disabled because we compute virial.
    - `stateGpu->reinit` is called, which allocates F and X buffers.
  - Step 1:
    - `stepWork.useGpuFHalo` is enabled, and the F buffer is allocated, so halo exchange works fine.
  - Step 2:
    - `stepWork.useGpuFHalo` is disabled because we compute virial, whatever.
- Second segment:
  - Step 2:
    - This is a new `do_md()` loop, so the GPU buffers are not initialized yet.
    - `stepWork.useGpuFHalo` is enabled because we don't compute virial.

closed_issues.title: GPU halo exchange with direct comm fails assertion in some regression tests
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

MR !2420 introduced a new assertion to prevent unsupported use of GPU-aware MPI.

This causes the regression tests complex/urea and complex/tip4pflex to fail when running on `dev-gpu03` with real MPI. The test harness by default sets the number of ranks to 8, which is too much. Tests pass with 2 and 4 ranks, fail with 8; urea fails with 6 ranks, while tip4pflex passes.

The error message correctly suggests using fewer ranks, so an end-user can deduce what is wrong, but the fact that `make check` fails is not nice.

## Exact steps to reproduce

On `dev-gpu03`:

- `module load cuda/11.5`
- `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/nethome/pszilard/programs/openmpi/4.1.2-cuda11.2_noucx/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`
- `export PATH=/nethome/pszilard/programs/openmpi/4.1.2-cuda11.2_noucx/bin:$PATH`
- `cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithAssert -DGMX_GPU=CUDA -DGMX_MPI=ON -DREGRESSIONTEST_DOWNLOAD=ON`
- `cmake --build . --target tests -- -j40`
- `GMX_ENABLE_DIRECT_GPU_COMM=1 make check`

Part of the output:

```
Abnormal return value for '/nethome/pszilard/programs/openmpi/4.1.2-cuda11.2_noucx/bin/mpiexec -np 8 -wdir /tmp/gromacs/build/mpi/tests/complex/tip4pflex gmx_mpi mdrun        -notunepme >mdrun.out 2>&1' was -1
FAILED. Check mdrun.out, md.log file(s) in tip4pflex for tip4pflex
Re-running tip4pflex using only CPU-based non-bonded kernels

Abnormal return value for '/nethome/pszilard/programs/openmpi/4.1.2-cuda11.2_noucx/bin/mpiexec -np 8 -wdir /tmp/gromacs/build/mpi/tests/complex/urea gmx_mpi mdrun        -notunepme >mdrun.out 2>&1' was -1
FAILED. Check mdrun.out, md.log file(s) in urea for urea
```

---

On a local machine with threadMPI and one GPU, the `complex/dd121` test fails with the same failed assertion after `make check` tries to run it with 12 tMPI ranks:

```

Abnormal return value for ' gmx mdrun -ntmpi 12       -notunepme >mdrun.out 2>&1' was -1
FAILED. Check mdrun.out, md.log file(s) in dd121 for dd121
```

## For developers: Why is this important?

We should not have `make check` fail.

## Possible fixes

We shall either change the default number of ranks or automatically use fewer ranks if the program fails, like we do in some other tests. Fixing the halo exchange to support multiple pulses in all dimensions would be nice, but out of scope for this release.

closed_issues.title: overcoming memory limitations in gmx hbond
closed_issues.description:
It was necessary to evaluate the lifetime of hydrogen bonds between solvent and solute in the model.
However, since the unit cell was relatively large, the hbond counted about 300 thousand donors and acceptors in it,
and allocate memory to ~ pow (10,11) pointers, naturally, could not. 
About this in hbond's help there is a corresponding note.
I looked at the source codes and concluded that matrix data storage is not effective, and, in most cases,
only a very small portion of the matrix will be used. I decided to try to replace the pointer matrix with 
std::map < std::pair<int, int>, t_hbond * >,
where the key in the map is a pair of donor and acceptor indices. A neat formal replacement in the code led to a fully functional version,
where the memory size limit has been pushed back. Next, replacing the search of row-columns of the matrix with a pass by the iterator on the map,
I also received a very noticeable increase in code performance, because in the trajectory under study there were only 40,000 donor-acceptor pairs instead of the maximum value of ~ pow(10,11) for sequental retrieval.
If the developers believe that such improvement in the functionality of gmx hbond is worthy of implementation, I am ready to patch the file gmx_hbond.cpp on the current version of master

closed_issues.title: GROMACS tries to use more OpenMP threads than GMX_OPENMP_MAX_THREADS
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

On a machine with 128 cores, some regression tests try to use 128 OpenMP threads, despite GROMACS being compiled with the default `GMX_OPENMP_MAX_THREADS` value of 64. They segfault.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Tested on `dt0` machine during Dardel hackathon. `gmx mdrun`, without setting `-ntomp` manually, tries to use too many cores in `complex/nacl` test and a few others.

## For developers: Why is this important?

GROMACS should at least print the nice warning, or, better yet, use valid number of threads.

closed_issues.title: Resolve / fix AWH likely inconsistent units
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

According to the discussion in !2361, AWH seems to use degrees as the units for awh1-dim1-start/end, while the documentation says radians, and if a cover-diameter is used, those units are not converted (meaning radians). 

## Exact steps to reproduce

See !2361

## For developers: Why is this important?

Inconsistent units for start/end vs. cover-diameter is a recipe for bugs, and we need the documentation to reflect the implementation.

## Possible fixes

Given that the standard pull package uses degrees everywhere, and AWH is apparently already partly doing that, by far the cleanest solution seems to standardize on that, even if it means cover-diameter will be reinterpreted.

closed_issues.title: Incorrect formula in reference manual
closed_issues.description:
The formula for the `3fd` virtual site given in the reference manual is incorrect and does not match the source code nor the diagram in Fig. 34.

The factor of (1-a) should not be there in either the numerator or denominator. The expression should be `r_ij + a r_jk`, not `(1-a) r_ij + a r_jk`.

closed_issues.title: Consider deafults and opimization of staged PME-PP communication
closed_issues.description:
Background: a major performance issue was observed with OpenMPI in PME-PP direct GPU->CPU communication on virial steps. For such transfers a workaround was implemented by staging the GPU->CPU copy GPU->GPU->CPU through the remote of the respective PP rank. During the review we identified that such an approach may have broader use to optimize PCIe link utilization (although potentially at the cost of added latency), but unconditional uniform use of such staging  may have unwanted side-effects e.g. when not all PME-PP communication is intra-note (see https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2377#note_817795404).
Therefore, more work is needed to assess what the default behavior should be with MPI an thread-MPI (and whether current default are correct), and whether MPI libraries will be / are already implementing such optimizations.

The following discussion from !2377 should be addressed:

- [ ] @pszilard started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2377#note_816908395):  (+6 comments)

    > Have you considered the use case when a PME-PP communication is inter-node? In such cases staging through the remote GPU may lead to copying to the remote GPU through the remote CPU's memory, then back to the remote CPU's memory in the final D2H.
    > 
    > Depending on the overhead of that we may want to check whether all PME-PP communication is intra-node before we pick this default?

closed_issues.title: gmx rms complains about missing atom masses even with -nomw flag
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

```
 -[no]mw                    (yes)
           Use mass weighting for superposition
```

Setting `-nomw` should force `gmx rms` to ignore atom masses. Yet it still tries to read them, and, if it fails, the program refuses to work.

Using an example from https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/3368#note_721329831:


```
Command line:
  gmx rms -s mol.pdb -f mol.xtc -f2 mol.xtc -o mol-rmsd.xvg -nomw

WARNING: second trajectory (-f2) useless when not calculating matrix (-m/-bm),
         will not read from mol.xtc

WARNING: Masses and atomic (Van der Waals) radii will be guessed
         based on residue and atom names, since they could not be
         definitively assigned from the information in your input
         files. These guessed numbers might deviate from the mass
         and radius of the atom type. Please check the output
         files if necessary.

Can not find mass in database for atom AR in residue 1 AR
Can not find mass in database for atom AR in residue 2 AR
Can not find mass in database for atom AR in residue 3 AR
Can not find mass in database for atom AR in residue 4 AR

-------------------------------------------------------
Program:     gmx rms, version 2022-beta2-dev-20220122-31f6f1eaf6
Source file: src/gromacs/fileio/confio.cpp (line 515)

Fatal error:
Masses were requested, but for some atom(s) masses could not be found in the
database. Use a tpr file as input, if possible, or add these atoms to the mass
database.

For more information and tips for troubleshooting, please check the GROMACS
website at http://www.gromacs.org/Documentation/Errors
-------------------------------------------------------
```

## Exact steps to reproduce

See above.

## For developers: Why is this important?

We have at least two user reports about poor guessing of the atomic masses (#3368, #4288), so the situation can happen relatively often.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

(1) `gmx rms -nomw` complains about missing atom masses.

(2) `gmx rms -nomw` works fine, because it does not need atom masses.

## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

See above.

## Possible fixes

If you have any suggestion, or even finished fix or merge request, that's awesome!

```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'cl::sycl::runtime_error'
  what():  Native API failed. Native API returns: -999 (Unknown OpenCL error code) -999 (Unknown OpenCL error code)
```

It happens at queue destruction only, so should not affect simulations. It affects tests (where queues are created and destroyed often), and the very end of the `mdrun`.

- Happens with oneAPI 2022.0.1 and open-source IntelLLVM 02b730102d7911ea466a2df6d8837971140d430f. Does not happen with oneAPI 2021.4.0
- Happens with SYCL_DEVICE_FILTER=level_zero:gpu, does not happen with OpenCL (the default).
- Setting `SYCL_PI_LEVEL_ZERO_BATCH_SIZE=1` seems to resolve the issue. Setting higher values (e.g., 8) reduces the probability of it happening.
- Oversubscribing GPU with high `-ntmpi` value increases the likelihood of the problem.
- Happens on multiple devices (Gen9 and Gen11 iGPU, XeMax dGPU).
- Sometimes, the program deadlocks instead of throwing an exception, with stacktrace deep in `libze_intel_gpu.so`). Rarely, it happens even if the L0 device was not actively used, being poked during GPU enumeration is enough (which always happens during the program start).
  - Setting `SYCL_DEVICE_FILTER=opencl:gpu` hides the L0 backend, and resolves the issue.
- Sometimes, the program fails with `Abort was called at 178 line in file: ../neo/opencl/source/os_interface/linux/drm_command_stream.inl`, from within `piQueueRelease`, instead.
- Adding `stream_.wait()` to `DeviceStream::~DeviceStream` leads either to a deadlock (on `piQueueRelease`), or to the same exception being thrown from `cl::sycl::detail::queue_impl::wait` instead of the destructor.
- Happens with libze_intel_gpu.so.1.2.22192, libze_intel_gpu.so.1.2.21786, libze_intel_gpu.so.1.1.20609.

## Exact steps to reproduce

- Configure GROMACS with oneAPI 2022.0.1: `cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx -DGMX_GPU=SYCL -DGMX_GPU_NB_CLUSTER_SIZE=4 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DGMX_FFT_LIBRARY=mkl -DREGRESSIONTEST_DOWNLOAD=ON`
- Run `SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=1 SYCL_DEVICE_FILTER=level_zero:gpu make check`
  - `SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT` is not necessary for this bug to reproduce, it's here to speed-up the tests, see #4218.

## Possible fixes

We can force setting `SYCL_PI_LEVEL_ZERO_BATCH_SIZE=1`, or at least warn the user?

closed_issues.title: Distance restraint force is calculated in an unexpected way in case of negative prefactor
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Forces and for distance restraints are calculated in the file
src/gromacs/listed_forces/disre.cpp
in the function ta_disres(). The prefactor for the forces is called k0. In an itp file with distance restraints, the ninth entry in any row is a free parameter for the restraint force. Usually, this parameter is supposed to be positive and if this is the case, everything works fine. However, if the parameter is negative, as in this example:

[gly10_alpha_small.pdb](/uploads/8adabd3aa15ea92fa64c7ec72695a3fd/gly10_alpha_small.pdb)

[grompp.mdp](/uploads/8a775edeec6d24607d8dc850b3978b39/grompp.mdp)

[test.itp](/uploads/19c286f0ecbe38283dfdad868293ab62/test.itp)

[topol.top](/uploads/5434fa94ffb1e1dc2988e9159c409f91/topol.top)

[topol.tpr](/uploads/109e747b32d480095c7b190e439f74d2/topol.tpr)

the force calculation is not as in the manual:

https://manual.gromacs.org/documentation/2019/reference-manual/functions/restraints.html#distance-restraints

While negative prefactors to a distance restraint may seem like a nonsensical thing to do, this is something which is of relevance for my use case. At any rate, I think as a matter of principle, the code should do what the manual says even in this case.

Since there seems to be no canonical way of outputting restraint forces, I have checked this bug only by reading the code.

**GROMACS version**

The releases release-2020, release-2021 and release-2022 are all affected. My version is:

    GROMACS version:    2022-beta1-dev-20211028-d0593a5845
    GIT SHA1 hash:      d0593a58454b855259dff740cb376a3d43f6c620
    Precision:          mixed
    Memory model:       64 bit
    MPI library:        thread_mpi
    OpenMP support:     enabled (GMX_OPENMP_MAX_THREADS = 64)
    GPU support:        disabled
    SIMD instructions:  AVX2_256
    CPU FFT library:    fftw-3.3.8-sse2-avx-avx2-avx2_128
    GPU FFT library:    none
    RDTSCP usage:       enabled
    TNG support:        enabled
    Hwloc support:      hwloc-2.1.0
    Tracing support:    disabled
    C compiler:         /usr/bin/cc GNU 9.3.0
    C compiler flags:   -mavx2 -mfma -Wall -Wno-unused -Wunused-value -Wunused-parameter -Wextra -Wno-sign-compare -Wpointer-arith -Wundef -Werror=stringop-truncation -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -Wno-array-bounds -O3 -DNDEBUG
    C++ compiler:       /usr/bin/c++ GNU 9.3.0
    C++ compiler flags: -mavx2 -mfma -Wall -Wextra -Wpointer-arith -Wmissing-declarations -Wundef -Wstringop-truncation -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -Wno-array-bounds -fopenmp -O3 -DNDEBUG

**Steps to reproduce**

This problem cannot be easily seen from simulation results, however it is obvious from reading the code.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

In the example above, distance restraint forces will be 1000*(r-r_1) instead of 1000*(r_2−r_1), with r taken from traj_comp.xtc.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Forces should be 1000*(r_2−r_1).

**Possible fixes**

In the file src/gromacs/listed_forces/disre.cpp replace the following line appears twice (line 564 and 579):

    f_scal = std::max(f_scal, fmax_scal);

The bug could be resolved by replacing this line on both occurrences with

    if (-f_scal/k0 > up2-up1) {
        f_scal = fmax_scal;
    }

(The somewhat awkward term -f_scal/k0 is necessary to account for all the different possibilities for the calculation of f_scal in the function.)

closed_issues.title: Calculation of distance restraint energies is faulty
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Forces and energies for distance restraints are calculated in the file
src/gromacs/listed_forces/disre.cpp
in the function ta_disres(). While forces are calculated as described in the manual
https://manual.gromacs.org/documentation/2019/reference-manual/functions/restraints.html#distance-restraints
the calculation of the energy ignores the parameter up2. This means that if a distance restraint is strongly violated, the energy can be vastly overestimated. Since this does not affect the dynamics (forces are calculated correctly) this bug is not terrible. Nevertheless it should be fixed.

I have checked this bug both by numerical experiments as well as by reading the code.

**GROMACS version**

    GROMACS version:    2022-beta1-dev-20211028-d0593a5845
    GIT SHA1 hash:      d0593a58454b855259dff740cb376a3d43f6c620
    Precision:          mixed
    Memory model:       64 bit
    MPI library:        thread_mpi
    OpenMP support:     enabled (GMX_OPENMP_MAX_THREADS = 64)
    GPU support:        disabled
    SIMD instructions:  AVX2_256
    CPU FFT library:    fftw-3.3.8-sse2-avx-avx2-avx2_128
    GPU FFT library:    none
    RDTSCP usage:       enabled
    TNG support:        enabled
    Hwloc support:      hwloc-2.1.0
    Tracing support:    disabled
    C compiler:         /usr/bin/cc GNU 9.3.0
    C compiler flags:   -mavx2 -mfma -Wall -Wno-unused -Wunused-value -Wunused-parameter -Wextra -Wno-sign-compare -Wpointer-arith -Wundef -Werror=stringop-truncation -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -Wno-array-bounds -O3 -DNDEBUG
    C++ compiler:       /usr/bin/c++ GNU 9.3.0
    C++ compiler flags: -mavx2 -mfma -Wall -Wextra -Wpointer-arith -Wmissing-declarations -Wundef -Wstringop-truncation -Wno-missing-field-initializers -fexcess-precision=fast -funroll-all-loops -Wno-array-bounds -fopenmp -O3 -DNDEBUG

**Steps to reproduce**

[gly10_alpha_small.pdb](/uploads/ccdf5fabef0eb0cd98ccdf68f83ac9b0/gly10_alpha_small.pdb)

[test.itp](/uploads/ff35b193bf40cb0545a7cad3102a14e7/test.itp)

[topol.top](/uploads/e903878391df1a0479870d1be9d7213e/topol.top)

[topol.tpr](/uploads/d12e11d61fe5a7917bb4c9906a0b76b4/topol.tpr)

[grompp.mdp](/uploads/f9e700615bbfcb7d571942290fc342db/grompp.mdp)

This simple example system should take ~30 seconds to run.

**What is the current bug behavior?**

In the example above, distance restraint energies from ener.edr will be 500*(r-r_1)^2 instead of 500*(r_2−r_1)*(2*r−r_2−r_1), with r taken from traj_comp.xtc.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Energies should be 500*(r_2−r_1)*(2*r−r_2−r_1).

**Possible fixes**

In the file src/gromacs/listed_forces/disre.cpp replace the line (515)

    vtot += 0.5 * k0 * gmx::square(tav_viol) * pairFac;

with

    if (tav_viol > up2-up1) {
        vtot += 0.5 * k0 * (up2-up1) * (2*tav_viol+up1-up2) * pairFac;
    } else {
        vtot += 0.5 * k0 * gmx::square(tav_viol) * pairFac;
    }

closed_issues.title: `pytest --rm success ...` not working as intended
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

`gmxapi.testsupport` adds support for a `--rm` option to pytest. The value of `success` is supposed to remove the testing temporary directory only when a test succeeds. At some point the logic seems to have broken, and the temporary directory is always removed unless `--rm never`.

**GROMACS version**

2020 and newer, but possibly dependent on `pytest` version.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Install gmxapi, or build GROMACS with `-DGMX_PYTHON_PACKAGE=ON` and change to the `${CMAKE_BUILD_DIR}/python_packaging/src/gmxapi_staging` directory.
2. `python -m pytest <other pytest args> --rm success /path/to/python_packaging/src/test/<failing_test>`

**What is the current bug behavior?**

pytest `--rm never` works as expected, but `--rm success` proceeds as if `--rm always`

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

As with `--rm never`, the temporary directory for a failed test should not be removed. Unless suppressed, a warning like the following would be visible:

```
===================================================================================== warnings summary ======================================================================================
test_subgraph.py::test_subgraph_simulation_extension
  .../python_packaging/src/gmxapi_staging/gmxapi/testsupport.py:194: UserWarning: Temporary directory not removed: /<tmp_dir_path_prefix>/tmp6e9mml_d
```

**Possible fixes**

pytest provides `tmp_path` and `tmp_path_factory` fixtures that do most of what we need, but which have a different retention policy that avoids some of the other issues we've run into. We can build on these fixtures, instead.

Issues avoided:
* race conditions in directory removal
* custom policies on temporary directory retention
* extra custom command line argument processing
* appropriate reporting of the temporary directory path and status

closed_issues.title: Provide gmxapi package data file even for "editable installs"
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Restore support for "editable installs" via `pip install -e ...` or `setup.py develop`.

Reliance on `gmxconfig.json` means that `pip install -e` and `setup.py develop` do not result in a completely valid importable package.

Instead of a full re-build->re-install, you could copy the generated `gmxconfig.json` from the build directory to the source directory after attempting an "editable install." Let's not do that anymore.

**Use cases**
Simplify development of the gmxapi Python package. Allow faster iteration when testing updates locally.

**Detailed description**

Python is only just achieving a standardized definition of a an "editable install" with the acceptance of PEP 660, but it is not yet widely implemented.

`distutils` and `setuptools` have traditionally provided a `develop` command for `setup.py`, which is also used for `pip install -e`.

Since we began relying on a package data file generated at build time, the gmxapi Python package has not worked in "develop" mode without manually copying `gmxconfig.json` from the build directory to the source directory.

Since the future of editable installs was uncertain, this didn't seem like a priority. Now that PEP 660 is accepted, we might as well support editable installs again. However, neither PEP 660 nor the distutils tradition offer guidance for exposing _generated_ package data files to the editable install. We can follow the model of the distutils build_ext until better guidelines are available.

Example:

```
(gromacs2023) MacBook-Pro:gromacs2023 eric$ . ~/install/gromacs-tmpi-debug/bin/GMXRC
(gromacs2023) MacBook-Pro:gromacs2023 eric$ pip install -e python_packaging/src/
Obtaining file:///Users/eric/develop/CLionProjects/gromacs2023/python_packaging/src
  Installing build dependencies ... done
  Checking if build backend supports build_editable ... done
  Getting requirements to build wheel ... done
  Preparing metadata (pyproject.toml) ... done
Requirement already satisfied: packaging in /Users/eric/.virtualenvs/gromacs2023/lib/python3.7/site-packages (from gmxapi==0.3.0) (21.3)
Requirement already satisfied: networkx>=2.0 in /Users/eric/.virtualenvs/gromacs2023/lib/python3.7/site-packages (from gmxapi==0.3.0) (2.6.3)
Requirement already satisfied: pybind11 in /Users/eric/.virtualenvs/gromacs2023/lib/python3.7/site-packages (from gmxapi==0.3.0) (2.9.1)
Requirement already satisfied: numpy>1.7 in /Users/eric/.virtualenvs/gromacs2023/lib/python3.7/site-packages (from gmxapi==0.3.0) (1.21.5)
Requirement already satisfied: pyparsing!=3.0.5,>=2.0.2 in /Users/eric/.virtualenvs/gromacs2023/lib/python3.7/site-packages (from packaging->gmxapi==0.3.0) (3.0.7)
Installing collected packages: gmxapi
  Running setup.py develop for gmxapi
Successfully installed gmxapi-0.3.0
(gromacs2023) MacBook-Pro:gromacs2023 eric$ python -m pytest python_packaging/src/test/
```

is followed by lots of errors like

```
...
E           FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/Users/eric/develop/CLionProjects/gromacs2023/python_packaging/src/gmxapi/gmxconfig.json'

../../../.pyenv/versions/3.7.7/lib/python3.7/importlib/resources.py:125: FileNotFoundError
...
```

without the patch.

**Disposition / Resolution**

@eirrgang has provided a patch, but the issue is probably not urgent enough to prioritize for gmxapi 0.3.0. This issue could go in a gmxapi 0.4 Milestone (or 0.3.1) or into a release target Milestone, pending acceptance.

closed_issues.title: Fix inappropriately named gmxapi exception.
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

* `gmxapi.exceptions.NotImplementedError` shadows a Python built-in exception.
* In gmxapi (and GROMACS), `NotImplementedError` has different semantics than in Python.

**GROMACS version**

GROMACS 2018+. (gmxapi 0.0.7+)

**What is the current bug behavior?**

* `from gmxapi.exceptions import NotImplementedError` is a reasonable thing for a developer to do within a module, but would then hide the built-in `NotImplementedError`.
* If a user triggers a bug (or encounters an incompletely implemented code path), they (or a GROMACS developer handling a bug report) may be grossly mislead when looking for the cause of a `NotImplementedError` exception.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

`libgromacs`, and, by extension, `libgmxapi` and the `gmxapi` Python package have used `NotImplementedError` to indicate an incompletely implemented code path or feature: either a logical state that was unanticipated or which simply hasn't been handled yet.

However, in Python, we expect `NotImplementedError` to mean something analogous to a pure-virtual function in an abstract base class.

**Possible fixes**

The Python `gmxapi.exceptions.NotImplementedError` should be renamed to `MissingImplementationError`.

The following discussion from !2337 should be addressed:

- [ ] @sebastian2802 started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2337#note_786947965):  (+1 comment)

    > ... I'd therefore suggest to fix the `NotImplementedError` in a separate commit but in all places then.

The `gmxapi._gmxapi.NotImplementedError` Python exception from the C++ bindings module should be renamed, as well, since it can also appear to a Python environment.

The `::gmxapi::NotImplementedError` to which `gmxapi._gmxapi.NotImplementedError` is bound should probably be renamed to avoid confusion.

`::gmx::NotImplementedError` should probably be left alone.

**Alternatives**

The Python exception name change is offered for gmxapi 0.3 in !2337 with the proposal to defer further C++ changes to gmxapi 0.4.

closed_issues.title: Note caveats when building client software in the presence of overlapping GROMACS installations.
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

If someone installs GROMACS to a location where GROMACS is already installed, the consequences of overwriting the CMake imported-target support may be non-obvious or confusing.

## Exact steps to reproduce

1. Configure and install GROMACS.
2. Choose different configure-time options for MPI or floating point precision. Rebuild and install to the same location without removing the previous installation.
3. `/path/to/gromacs/share/cmake/gmxapi/*cmake` reflect the most recent installation only. Libraries with different suffixes remain in `/path/to/gromacs/lib/` from previous installations, but `find_package(gmxapi)` is not aware of them.
4. `pip install gmxapi` will use the CMake target produced by `find_package(gmxapi)`, regardless of other invocation details such as CMake toolchain/hints file or GROMACS_DIR value. However, the result is undefined behavior that may not produce an error right away (or ever), though the resulting installation may not be as the user expected.

## For developers: Why is this important?

Ref https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/4324: 

> > I hope this isn't a common source of confusion. Would it help if `gmxapi-config.cmake` provided some additional output about the build configuration it is associated with?
> 
> Definitely one way to deal with it. An obvious warning about multiple installations in one directory on https://manual.gromacs.org/current/gmxapi/userguide/install.html will help, too, I guess.
> 

## Possible fixes

In the short term, we can update the "cmake hints" and "troubleshooting" sections of `gmxapi/userguide/install`

In the longer term, depending on whether GROMACS wants to embrace or discourage overlapping installations, we could update the CMake infrastructure to support or prevent multiple `libgmxapi*` targets to be imported by `find_package(gmxapi)`, link multiple GROMACS ABIs from one `libgmxapi`, define multiple gmxapi CMake package modules, or add safety checks to prevent ambiguous installations. This also related to the long-term disposition of `libgromacs`, the legacy API, future public API, and reconciliation of the separate `libgmxapi`/`libgromacs` libraries.

These decisions would need to be reconciled in other places, such as Spack recipes and packaging strategies for the several Linux distributions. There is also a question of what should happen when someone does `pip install gmxapi`, and what the mechanisms should be for customizing the dependency resolution.

closed_issues.title: libgromacs INSTALL_NAME_DIR should not refer to the client location
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

`libgromacs*dylib` advertises its identity incorrectly on OS X (due to `CMAKE_INSTALL_NAME_DIR`), leading to potential problems resolving dynamic linking instructions.

INSTALL_NAME_DIR

Ref: https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_tgt/INSTALL_NAME_DIR.html

**GROMACS version**

Since GROMACS 2019.

**Steps to reproduce**

Perform a regular installation on Darwin / OS X, without disabling shared objects.

`otool -D /path/to/lib/libgromacs*.dylib` shows `@loader_path/../lib/libgromacs_mpi.6.dylib` (or `otool -l` will show it for LC_ID_DYLIB)

`otool -l some_client_program` will show `@loader_path/../lib/libgromacs_d.6.dylib` in a `LC_LOAD_DYLIB` section.

For a more specific example, consider the `sample_restraint` test binaries. In the gromacs 2021 repository,
```
    . /path/to/gromacs/bin/GMXRC
    cd python_packaging/sample_restraint
    mkdir build
    cd build
    GROMACS_DIR=/path/to/gromacs cmake .. -DGMXAPI_EXTENSION_DOWNLOAD_PYBIND=ON -DDOWNLOAD_GOOGLETEST=ON -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=/path/to/gromacs/share/cmake/gromacs/gromacs-toolchain.cmake
    make -j8
    ctest
```
**What is the current bug behavior?**

Client programs are not portable (unless moved in tandem with the GROMACS installation).

Client programs produce runtime errors such as the following.

`dyld: Library not loaded: @loader_path/../lib/libgromacs.6.dylib`

The problem can be mitigated by setting DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, but wrappers like `ctest` may remove this from the environment.

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

The CMake support for libgromacs should be sufficient for client software to configure sufficient linking instructions such that DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH is not necessary.

```
otool -D /path/to/libgromacs.dylib 
/path/to/libgromacs.dylib:
@rpath/libgromacs.6.dylib
```

```
otool -l some_client_program
...
          cmd LC_LOAD_DYLIB
      cmdsize 72
         name @rpath/libgromacs*.dylib
...
          cmd LC_RPATH
      cmdsize 72
         path /path/to/gromacs-installation/lib 
```

**Possible fixes**

Remove `set(CMAKE_INSTALL_NAME_DIR ${CMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH})` from the CMakeLists.txt

playing with a simple model system for free energy calculations
i came across an issue, possibly related to pair-list generation,
and the PBC implementation, when free-energy=yes.

closed_issues.title: Consider consolidating gmxapi test jobs and GitLab CI rules.
closed_issues.description:
This issue continues a discussion from !2296, describing an alternative to #4317.

The following discussion from !2296 should be addressed:

- [ ] @eirrgang started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2296#note_756883590):  (+3 comments)

    > Having explicit rules seems easier...

Maybe. Others have expressed displeasure at the abundance of rules and job definitions (in the yaml), and scripts (in `admin/ci-scripts`).

The alternative would be to consolidate on a single `.rules:merge-requests` (to reduce the amount of GitLab magic and so that gmxapi jobs would be less of an outlier), and consolidate the jobs that vary primarily in the variant of the rule they use.

Logic that needs to be different for different versions of the client software would no longer be separated into separate scripts. Logic for old versions would no longer be as clearly static. This would mean that it might be slightly harder to catch ourselves before changing behavior for an older version that was intended to be final.

The scripts would have slightly more logic in them, but the logic would be more self-contained.

@acmnpv and @mark.j.abraham are the main people who have dealt with similar merges and CI updates in the past.

closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

Nbnxm kernel is running with different global size for CUDA (2974 blocks) and SYCL (3198 blocks) that may lead to ~7% of SYCL performance degradation due to larger number of threads. In both cases GMX_GPU_NB_CLUSTER_SIZE=8 is used.
Also the difference in global sizes complicates direct SYCL vs. CUDA comparison.

**GROMACS version**
```
GROMACS version:    2022-beta1-dev-20211129-3e3acff3f2-dirty
GIT SHA1 hash:      3e3acff3f2dcd429b630f3eaf40570c21a566e64 (dirty)

GPU FFT library:    unknown

Hwloc support:      disabled

C compiler:         /home/avgorshk/compiler/llvm/build/bin/clang Clang 14.0.0
C compiler flags:   -mavx2 -mfma -pthread -Wall -Wno-unused -Wunused-value -Wunused-parameter -Wno-missing-field-initializers -O3 -DNDEBUG

```
**Steps to reproduce**

To see the difference one can run benchMEM workload for CUDA and SYCL builds, and use NVidia NSight for Compute to get kernel global sizes, e.g.:

closed_issues.title: Running pipelines on MRs from forks
closed_issues.description:
**Summary**

We want to be able to manually run the CI to test and merge MRs that are created from a fork of the GROMACS repo.

**Use cases**

Several times we had an MR from an external contributor, we had to add them to the GROMACS project and ask them to create a new MR or do it ourselves: 

- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2248
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/1909
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/125
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/1532
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/1119
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/1034
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/558
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/376
- https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/152

**Impact**

It will make external contributions more straightforward. 

It will also avoid us having to add external, often one-off, contributors to GROMACS project, thus slightly improving the security.

**Detailed description**

We occasionally have MRs from external contributors. Since they can not push a branch to the main GROMACS repo, they create an MR from their fork.

GitLab does not automatically run pipelines on forks, to avoid abuse of the CI infrastructure.

But we want to be able to manually trigger CI runs, and be able to merge such MRs.

Currently, we have to add the contributor to the GROMACS project and ask them to push their branch there and create a new MR.

Apparently, GitLab supports it: https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/pipelines/merge_request_pipelines.html#run-pipelines-in-the-parent-project-for-merge-requests-from-a-forked-project

But for some reason, we don't have the "Pipelines" tab in the external MRs, so no way to do what the documentation suggests:

> Parent project members with at least the Developer role can create pipelines in the parent project for merge requests from a forked project. In the merge request, go to the Pipelines tab and select Run pipeline.

**Summary**

muparser test is not disabled when -DBUILD_TESTING=off.
This leads to a cmake error during gromacs compilation.

**GROMACS version**

```
Command line:
  gmx -quiet --version

GROMACS version:    2022-beta1-dev-20211130-6fae6b2621
GIT SHA1 hash:      6fae6b26211f78638aadba339a54645051a04f8d
```

**Steps to reproduce**


From an empty "build" folder inside the gromacs repository,

`cmake ../  -DBUILD_TESTING=off  -DREGRESSIONTEST_DOWNLOAD=off`


**What is the current bug behavior?**

On using the above command, the following cmake error can be seen.

```
CMake Error at src/external/muparser/CMakeLists.txt:143 (add_dependencies):
  Cannot add target-level dependencies to non-existent target "tests".
 
  The add_dependencies works for top-level logical targets created by the
  add_executable, add_library, or add_custom_target commands.  If you want to
  add file-level dependencies see the DEPENDS option of the add_custom_target
  and add_custom_command commands.

.
.
.
-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
```

**What did you expect the correct behavior to be?**

Do not expect any testing related error when the -DBUILD_TESTING=off.

**Possible fixes**

closed_issues.title: Use CMake to find TBB
closed_issues.description:
It is necessary to handle linking of Thread Building Blocks (TBB) to use many of the parallel components of the STL. This can lead to a very large number of OMP loops being replaced by, e.g., std::transform and std::copy. All the compilers we support for release 2023 will also have support for TBB, but linking sadly does not happen by default. Handling this linking at CMake time should be as simple as `find_package(TBB)`, potentially with a few extra steps in some cases.

This issue is meant as a starting place for discussion about the pros and cons (if any) of including TBB so that parallel STL algorithms can be used.

closed_issues.title: Fix broken CUDA 11 CI images
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The test failures in the Clang 12 + CUDA 11.4.1 CI builds are caused by an (unnecessary?) step in the image build process.

## Exact steps to reproduce

Start a container with the image, run ldconfig, and try to run a CUDA sample:
```
$ docker run -it --gpus 1 --rm registry.gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/ci-ubuntu-20.04-llvm-12-cuda-11.4.1-hipsycl-7a309b808-rocm-4.3:latest /bin/bash
# ldconfig
# git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuda-samples.git
# cd cuda-samples/Samples/matrixMul
# make
# ../../bin/x86_64/linux/release/matrixMul
[Matrix Multiply Using CUDA] - Starting...
CUDA error at ../../Common/helper_cuda.h:795 code=803(cudaErrorSystemDriverMismatch) "cudaGetDeviceCount(&device_count)"
```

That is the same error that shows up in the CI pipeline, e.g. https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/jobs/1833778137

The cause for this issue is a combination of two things. The CUDA images come with the package `cuda-compat-11-4` installed, which puts driver files for forward-compatibility (only supported on Tesla GPUs) in the directory `/usr/local/cuda-11.4/compat`. Then this step:
 https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/master/admin/containers/scripted_gmx_docker_builds.py#L437
blindly creates links for all these files in `/usr/local/cuda/lib64`.

## Possible fixes

Removing the driver links fixes the issue:
```
# unlink /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so
# unlink /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.1 
# unlink /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so.470.57.02
# ../../bin/x86_64/linux/release/matrixMul
[Matrix Multiply Using CUDA] - Starting...
GPU Device 0: "Pascal" with compute capability 6.1

MatrixA(320,320), MatrixB(640,320)
Computing result using CUDA Kernel...
done
Performance= 445.02 GFlop/s, Time= 0.295 msec, Size= 131072000 Ops, WorkgroupSize= 1024 threads/block
Checking computed result for correctness: Result = PASS
```

Can someone comment on why all these links are created in the first place?

    > It is less than ideal that we have to duplicate these calls (in fact this will be the third time we call `pme_receive_force_ener()` in `do_force()`), but this is the straightforward solution so at least on the release branch this is the appropriate fix. closed_issues.title: gmx rms does not recognize certain ions in PDB files
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

When running `gmx rms` on PDB files that contain Ions such as Magnesium or Zinc, the following error message is shown:

```
Can not find mass in database for atom ZN in residue 719 ZN
Can not find mass in database for atom MG in residue 721 MG
```


## Exact steps to reproduce

 1. Obtain structure from 6ZPQ as PDB file from the RCSB PDB or the file attached here.
 2. Run `gmx rms -s 6ZPQ.pdb -f 6ZPQ.pdb`

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

(1) The following output is generated:

```
Can not find mass in database for atom ZN in residue 719 ZN
Can not find mass in database for atom MG in residue 721 MG
Can not find mass in database for atom ZN in residue 715 ZN
Can not find mass in database for atom MG in residue 717 MG
Can not find mass in database for atom ZN in residue 712 ZN
Can not find mass in database for atom MG in residue 714 MG
Can not find mass in database for atom ZN in residue 715 ZN
```


(2) Expected: RMS is calculated between files


## Relevant input files, logs and/or screenshots

[6ZPQ.pdb](/uploads/e4ef7cebcb7b10933bb4d379c76f0943/6ZPQ.pdb)

## Possible fixes

It seems that `gmx rms` uses case sensitive comparison to look for the atoms in the `atommass.dat` file, so "MG" and "ZN" can not be found despite "Mg" and "Zn" being present.

When searching the `atommass.dat` file for atom names, use a case insensitive comparison.

closed_issues.title: sample_restraint CMake scripting breaks with current googletest source.
closed_issues.description:
## Summary

The `-DDOWNLOAD_GOOGLETEST=ON` option for the sample project no longer works correctly due to upstream changes in `googletest` distribution. This is expected to affect all releases (all repository branches).

## Exact steps to reproduce

See, for example, https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/jobs/1785962077, and https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/master/admin/ci-scripts/build-and-test-sample_restraint-2021.sh

## For developers: Why is this important?

The most immediately observable affect is the failure of CI jobs, but it also indicates that the documentation for the sample code may need updates.

## If this is a bug, (1) what happens, and (2) what did you expect to happen?

Note the error:

    [ 22%] Performing download step (git clone) for 'googletest'
    Cloning into 'googletest-src'...
    fatal: invalid reference: master
    CMake Error at googletest-download/googletest-prefix/tmp/googletest-gitclone.cmake:40 (message):
     Failed to checkout tag: 'master'

## Possible fixes

The two quick solutions:
- [x] reference the local copy of googletest sources available from the GROMACS repo, which should be available to the job in `/builds/gromacs/gromacs` instead of using `-DDOWNLOAD_GOOGLETEST=ON` in regular CI (!2211)
- [x] update the behavior of `-DDOWNLOAD_GOOGLETEST=ON` to correctly use the googletest repository and/or pin to a specific googletest release (!2204)

For a long-term solution, we can review the googletest project docs for best practices on new projects so that we can appropriately suggest and test a primary use case that we can advocate for users.

closed_issues.description:
The `output.trajectory` attribute of `gmxapi.mdrun` references was hard-coded to look for `traj.trr` in the resolution to #3144.

closed_issues.title: Allow all arbitrary runtime arguments to gmxapi.mdrun
closed_issues.description:
gmxapi.mdrun is severely limited by a combination of
* slow progress on API features for simulation and work load input
* shifting behavior with respect to mdrun command line options

Since these are not likely to be resolved soon, we might as well let `gmxapi.mdrun` accept arbitrary command line arguments, subject only to the usual mdrun user input handling.

The `-s` option (TPR file) is still reserved, since it is essential that the API instrumentation manage the main input source.

The initial merge request must patch the libgmxapi C++ code to allow for the possibility of all other user-provided options, while guaranteeing that a trajectory output and a checkpoint output will be available at a knowable location.

(A follow-up merge request adds a *runtime_args* key word argument to `gmxapi.mdrun()`, accepting a dictionary of input.)

This will mean having the MR ready by November ~5, since we need another 10 working days for code review, and ~5 days for testing before doing the beta. 

2. Since somebody is working actively on it, that person should have the issue assigned, and with ~10 days left, it is likely difficult for anybody to be responsible for more than 10 issues.

3. Since this is our last beta, any new code that doesn't make this milestone won't be in the release. For the release candidates we will ONLY add fixes.

closed_issues.title: 2021.4 - regression in GammaDistributionTest.Output on some architectures
closed_issues.description:
Debian autobuilds of 2021.4 on *some* architectures (so far: arm64, powerpc, ppc64, ppc64el, and s390x) have a new, just-over-the-tolerance error on one test, in double precision only:

```32: [----------] 4 tests from GammaDistributionTest
32: [ RUN      ] GammaDistributionTest.Output
32: ./src/testutils/refdata.cpp:927: Failure
32:    In item: /GammaDistribution/[28]
32:     Actual: 24.49245196388771
32:  Reference: 24.492451963887692
32: Difference: 1.77636e-14 (5 double-prec. ULPs, rel. 7.25e-16)
32:  Tolerance: abs. 8.88178e-16, 4 ULPs
32: [  FAILED  ] GammaDistributionTest.Output (1 ms)
```

The same test passes in an identical build environment with 2021.3, and also passes with 2021.4 on other architectures tested, including the 32-bit ARM builds.  Single-precision passes across the board.

Example build logs:
- https://buildd.debian.org/status/fetch.php?pkg=gromacs&arch=arm64&ver=2021.4-1&stamp=1636246899&raw=0
- https://buildd.debian.org/status/fetch.php?pkg=gromacs&arch=ppc64el&ver=2021.4-1&stamp=1636245238&raw=0
- https://buildd.debian.org/status/fetch.php?pkg=gromacs&arch=s390x&ver=2021.4-1&stamp=1636246939&raw=0

milestone.description:
The very last scheduled patch release for 2021 series.

All scheduled changes/bugfixes for release-2021 have to be in before the end of the year (thus the due date). After that we plan to wait 1-2 weeks and also include any major issues we find after having released version 2022.

After this deadline, the only changes going into release-2021 will be fixes for major bugs with major risks for silently corrupting scientific results for large numbers of users.

closed_issues.title: StatePropagatorDataGpu is initialized/reinitialized incorrectly
Malformed safety check may affect gmxapi restartability.
closed_issues.description:
A typo may have prevented gmxapi simulations from continuing from checkpoints
after being interrupted. It is possible this bug has not been encountered, but
a script containing gmxapi simulation instructions that is interrupted and then
re-run without alteration should be able to continue a partially complete simulation
from its checkpoint file. The typo should be corrected.

closed_issues.title: Let CI image build script just produce commands rather than run them.
closed_issues.description:
Follow-up from "Add GROMACS-CP2K build CI job #3172".
The following discussion from !2096 should be addressed:

- [ ] @eirrgang started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/merge_requests/2096#note_722142914): 

    > `buildall.sh` is becoming less useful with really long builds. I will propose an update in a follow-up change.

# Proposal

Generate and echo various lists of commands that might be needed, and let the user copy-paste those that are actually needed.

closed_issues.title: Change !545 breaks mdrun without MPI or THREAD_MPI, and all reference builds
closed_issues.description:
The change !545 that should "Improve naming and docs" introduces changes in the logic of communicators that causes all Gromacs builds where both MPI and THREAD_MPI are disabled to always fail with a critical assert at the start of mdrun.

The relevant change seems to be around line 852 in runner.cpp where communicator is now checked to be different from MPI_COMM_NULL, rather than identical to MPI_COMM_WORLD.

Since the reason for changing the logic isn't documented in the comment, I presume this can be reverted tomorrow unless we hear back from @eirrgang until then.

This is currently making it impossible to update our reference values in the regression tests (since those need a reference build type, where all MPI options are disabled), which in turn is holding up %2021.4, so it's pretty urgent.

Using CMake with Make or Ninja makes no difference. NBLIB API installation is enabled:

$ grep NBLIB CMakeCache.txt
GMX_INSTALL_NBLIB_API:BOOL=ON

The headers that get installed are:

```
$ ls ~/programs/gromacs/include/nblib/*

closed_issues.title: Impove Intel MPI detection
closed_issues.description:
Currently, MPI detection fails when using oneAPI ICX/ICPX compilers even if Intel MPI is installed and even with latest CMake 3.21.3.

The guide at https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/technical/compile-and-run-mpi-programs-using-dpcpp-language.html suggest two options: use `I_MPI_CXX` env. var and `mpicxx` wrapper, or copy flags manually from `mpiicpc -show` (`mpiicpc` itself will use old Intel compiler).

Intel's `mpicxx` wrapper does not support `I_MPI_CXX=icpx`, and `I_MPI_CXX=dpcpp` does not support OpenMP, so we're left with the second option.

As a proof-of-concept, `cmake ../.. -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=icx -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=icpx -DGMX_MPI=ON -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="$(mpiicpc -show | tr -d \" | sed 's/icpc //')"` works (unless oneAPI installation path has spaces in it).

It must be integrated into CMake properly if we want to use Intel MPI, because it's not nice to force end-users to do that.

closed_issues.title: Energy correction term and possibly the pressure correction for dispersion interactions have regressed between GROMACS 2020.6 and 2021.1.
closed_issues.description:
As part of a study, a group of us have been comparing the long range correction terms in energy and pressure between multiple simulation engines and manually by hand.
We discovered that GROMACS, in comparison with LAMMPS, GOMC, Cassandra, MCCCS, was providing a value ~2x the value provided by these other engines and by hand.

Upon further investigation, a member (@daico007) discovered that the ~2x difference in GROMACS was only present in 2021+ versions (there appears to have been an overhaul to the dispersion correction data structures around this time). Previous versions of GROMACS did provide the expected value and not double the other engines. It seems that a possible regression has occurred in this calculation and a mwe and environment has been provided in the tarball below. Using the script below and by performing a git bisect to find the commit that causes the change in behavior. We find that [this is the offending commit](https://github.com/gromacs/gromacs/commit/eebc36c13bf6d15f6beb7cef951c8c6e8a91dc9d), versions previous to this commit return the expected value: `~-128` and after this commit, the incorrect value of `-256` is returned.

Note, for ease of calculation, this uses the [`panedr`](https://github.com/jbarnoud/panedr) library to coerce the `.edr` files to pandas dataframes. There is a provided `environment.yml` file to create a conda environment which contains the necessary libraries to run this. Note: This has been tested using manually compiled versions of the GROMACS source code (thanks to @tcmoore3), as well as the shipped GROMACS versions on the `bioconda` channel. I included GROMACS 2020.6 in the bioconda channel.

The `mwe.py` should be ran each time a new version of `gmx` has been compiled/installed.

The difference is the potential energy difference between a LJ potential with a hard cutoff and no dispersion correction, and the same system with a hard cutoff but `ener_press` toggled for the dispersion correction. The system is essentially an LJ fluid with no charge.

```bash
tar -xvf mwe.tar.bz2
cd mwe
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate gmx-mwe-lrc
python mwe.py
```

[mwe.tar.bz2](/uploads/5ac58fd016f5ce9ca495cd82a3cf3d82/mwe.tar.bz2)

closed_issues.title: convert-tpr charge zeroing broken
closed_issues.description:
The charge-zeroing `-zeroq` function of convert-tpr is broken since ec5d23831a6217 ([relevant change here](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/ec5d23831a6217a92ac4e3dc36d75e93be5236a9/src/kernel/tpbconv.c#L284) vs previous version [here](https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/blob/72689267857d81da2e25d79c95d443628013e969/src/kernel/tpbconv.c#L233)), which dates from 2008.

The index used in the `zeroq()` function originates from get_index, and so it is a global atom index, not moltype-aware. This worked before because the old t_topology has a all-concatenated array for atoms.

Thus this causes array out-of-bound write, or incorrect atom charge-zeroing. (Confirmed with ASAN and gdb)

Attached is a [tpr](/uploads/42ef9ea107dd19cafee7b61b8d1cf392/em.tpr) and [index file](/uploads/c8d49c5c47cc1ebb38dbad4a5e8e24a5/index.ndx). For reproduction, `gmx convert-tpr -s em.tpr -o em_out.tpr -zeroq -n index.ndx` with group 12 (Water) selected will segfault.

Should this particular function of the tool be removed?

closed_issues.title: CMake may end Sphinx detection with the wrong executable.
closed_issues.description:
The GROMACS `FindSphinx.cmake` does not use the configured Python interpreter (if available) to guide detection of `sphinx-build`.

This means that autodoc may run with a different version of Python than the version for which GROMACS scripts are written or for which bundled packages (like `gmxapi`) are built.

It also means that `FindSphinx` may not find the `sphinx-build` entry point that users have installed in a virtual environment, even though CMake tells them that their virtual environment was correctly detected.

In the case of a package manager or environment manager that handles multiple (selectable) Python installations, a "shim" script may be detected instead of the actual `sphinx-build` executable. A potential error message can be
```
CMake Warning:
  Value of SPHINX_EXECUTABLE_VERSION contained a newline; truncating
```

closed_issues.title: DPC++ MKL FFT known bugs and limitations
closed_issues.description:
_This is an issue to keep all relevant information on why we can't use full-GPU mode with SYCL DPC++ right now. It's not particularly actionable on GROMACS side._

As of oneAPI 2021.4, the Intel MKL has the following issues affecting us (See "DPC++ Known Issues and Limitations" in [Intel Release Notes](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/release-notes/onemkl-release-notes.html)):

- Real backward out-of-place DFT can produce incorrect results on Intel GPU. As a workaround, use the in-place transform.
  - This can indeed be worked around, but the rest of our GPU backends use out-of-place transforms, so we get extra code divergence, which is not nice, but manageable.
- For DFT on GPU, user-defined strides with padding are not supported.
  - We do use user-defined strides, so not an easy fix unless we are brave enough to change indexing in our PME kernels.
- Modern kernel (5.18) and compute-runtime (22.10) cause even the in-place to fail unit tests when using LevelZero on Xe Max (OpenCL works fine). Older software (5.4 kernel, 21.37 compute-runtime) worked okay.

As of oneAPI 2022.0.1, these issues are no longer listed in release notes, and indeed:

- Out-of-place DFT works fine.
- User-defined strides work, but extra padding is required for real matrices.
  - Otherwise, an exception is thrown when creating the plan (in-place) or wrong results are returned (out-of-place).
  - A flag to enable this extra padding is added to `src/gromacs/ewald/pme_gpu_internal.cpp` (`needWorkaroundForOneMkl`).

As on oneAPI 2022.2.0, the code appears to work fine even without extra padding (at least on Xe MAX with compute-runtime 22.15).

Depending on oneAPI version requirements for future releases, the `needWorkaroundForOneMkl` flag can be removed if we settle on oneAPI >= 2022.2 (which is likely).

closed_issues.title: Very slow tests with SYCL and Intel GPUs
closed_issues.description:
The runtime kernel compiler cache is not working well, and in tests, each kernel gets recompiled multiple times for the same device. This increases, e.g., MdrunIoTest runtime from ~30 to ~300 seconds.

This happens with oneAPI 2021.2-2021.4, possibly earlier versions as well. Does not affect the "real" MD runs. Probably related to device re-initialization or something.

@rolandschulz is aware of that, and the core issue is being worked on.

In the mean time, setting `SYCL_CACHE_PERSISTENT=1` (which will enable on-disk cache) remediates the problem (even if we start with empty on-disk cache).

Note: the same env. variable can be used to cache compiled kernels across CI jobs, but the benefit seems negligible.

closed_issues.title: Consider lighter weight CI infrastructure.
closed_issues.description:
Our Docker images are big and slow to build. Our CI job artifacts are big and numerous. Our CI workflows spend a lot of time starting and stopping containers or transferring data.

# Proposals

### Merge the configure and build stages

We probably spend more time on overhead than actually running the configure stages. On the rare occasions that configure stages are used by multiple build jobs, it is probably cheaper to duplicate the configure. Also, it is not safe to use the configure stage output without rerunning CMake anyway, since we don't use commit-specific artifact names or cache keys.

### Reduce artifact and cache storage

Consider discontinuing artifacts and caches that are easily invalidated (requiring extra wall time and leading to wasted transfer time). Corollary: Don't store and transfer data that is easy to reproduce.

### Evaluate/optimize ccache usage.

The build jobs spend a long time downloading and uploading ccache databases. We should check whether this is costing or saving time. Consider adding `ccache -s` to the beginning and end of the build scripts. Consider checking the distribution of job wall times for a couple of job names across a bunch of commits.

To make ccache most useful, store ccache even for failed builds.

Most failed builds still manage to compile a lot of files that will not be modified in the MR. By default, the CI `cache` parameter is set to `when: on_success`. For ccache, we should probably use `cache: when: always`.  

Related: something in our build system causes a lot of ccache records to be invalidated much more often than should seem necessary. If we could figure out what is causing this, we could probably save ~90% of the build time for initial MR pushes by inheriting the ccache cache from the master branch.

### Use more specific builds for test stages

We can either merge the build and test stages or tag the installation artifacts more vigorously, but it is currently possible for test jobs to pick up artifacts from other pipelines run for the same ref.

Also, merging the build and test pipelines would allow us to conditionally store more build artifacts for failed tests and discard all but the test results for passing tests. Note that we would want to add `when: 'always'` to the `cache` CI parameter so that ccache database is updated for failed jobs.

Only a small number of jobs, if any, fail late in execution from transient resource interruptions, and we only need cache (not artifacts) to mitigate the cost of re-building. There is not much gained by "check-pointing" the CI workflow between build and test.

### Reevaluate CI Docker images for size

The images take a lot of time to download, build, and upload, and take up a lot of space in our GitLab project storage. Large image size also means that fewer Docker images will remain in local caches for less time. (Note that Docker registries may self-optimize, and avoid storing duplicated layers across images, so the actual storage used is not necessarily the same as the sum of image sizes.)

We need some extra files in order to use the containers as build environments, but we probably have bloated containers that could be shrunken somewhat with more judicious use of features like [hpccm.Stage.runtime](https://github.com/NVIDIA/hpc-container-maker/blob/master/docs/misc_api.md#runtime)

We can revisit the hpccm building blocks available, but also should consider relying more on packages from the OS distributions. In particular,

#### MPI
MPI can take a long time to build, but recent Ubuntu releases are fairly flexible with configuring MPI installations for different toolchains. The flexibility is affected, though, by MPI flavor and OS distribution.

#### Python

Recent OS distributions have gotten much better at managing multiple Python installations, and native packages may have substantially smaller footprints than from-scratch installations.

We have at least one extra Python installation already, since we are explicitly installing the OS distribution's Python3 in addition to the pyenv installations.

### Use additional projects to test new CI images

We use the `latest` tag for CI images that are still evolving, but this means that we can't easily stage in new CI images without extra temporary edits to the job configurations.

If we used `${CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE}` instead of `${CI_REGISTRY}/gromacs/gromacs` in our image names, we could push trial images to a different registry (e.g. https://gitlab.com/gromacs/testing/gromacs/container_registry) to confirm that a fork of `master` (or the branch in need of the image update) at `https://gitlab.com/gromacs/testing/gromacs.git` will work as expected without editing the gitlab-ci yaml.

### Only run one CI pipeline per MR update

https://gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs/-/issues/3617

# Resolution

This issue is intended to focus discussion and launch new issues when it is determined that action should be taken. To clarify scope, I suggest closing this issue once each proposal can be accepted or rejected, or after a couple of planning meetings have passed without evidence that these topics have significant priority.

closed_issues.title: Performance regression of LINCS wit all-bonds and many threads
closed_issues.description: Do to always using the DD atom ordering, LINCS constraints are no longer assigned in the topology order when using a single domain. The topology order is usually optimal. This makes LINCS a factor 3 slower on 64 OpenMP threads. To regain some of this performance, the order of assignment needs to be changed. This will also benefit performance of the DD multidomain case.

closed_issues.title: CMake Toolchain file insufficient for regular build.
closed_issues.description:
GMX_REQUIRE_VALID_TOOLCHAIN=ON shows that the generated `gromacs-toolchain.cmake` does not correctly set some variables (such as `MPI_RUN_RESULT_C_libver_mpi_normal`) that may be required in normal builds. It still may be usable by client software, but if the toolchain file is insufficient to build the project from which it was generated, I think its utility is marginal (and its integration testing is certainly inadequate).

Rather than refining cross-compilation testing, I propose that we avoid this non-normative CMake usage, remove the generation and installation of this file, and adopt a different approach for hinting build system details to client software. Relates to #3279: provide instead a CMake cache file (to be used with `-C gromacs-hints.cmake` instead of `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` or `--toolchain`).

This also requires updating the advice for client software and Python package builds. See #3273.

closed_issues.title: CUDA kernel for nonbonded FEP
closed_issues.description:
We have implemented GPU acceleration for nonbonded FEP by writing an extra GPU nonbonded kernel. And we hope to merge our codes to GROMACS official repository.

Our codes can be viewed here: https://gitlab.com/deepmodeling/gromacs/-/tree/2021.3-nb-gpu

From the time we proposed previous issues (#3994 #4010), we have fixed dhdl calculation. Now our codes can give correct results for energy, forces and dhdl, which is tested by some of our examples.

## Performance results

We tested the performance of our codes with a 44k atoms system, previously offered by Prof. Gapsys. We compared performance with v2021.3, on which our codes are based.

![image](/uploads/ee444576c7fda22c2e8c2797aaaf2ac3/image.png)

Our tests were done by using a 2080ti GPU and 1 or 16 CPU(s). And we achieved a speedup ratio in the range of 2.5 to 3.8 in FEP, depend on the number of CPUs.

The data and scripts are attached for reproducing the results.

```shell
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=16;

gmx_mpi grompp -f production_sep.mdp -c conf.gro -p processed.top -o topol_1.tpr 
gmx_mpi mdrun -notunepme -deffnm topol_1 -nsteps 100000 -bonded gpu
```

Data files: [data.zip](/uploads/ae8dc61d4e94c53e96d1104b4f8c8536/data.zip)

## Next steps to PR

We still have some questions about the things we should do before PR.

1. **Updates since v2021.3.** For readiness, our codes are based on v2021.3. But we noticed that many updates were made since the release, which may cause inconsistency with our codes.
2. **Unit tests.** At the current stage, We have not made efforts to ensure our codes to be consistent with unit tests.

We need suggestions from developers on how we should do before PR. And it'll be of great help if developers who are familiar with the above two aspects can give us instructions.

---

Junhan Chang, Yuxuan Yan, Yuzhi Zhang

Deepmodeling Community

closed_issues.title: Negative normalization factor in gmx spatial (giving wrong results)
closed_issues.description:
I've had a few cases where after calculating spatial distribution function, negative normalization factors were printed out to stdout. For example

> Reading frame   11000 time 374950.000                                                                                
> Counts per frame in all 1092727 cubes divided by -1.668011e-02                                                       
> Normalized data: average 1.000000e+00, min -0.000000e+00, max -2.510009e+00
>                                                                                    
> GROMACS reminds you: "Kissing You is Like Kissing Gravel" (Throwing Muses) 

I traced the origin to near line 448 in gmx_spatial.cpp:

>     if (bCALCDIV)
>     {
>         norm = static_cast<double>(numcu * numfr) / tot;                                                      
>     }

where all numbers should be positive, hence norm > 0.

The type cast should be done before the multiplication.

My machine:
- OS:  CentOS Stream 8, 4.18.0-326.el8.x86_64
- gcc: 8.5.0
- CUDA:V11.4.120
- GROMACS: 2021.1

closed_issues.title: Formatting of CMake files
closed_issues.description:
Currently, CMake files in GROMACS have no consistent style: mixed tabs and spaces, different placement of parentheses, etc.

Unfortunately, clang-format does not support CMake, but there are dedicated tools like [cmakelang](https://github.com/cheshirekow/cmake_format) that do formatting and linting of CMake files.

Pros: 

- Our CMake infrastructure is quite extensive and convoluted, so additional static analysis can be helpful.
- Enforcing a unified format will make the code more beautiful.

Cons:

- One more formatter/linter too to wrestle with whenever we do something it does not like.
- `cmakelang` is a relatively obscure python package, so not sure how well it is supported.
- More tools for developers to install.

    >

That is UB and could also fail with some weird error with some STL in some mode. memset is really only allowed for trivial copyable types.

We should stop using memset to set t_inputrec to 0 (and its directly contained structs, and the pointers to indirectly owned structs). To achieve this

- [ ] Rotational pulling data structures need updates
- [ ] t_inputrec et al need updates

Described more (apparently correctly) here: http://cgmartini.nl/images/tools/anglepots/ReadMe.pdf

closed_issues.title: OpenMP usage incompatible with Visual Studio
closed_issues.description:
We aren't testing with Visual Studio anymore and multiple OpenMP constructs which aren't supported by Visual Studio have been added.

- `src/gromacs/mdrun/minimize.cpp`:
`
#pragma omp parallel for reduction(max : maxDiffSquared) num_threads(nthreads) schedule(static)
`
- `src/gromacs/modularsimulator/statepropagatordata.cpp`:
`
#pragma omp parallel for num_threads(nth) schedule(static) default(none) shared(nth, velocityScalingFactors_, velocities)
`

I think there are more. I didn't look further. The first isn't OK because reduction isn't supported. And the 2nd isn't OK because member variables aren't allowed inside shared (this one seems to be a not allowed even according to the spec but other compilers seem to be fine with it).

Options:
- don't support Visual Studio anymore. And recommend clang or Intel compiler for native Windows binaries or WSL as easiest solution.
- support Visual Studio but only without OpenMP. Would still require recommending other Compilers in install-guide.
- Fix OpenMP constructs where it is easy and put others inside an `#ifndef _MSC_VER` (e.g. reduction)
- Make all OpenMP construction only use the Visual Studio supported constructs by rewriting code as required (e.g. manual reduction).

closed_issues.title: Windows MAX_PATH issue
closed_issues.description:
The renaming of preprocess tests (285b6971a5f1e1fe4cd0fd0) has caused pathnames to become long and cause issue with Windows MAX_PATH of 260.

Windows does have support for longer paths, but not with the non-unicode IO functions we or google-test are using ( 
https://github.com/google/googletest/issues/3406).

We could change the IO functions but I suspect we don't have the resources to do that.

That leaves us with agreeing on a maxing path length for GROMACS files and then documenting in the install guide the maximum allowed path-length where the GROMACS source is placed.

Currently the longest path is `src/gromacs/gmxpreprocess/tests/refdata/ForCharmm27CyclicSystem_Pdb2gmxTest_ProducesMatchingTopology_ff_charmm27_water_tip3p_vsite_none_chainsep_id_or_ter_merge_all_input_cyclicproteinsmallpdb_format_gro_matchfullconfiguration_false_.xml` with 237 characters. If we don't rename it the maximum path of the gromacs folder is 23. Given that `c:\gromacs\` is 11 this leaves 12 characters for any level between. If the user wants to put it into their home directory than this doesn't work as long as the username is more than 4 characters (given the `Users\` prefix under Windows). And it doesn't work at all if the users wants to put it into the default location of Visual studio (`{user-folder}\source\repos\`).

The longest path not including `gmxpreprocess/tests/refdata/` is `src/programs/mdrun/tests/refdata/ReplicaExchangeIsEquivalentToReferenceLeapFrog_ReplicaExchangeRegressionTest_WithinTolerances_ReplExRegression_md_NoseHoover_ParrinelloRahman_4Ranks_2RanksPerSimulation_s.xml` with 207.

If we are willing to limit our path length to 207 and rename the files in refdata in gmxpreprocess, then the max gromacs folder path would be 53 and this would be sufficient for normal source locations (e.g. the default `{user-folder}\source\repos\` for reasonable long user names).
